News.title: Ten years after Brazil’s Zika epidemic, its children are still paying the price
News.content:
In the heated pool, ten-year-old Stephany Vitória Silva Costa is weightless. The water soothes her convulsing muscles, providing brief respite from constant pain, and she coos with delight, igniting smiles among everyone in the room.

Stephany is a “Zika baby”; one of more than 3,080 children born with Congenital Zika Syndrome (CZS) following a devastating outbreak of the mosquito borne virus that swept Brazil in 2015-16. At least 444 of those children have died, mainly from respiratory and infectious diseases.

Like most of the surviving children from the cohort, she has suffered from an array of symptoms including microcephaly, severe cognitive and motor impairment, vision and hearing loss and seizures – which can occur up to ten times a day.

But a decade after the outbreak, a second wave of complications are emerging in children like Stephany.

Stephany’s exposed back, showing the pronounced 120-degree curvature caused by rapid, severe scoliosis Credit : Lucas Landau/The Telegraph

As her therapist gently turns her in the pool, a pronounced bulge shows through the back of her pink and blue swim top. Over the last two years, her growing spine has been pulled 120-degrees into an S-shaped curve that is now crushing her lungs.

While many of the children born with microcephaly after the outbreak died in early infancy, a much-loved group including Stephany lived on. Now, however, mortality rates are again climbing as the children near adolescence.

An x-ray image showing a severe s-shaped spinal deformity threatening to compress a young patient’s lungs Credit : Lucas Landau/The Telegraph

“It weighs heavily on my heart. After so many years of following these children, it is inevitable to form bonds – not only with them, but with their families,” says Dr Milena Cavalcanti, one of just 11 paediatric neurologists in the state.

“Every loss affects me deeply. It is very hard to say goodbye to them”.

At the Altino Ventura Foundation’s (FAV) hydrotherapy centre, steam clings to murals depicting ocean scenes – a smiling pink octopus swims around a silver painted shipwreck.

As Stephany coos, another girl in a brown swimsuit and rainbow coloured shorts smiles as her mother fills a cup with water and pours it over her black curls.

Originally an ophthalmology institute, FAV expanded into neuro-rehabilitation as the Zika crisis unfolded. It provides free therapy to children with CZS twice a week, with treatment plans reassessed every six months.

Some 230 children affected by the syndrome have had therapy at the foundation and 84 are currently being treated. Its clinicians are tracking the cohort's long-term development.

Physiotherapist Gustav Wagner assists a young patient in the hydrotherapy pool Credit : Lucas Landau/The Telegraph

None of the Zika children present can walk or hold themselves up, and the majority have already had at least one major surgery.

Nevertheless, Gustav Wagner, a physiotherapist, says installing the hydrotherapy pool – which increases blood flow and loosens muscles – was a major breakthrough.

The children can’t express pain verbally. Mr Wagner and his team instead use a visual scale from one to ten, based on reading their posture and expressions. The mothers, above all, learn to spot the smallest changes and the pool, they say, makes a huge difference.

“It’s a very peculiar disease,” says Amanda Rodrigues, a physiotherapist. “We have to learn with them how to get better – we have never treated something like this before”.

A silent invasion

First discovered in 1947 in Uganda’s Zika forest, the Zika virus is thought to have quietly reached Brazil in 2014.

Experts attribute its arrival to increased air travel; either carried by visitors landing for the 2014 FIFA World Cup or brought from active outbreaks in the South Pacific islands.

Either way, the virus spread unnoticed and unchecked in Brazil for over a year.

Most Zika infections are asymptomatic or easily mistaken for dengue, both cause a similar red rash and flu-like symptoms.

The alarm was finally raised in August 2015 when neuropaediatrician Dr Vanessa van der Linden identified an unprecedented surge in infants born with microcephaly across Pernambuco state.

“It was very chaotic at the beginning,” says Dr Milena Cavalcanti. She added that doctors frantically coordinated emergency responses over WhatsApp as the crisis unfolded.

“The physical toll on the children was devastating,” she said.

Paediatric neurologist Dr Milena Cavalcanti Credit : Lucas Landau/The Telegraph

Infections early in pregnancy inflicted the worst damage. And in one of the side rooms of the hydrotherapy centre, it's evident that the disabilities are profound.

Five children sit motionless in their wheelchairs with blankets pulled up to their necks. One of them, Emily Sophia dos Santos Luna, weighed just six kilograms at age two before being given a feeding tube to enable her to survive.

The children are unable to swallow, causing mucus to pool in the back of their throats. To prevent choking, their wheelchairs are permanently tilted at a 45 degree angle.

Maria José da Silva wheels her granddaughter to specialist transport Credit : Lucas Landau/The Telegraph

“In the beginning, we thought they would discover a treatment,” says Emily’s grandmother, Maria José da Silva, 43. “But now we understand she will always be this way”.

She added: “It’s a very difficult life, but God gave us the power to keep going. I will take care of her until the day God wants”.

In the therapeutic gym, a large room filled with foam mats, standing frames and slings hung from the ceiling, Allana Kauane perches on a large silver balance ball.

She wears a green skirt, shin-high pink socks, and a white T-shirt that has “be happy” printed in shimmery lettering.

Ms Rodrigues, her physiotherapist, supports her torso and bounces her gently to build core strength. With every movement, she patiently lifts Allana’s head back up as it falls onto her chest.

Thailene Maria uses a bright gold pompom to draw her daughter’s focus Credit : Lucas Landau/The Telegraph

Thailene Maria, the child’s 28-year-old mother, waves a bright gold pompom in front of her eyes in an effort to draw her focus.

Down the corridor in a consultation room, Dr Cavalcanti examines another patient.

It’s a girl who has not had a seizure in six years, but her last one lasted thirty minutes – six times the length that defines a medical emergency in Brazil.

Manuelle does not like to be touched, her grandmother says. She used to bite herself, now she pulls at her own hair instead.

As Dr Cavalcanti taps gently at her knee with a reflex hammer, the girl tenses and struggles to lie flat. Fine dark hair has started to grow along the girl’s shins – a side effect, says Dr Cavalcanti, of the anticonvulsant medication she relies on to control her seizures.

It is one of several changes the clinic still cannot fully explain. Many patients entered puberty years earlier than expected, one as young as three. Most are treated with hormone-blocking injections.

Dr Cavalcanti gently tests the reflexes of a young patient’s knee Credit : Lucas Landau/The Telegraph

“We don’t know,” says Dr Cavalcanti, when asked about the cause. “We are just following the cases”.

On the ground floor, past the therapy rooms, sits the Capela Santissima Trinidade, a small wood-pannelled chapel. Inside, there are rows of pews, and in the centre is a large stained glass window.

It’s a small reminder that the building was designed to cater for the spiritual needs of its patients alongside their medical care.

While infants with CZS initially received only basic motor stimulation, severe musculoskeletal issues are emerging as they reach adolescence.

Dr Epitácio Rolim, the top orthopaedic surgeon in the state, has tracked a cohort of 152 children since the outbreak.

By age 10, 98 per cent developed orthopaedic deformities – 70 per cent suffer hip deformities, and 64 per cent from spinal curvature.

Previously, the public health system did not offer corrective surgeries or have a structured waiting list.

Some 230 children affected by the syndrome have had therapy at the foundation Credit : Lucas Landau

Dr Zilda Cavalcanti, Health Secretary of Pernambuco state, told The Telegraph: “We know we have a lot to do yet. The needs are giant and the funds are not”.

The root problem is neurological, says Dr Rolim. Damaged brain pathways create severe muscle imbalances around major joints. Unable to reposition themselves, the children’s relentless muscle tightness pulls their hips out of their socket and twists their spines.

Delaying intervention drastically restricts surgical options, Dr Rolim warns.

In the worst cases, repairing the hip is no longer possible. Surgeons must instead remove the top of the thigh bone simply to stop it from grinding against the socket.

“I am not talking about surgery to make most of these children walk,” says Dr Rolim. “The realistic goal is quality of life… hope does not mean promising a cure that we do not have… it means living with as little pain as possible”.

Dr Zilda Cavalcanti, Health Secretary of Pernambuco State Credit : Lucas Landau/The Telegraph

Only five to seven per cent of pregnant women exposed to Zika had babies with visible symptoms like microcephaly. For the rest, timing of the infection in pregnancy determined how destructive the virus was.

“The children you saw with microcephaly were at the extreme end of the spectrum,” says Dr Ernesto Marques, a senior researcher at Fiocruz in Recife. “As the others become teens, developmental delays are showing up more clearly”.

Dr Patricia Garcez, a neuroscientist at King’s College London who helped establish the link between Zika and brain defects in 2016, said that many of the “milder” CZS cases are now displaying severe autism and neurodevelopmental delay, or motor deficits caused by prenatal Zika exposure without severe microcephaly.

The perfect breeding ground

The night we arrive in Recife, known as the “Brazilian Venice”, heavy rains transform the city’s roads into rivers. Gesturing to the rising water outside, our taxi driver chuckles: “Here we say: When someone sneezes, the whole city floods”.

Centuries ago, the city was a low-lying landscape of tidal sandbanks, estuaries and mangroves. When Dutch colonisers arrived in the 1600s, they engineered canals, bridges and dikes to prevent flooding and make the swamplands habitable.

It is this geography that made Recife, the capital of Pernambuco, the epicentre of the 2015-16 Zika outbreak, its pools of still water proving the perfect breeding ground for mosquitoes.

News.title: Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest
News.content:
Leeds manager Daniel Farke said: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

“I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

“He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”

Forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

Forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a new right wing-back before the deadline.

Newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

Glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He said: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

Sports.title: Southampton exploring emotional return for James Ward-Prowse just three years after selling ex-England ace for £30m
Sports.content:
SOUTHAMPTON are exploring a move to bring James Ward-Prowse back to the club.

The ex-Saints skipper, 31, left St Mary’s following relegation in 2023 to join West Ham in a £30million deal.



Ward-Prowse made 410 appearances for the club having come through the academy at the age of eight, spending 20 years at the club before his exit.

The midfielder has just one year left on his deal at the London Stadium and would be allowed to leave for a nominal fee.



Ward-Prowse is still thought to earn around £50,000-a-week in the Championship, which could prove a stumbling block for his former club.

However, the former England man is thought to be open to returning to the south coast club.

Ward-Prowse was not part of the West Ham squad for their 4-1 Carabao Cup win at Southampton on Tuesday night.

Meanwhile, Southampton have have agreed a deal to sign German defender Keven Schlotterbeck.

Saints will pay around £4million to Bundesliga side Augsburg amid interest in Taylor Harwood-Bellis.

Harwood-Bellis has been left out of Southampton’s last two matchday squads after the club rejected bids from Benfica and, more recently, Aston Villa.

Sports.title: Fans convinced Carabao Cup pre-draw is ‘most rigged ever’ with Man Utd among big teams landing home ties
Sports.content:
FOOTBALL fans are fuming as they claim the pre-draw for the Carabao cup is rigged.

The controversial pre-draw features the eight teams that have qualified for the Champions League or Europa League this season.



Carabao Cup chiefs previously announced that due to Uefa fixtures being fixed and unable to be rescheduled, any teams in those European competitions would not be able to face each other in the Cup.

The worry stems from a potential situation in which a Champions League team was drawn against a Europa League team in the Cup, leaving no eligible day for the fixture to be played due to limits on fixture congestion.



The eight teams in question were drawn either home or away before Wednesday evening’s fixtures, and the following main draw.

But fans were not pleased with the result, with some rattled supporters even complaining that they felt the draw was ‘rigged.’

The controversy stemmed from the majority of the teams being drawn at home, with only Arsenal and Aston Villa facing the prospect of a fixture away from home.

One fan wrote: “Two out of 8 home fixtures for the big boys. Surely would’ve been fairer if there were more home and away balls to pick from rather than three of each. Total farce. Rigged.”

Another supporter fumed: “Omg this is the most RIGGED draw ever? What are these people doing? Only to have the big teams at home… mental stuff hahaha.”

A third fan wrote: “Is this Carabao third round preliminary draw fixed? Why are the home or away balls being put straight back in the bucket?”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

And a fourth added: “That is the most fixed draw ever. Why are the home and away balls a different colour?”

Manchester United, Manchester City and Liverpool were among the clubs to snag themselves a home tie in the next round.

Sports.title: Charlton star carried off on stretcher less than 15 minutes into Tottenham clash as Addicks suffer double injury blow
Sports.content:
INJURY HEARTACHE Charlton star carried off on stretcher less than 15 minutes into Tottenham clash as Addicks suffer double injury blow

CHARLTON defender Collins Sichenje was carried off on a stretcher with his head in his hands just minutes into Wednesday’s Carabao Cup clash at Tottenham.

The Kenyan centre-back went down just three minutes into the second round tie, before getting to his feet and carrying on.



Sichenje initially went down after a challenge from Spurs ace Mathys Tel, whose boot appeared to come down on the Charlton man’s foot.

The defender looked uneasy following that moment and his night was brought to an unfortunate end soon after.



Sichenje went down again minutes later and was forced off on a stretcher, with the defender inconsolable as medics carried him off.

In a further blow for the Addicks, centre-back partner Billy Koumetio was also forced off before the 15 minute mark.

The 23-year-old was holding his hamstring and ultimately hobbled off the pitch and down the tunnel.

Charlton boss Nathan Jones replaced the pair with Lloyd Jones and Dan McNamara.

Jones had been hoping to rest them both, having made 10 changes coming into the game, but was forced to introduce them early.

Among those coming into the starting XI was goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks – making his professional debut having never played above the National League before.

Sports.title: ‘Fergie, Pep & Klopp combined wouldn’t keep them up!’ – Statman Dave picks his all-time Prem XI on Greatest of all Teams
Sports.content:
“SIR ALEX FERGUSON, Pep Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp rolled into one wouldn’t keep this team up!”

That was former Premier League winning captain Tim Sherwood’s brutal assessment of guest Statman Dave’s ultimate all-time XI.



The former Blackburn, Tottenham and England is co-hosting The Sun’s brilliant new show Greatest of all Teams, brought to you by Sun Vegas.

And joining Sherwood and StevoTheMadman on the first episode is YouTube star Statman Dave.



And ex-Spurs and Aston Villa boss Sherwood watched in disbelief as the randomiser game spiralled into chaos.

The premise is simple: pick one player from 11 randomly drawn Premier League clubs, each in a particular season, to build a functional line-up.



But our expert panel prove it’s nowhere near as easy as it sounds.

Cue a team featuring Prem icons like Steven Gerrard and John Terry… alongside a 92/93 Sheffield United right-back you “need a helmet to play against”.

But was it a relegation scrap or a battle for Europe for Statman Dave’s boys?

Head over to YouTube now for all the picks, anecdotes and Premier League nostalgia in the full episode of Greatest of All Teams.

Sports.title: Al Hilal agree £51million Ollie Watkins transfer with Aston Villa set to sign Nicolas Jackson as immediate replacement
Sports.content:
AL HILAL have agreed a transfer deal for Aston Villa star Ollie Watkins.

The England international’s six-year stint with the Villans is set to come to an end.



That is according to Fabrizio Romano, who claims the teams have hammered out a deal worth up to £50million.

The deal marks an end to a drawn-out transfer saga this summer, with Unai Emery giving a cryptic answer when asked about his situation ahead of their Premier League opener.



Watkins was absent from the matchday squad, with Villa falling to a 4-0 defeat in the fixture at Brighton’s Amex Stadium.

But the coach will hope that he won’t be so shorthanded in the near future, as Villa have already agreed a deal to bring in Nicolas Jackson as Watkins’ successor.

The Blues are working on finalising the last details for a switch worth £47.5m, rising to as much as £65m if certain add-ons are reached.

The Senegalese striker spent last season on loan with Bayern Munich, who elected not to pursue a permanent deal at the end of the season.

But with Joao Pedro and new signings Emanuel Emegha and Danny Welbeck already in the Stamford Bridge dressing room, it was clear Jackson would have to find a new home if he wanted regular minutes.

He was subject to interest from a number of suitors, with Newcastle eyeing up a potential deal earlier this summer.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

But Villa have won the race for his signature, and SunSport understands Jackson is set to undergo his medical on Thursday.

That timeline means he could be available for their Arsenal clash on Monday if all goes smoothly.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes hails Man Utd’s next big thing with ‘different mentality’ who he coached when he was just 14
Sports.content:
BRUNO FERNANDES views Shea Lacey as Manchester United’s next breakout star.

The Old Trafford skipper praised 19-year-old Lacey, having previously coached him at Under-14 level while working toward his coaching badges.



Lacey has been in and around the first team since the start of last season and was brought on ahead of Joshua Zirkzee during United’s 2-0 defeat at Hull City on Saturday.

Quizzed on the next prodigy to break through from United’s famous academy, Fernandes told Men In Blazers: “Shea came with a different mentality this season in terms of playing off the ball—it’s been great. It was one of the first things I said to him when I got back.



“Because I had to watch the first three pre-season friendlies and he was playing in the position I play, where it demands a lot of running and emotional intelligence to be covering spaces and helping the ones in front.

“And he did that very well. His technical ability was never in doubt, he is an exceptional player. He has some very good abilities. I am always joking with him because I coached him during my badges when he was 14.

“I was basically his manager for one day, me and Juan Mata. I tell him he is much better now than when he was 14. He’s much more mature, he’s doing very well. He is always on it in training and that is something they all need to do.”

Incidentally, former United midfielder Mata presented close friend Fernandes with the PFA Player of the Season award at Manchester Opera House on Tuesday night.

But Fernandes also aired caution around fast-tracking academy players too early.

He added: “You’ve spoken about Lacey and Harry Amass. We also have Tyler and Jack Fletcher. We have a lot of young players with potential but we cannot burn them out straight away.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“We need to give them time. They need to play, they will only become good enough if they get minutes, but at the same time our squad is very strong and they need to earn their place in the squad.”

The Fletcher twins stepped back down and starred in the Under-21s 5-0 victory over Ipswich Town on Monday night.

Dad Darren, who is United’s Under-18 lead coach, was in the crowd with first team boss Michael Carrick at Leigh Sports Village.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta must play bizarre ‘psychological trick’ on his own Arsenal stars to ensure they sink Emery’s Aston Villa
Sports.content:
ARSENAL started the Premier League title defence with a comfortable 3-0 win over newcomers Coventry City.

But facing Aston Villa away at Villa Park this weekend presents a completely different tactical puzzle.



Among Mikel Arteta’s main challenges won’t just be outsmarting his rival managers, but pulling off a psychological trick on his own squad to keep every player bought into his gameplan.

SunSport tactical expert Dean Scoggins breaks down the upcoming clash and explained why Arteta’s starting line-ups are no longer set in stone.



This is going to be the season of flexibility for Arteta.

They’ve got such an amazing squad that now it can be horses for courses.

And when they play against different tactical line-ups, they can do different things.

In a new squad system, with this flexibility, if Arteta decides Kai Havertz sits out, he is not going to think the manager has the hump with him.

The explanation is Viktor Gyokeres is better suited to running in behind against a team that plays a higher line like Villa.

If they’re playing against high lines, Gyokeres is a fabulous option. If it’s a bit more congested, Havertz is your man.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

The Gunners could also hand a full debut to £51million summer signing Ezri Konsa against his former club.

The England defender brings a unique skill set to Arsenal‘s backline that could completely unpick Villa’s defensive shape.

What Konsa brings is elite passing ability — he was number one in the Premier League last season for passes completed.

He’s also a ball carrier. If they manage to attract somebody on the press, he carries the ball in and tries to engage that player.



A centre-back who can carry and engage midfield players is a real danger because then all of a sudden you’re 1v1 everywhere else.

He will play brave passes, he’s elite in duels, and his recovery pace is top class.

But Arsenal’s tactical evolution isn’t just about individual line-up changes, but a far less rigid setup in the middle of the park.

With the options now available to Arteta, Declan Rice‘s position at the base of the midfield will give the Gunners complete freedom to attack.



The key to all this is Rice. The only place an opposition team can counter-attack is in the space out wide.

Rice’s recovery runs mean that even if Villa get three or four in attack, you’re matched up and you’re ok.

I see Declan Rice playing at the base of that midfield as the pivot because of those recovery runs much more often.

That just means Arsenal can lead more players forward and be more dangerous.

Sports.title: Incredible £475million XI of stars Man City let leave this summer including Rodri and two England stars
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER CITY have let an entire team of stars worth nearly HALF A BILLION pounds leave this summer.

It is a major transition period for the Etihad club right now.



After ten years in the dugout, the club bid an emotional farewell to Pep Guardiola.

His former assistant Enzo Maresca returned to the club he helped win the Treble just three years ago.



But the squad tasked with winning a first Premier League crown in three seasons looks very different from the one in Guardiola’s last campaign.

In fact, it is possible to make a full XI up once expected exits are confirmed before the transfer window closes on Tuesday night.



And adding the fees City paid for them up together, the grand total comes to £475.2m.

In goal, James Trafford only returned to City from Burnley a year ago for £27m – but has left again in a £40m deal to Leeds.

In front of him is another member of England’s World Cup squad.

John Stones arrived for £47.5m and was a tremendous servant for City over the years but was released when his contract expired – meaning he played for England despite being unemployed.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Fellow defenders Manuel Akanji and Nathan Ake were signed for £15.1m and £41m respectively.

Akanji made his loan move to Inter Milan permanent while Ake joined Fenerbahce for £8.5m.

The makeshift defence is completed by £45m Kalvin Phillips – and admittedly he has only left for Sheffield United on loan, rather than sold or released this summer.

But this is his fourth loan since 2024 and even though he has two years left on his Etihad contract, it is clear he is not part of the plans and will almost certainly not play for Man City again.



The midfield three is pretty heavyweight, though, with main man Rodri heading to Barcelona.

City sold him for £65.4m – £2.9m more than they paid Atletico Madrid for him in 2019.

The other two did not last long at all.

Nico Gonzalez is expected to complete his switch to Newcastle for £52m – a £2m profit on the midfielder City bought in February 2025.



And Tijjani Reijnders lasted just one season between his £46.5m arrival from AC Milan and £52m exit to Al-Qadsiah.

Two of the front three are swapping the north-west for North London.



Savinho was a £33.6m signing from sister-club Troyes in 2024, seen by many as the Riyad Mahrez replacement, but left for Tottenham in a whopping £85m deal.

Omar Marmoush is set to make the same journey, despite only arriving from Eintracht Frankfurt in a £64m deal in January of last year.

And the final member of the departing XI is Bernardo Silva.

The Portuguese playmaker spent nine years at City following his £43m transfer from Monaco in 2017 – and signed a two-year contract at Real Madrid as a free agent.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The staggering list of departures has been somewhat offset by the £234m of incomings – most of which went on £116m man Elliot Anderson and £81.4m teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi.



And that figure could increase by another £100m-plus should City land Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea, too.

Sports.title: Atletico Madrid 'explode' at Julian Alvarez as Arsenal and Barcelona eye transfer
Sports.content:
Atletico Madrid 'explode' at Julian Alvarez as Arsenal and Barcelona eye transfer

Atletico Madrid have exploded and issued a fiery response following Julian Alvarez's decision to miss training on Wednesday amid speculation around his future

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez has been linked with a move to Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Atletico Madrid have insisted there is a 0% chance of selling Arsenal target Julian Alvarez to Barcelona after club president Joan Laporta said they are still interested in signing the forward.

‌



Alvarez, 26, has been the subject of intense transfer speculation this summer, after making it clear he wants to leave Atletico. Back in June, the Argentina international expressed his desire to quit the La Liga club to "fulfil his dream" and admitted the "best thing for everyone is a transfer".

‌



Despite interest from Arsenal and Barcelona among others. Alvarez is still at Atletico and made his return to action as a second-half substitute during Sunday's 2-2 draw against Villarreal at Wanda Metropolitano.

‌



David Raya reveals new goal Arsenal stars and Mikel Arteta and have sights set on READ MORE :

Alan Shearer makes Julian Alvarez transfer prediction as Arsenal target nowhere to be seen READ MORE :

But the former Manchester City man was booed after coming on - and it's safe to suggest the Atletico supporters do not want to see him feature again following his wish to leave the club. Alvarez then missed training on Wednesday, though his absence was thought to be down to illness.

Now, Atletico have slapped back at Laporta's latest video, after the Barcelona president said that a £85.7million bid for Alvarez remained on the table. Marca report that Atletico have 'exploded' about the situation, with their feelings abundantly clear on Barcelona and the striker's behaviour.

The Spanish outlet reports that the club feels 'this is not about money, it's about dignity. The player is being victimised, but the only victim in the Julian case is us'.

‌



Atleti feel that they have been harmed 'economically and socially' by the move to try and force the Argentina out of the club - a 'campaign of lies'. There is a '0% chance' of them doing any business with Barcelona before the window closes, which could be good news for Arsenal.

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez of Atletico Madrid (Image: Alberto Gardin/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

In the video, Laporta said the club had great respect for Atletico but the bid they submitted earlier this summer was still on offer. It's reported that Barcelona are going to keep trying to sign Alvarez until the end of the window, despite Atleti making it clear the only way they will be able to sign him is by paying his vast buyout clause..

‌



Arsenal, meanwhile, are another that are keen on signing Alvarez. The Gunners are still active in the market for a superstar forward before the September 1 deadline, after Vinicius Jr's decision to remain at Real Madrid.

They have been long linked with a move for Alvarez and he would add an extra threat to Arsenal's front line as they look to retain the Premier League title and challenge in the Champions League this season.

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal £50m agreement, Man Utd land huge boost, Liverpool bid
Sports.content:
Ayyoub Bouaddi completes Man City transfer

Ayyoub Bouaddi has wasted no time in sticking the boot into his new rivals - after admitting Manchester City are the best club in the world.

The Moroccan sensation has completed an £85m switch to City from Lille.

The teenage midfielder has agreed a deal that will keep him at the Etihad until at least 2031.

And Bouaddi has told the likes of Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United there is no place he would rather be.

Bouaddi said: "Manchester City are, for me, the best club in the world. It's a dream to be here and be able to call myself a City player.

"I have spent most of my life working hard to become the best player I can be and reach the top of the game.

"I've watched City for many years, and I love their style of play. City always try and play quality football.

"And they have shown they are winners - this club feels like it's built to win.

"The squad is world-class and Enzo (Maresca) is a top manager. And I’m really looking forward to playing at the Etihad Stadium, in front of all the fans.

"I have plenty of improving to do. I am only 18. I am happy with the progress I have made so far, but I also know I can improve so much. This is undoubtedly the best place for me to do that.

"This club demands trophies and I will give everything to make sure we are challenging for every title."

Sports.title: Jack Grealish offered shock Premier League lifeline after Man City U-turn
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish offered shock Premier League lifeline after Man City U-turn

Jack Grealish has been the subject of a Sunderland loan bid with Manchester City willing to let the winger leave this summer

View 2 Images Man City are willing to let Jack Grealish leave (Image: Getty Images)

Sunderland have made a loan bid for Jack Grealish with his Manchester City future still unclear ahead of the transfer window closing.

‌



The winger spent last year at Everton and remains on the fringes at the Etihad despite a change in manager and the Black Cats are hopeful of landing a major coup in the form of the England international.

‌



Sunderland, who are having to prepare a squad capable of playing domestically and in Europe, have tabled an offer that would not only see City cover part of his salary but also include the chance to make the move permanent next summer when his contract expires, reports The Athletic.

‌



City have always been open to Grealish leaving - be it on loan or permanently - and that still remains the case despite Savinho's exit to Tottenham with Omar Marmoush set to follow him.

Despite being frozen out by Pep Guardiola, who made it clear he had no future at The Etihad, the 30-year-old has come on as a second-half substitute in each of City’s first two games this season - the Community Shield loss to Arsenal and Sunday’s 2-1 win over Bournemouth in their Premier League opener.

‌



Everton turned down the option of making Grealish's loan move a permanent one, which would've cost them £50million, and he's returned to Manchester as a result. The playmaker sustained a stress fracture in his foot in January which curtailed the remainder of his season on Merseyside. Before that Grealish had made 22 appearances, scoring two goals and providing six assists.

View 2 Images Sunderland want to take Grealish on loan (Image: Stu Forster/Getty Images)

Grealish, up until recently, remained City's record signing having joined from Aston Villa for £100m back in 2021. He was a regular initially but has struggled to live up to his price tag.

City's new manager, Enzo Maresca said on Grealish's future: "Jack (Grealish), again, until the day he isn't here, it's my duty to try and coach Jack and to try to get the best from him. It's one more week to go (until the transfer window closes) and we'll see what happens, not only with Jack, but with more players."

Sports.title: UEFA's boycott backdown must not stop them pushing for the ultimate Gianni Infantino sanction
Sports.content:
UEFA's boycott backdown must not stop them pushing for the ultimate Gianni Infantino sanction

The European governing body appears to have lifted its immediate threat of not taking part in FIFA competitions but is expected to discuss its next course of action at its meeting in Monaco

View 3 Images Aleksander Ceferin has been heavily critical of Gianni Infantino's FIFA tenure (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

At the height of the relatively brief World Cup sell-off scandal, UEFA somehow manoeuvred itself onto the high moral ground. Aleksander Ceferin’s scriptwriters were in sensational form. One of their opening gambits was that ‘the soul and governance of football are not assets to trade’.

‌



Nice line from the organisation that has turned the beautiful European Cup into a bloated, corporate mess with its own phoney anthem - a once-great competition beholden to its sponsors. Remember Gazprom, anyone? UEFA was not so moralistic then.

‌



Anyhow, as one of their later holier-than-thou statements on FIFA and Gianni Infantino said, UEFA now cherishes the principle of football belonging to the fans. Ah, lovely.

‌



You never know, that principle might get an outing over the next couple of days when President Ceferin and the great and good of UEFA convene in that well-known hub of the common fan, Monaco. And when they have stopped congratulating themselves on the perceived success of the newish Champions League format - the interminable, seemingly random tide of matches that produce glaringly obvious knockout contenders - they might well produce more flowery indignation about FIFA and Infantino.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

But for now, they have backed out of a boycott of FIFA competitions after apparently receiving assurances that no repeat of Infantino’s scheme to sell off World Cup rights to private investors will ever materialise. Which, in one sense, is a good thing.

‌



It means the under-20 women’s World Cup can go ahead in a week’s time in Poland. It is good that young players who had nothing to do with Infantino’s plot can perform on a big stage.

View 3 Images Samuel Eto'o has given his support to Gianni Infantino (Image: Getty Images)

But if the lifting of the threat of a boycott becomes a set-in-stone policy decision over dinners in Monte Carlo, it will be a cop-out. It is almost a month since the news of Infantino’s Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal broke to widespread outrage.

‌



UEFA, the Football Association, various football federations, and political leaders have not only expressed their distaste for Infantino’s money-making scheme, they have all but told him to resign. But Infantino is proving to be even more thick-skinned than most people thought.

And we already knew he was very thick-skinned. Even an open letter calling for him to leave his post - signed by French World Cup winners Emmanuel Petit, Bixente Lizarazu and Robert Pires - has had no effect on Infantino.

Brazilian legends Cafu and Roberto Carlos have issued statements giving their full support to Infantino, as did Cameroon great Samuel Eto’o. Infantino is going to try and brazen this one out. Or tough it out, depending on your take.

‌



View 3 Images Emmanuel Petit has signed an open letter calling for a change of leadership at FIFA (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Let’s put it this way. He is not going to be forced out of office by grand, highfalutin words from UEFA, an organisation many at FIFA consider to be full of its own importance, don’t forget.

Action, not words, will force Infantino out, which is why he will probably see UEFA’s lifting of the threat of an immediate boycott as some sort of minor triumph. This is why UEFA needs to have its ace card ready to use sooner rather than later.

Article continues below

If Infantino plans to preside over the next World Cup, UEFA will not sanction the participation of its 55 members. It is as simple as that. And when they are not having fun in the billionaires’ playground of Monaco, they need to make that abundantly clear over the next few days.

Sports.content:
Chelsea ready last-ditch Alex Scott bid with Enzo Fernandez closer to £120m exit

Chelsea have their sights set on Alex Scott to replace Enzo Fernandez, who is closer than ever to an exit with Manchester City now ready to pay the midfielder's £120m price tag

View 2 Images Alex Scott is wanted by Chelsea as a replacement for Enzo Fernandez (Image: James Gill/Danehouse)

Chelsea are ready to make a last-ditch mega offer to sign Alex Scott as a replacement for Enzo Fernandez.

‌



Bournemouth are adamant that Scott is not for sale after already turning down a £64m offer from Chelsea earlier in the window. But Chelsea remain keen on the 23-year-old midfielder and are ready to test Bournemouth’s resolve again as Scott is their No 1 target to replace Fernandez.

‌



Chelsea have also looked at Real Madrid ’s Eduardo Camavinga but they have pursued Scott all summer and want to try and get him. Bournemouth have insisted they will not make any more sales and shifting that position now for one player would also put them at risk of a potential backlash from others.

‌



Manchester City are targeting Chelsea midfielder Fernandez and are lining up a last-ditch bid to bring in the Argentina star. Chelsea are demanding £120m and have made it clear they want a replacement before they do business on Fernandez.

The Blues are also targeting a cut-price deal for Aston Villa keeper Emiliano Martinez who has been offered to Chelsea. Villa are ready to offload the World Cup winning keeper who is open to moving to Stamford Bridge this summer.

Sports.title: David Raya reveals new goal Arsenal stars and Mikel Arteta and have sights set on
Sports.content:
David Raya reveals new goal Arsenal stars and Mikel Arteta and have sights set on

Arsenal are looking to retain their Premier League crown - a feat few teams have achieved - with European success also on their radar after last season's near miss

View 3 Images David Raya helped Arsenal finally end their title wait (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

David Raya insists Arsenal are determined to build a dynasty of success - and prove their title was not just a one-off. The Arsenal keeper says the Gunners are targeting even more trophies after winning their first title in 22 years last season.

‌



Gunners keeper Raya even claimed they have got the Champions League in their sights and well as the domestic cups and retaining the Premier League.

‌



Spain international Raya, 30, said: “We want to become winners, not just a one-off. I think we’re going to have to attack the league again, attack the cups, attack the Champions League because we want more.

‌



“We want all the trophies, and we are confident that we can beat anybody at any time, so we just have to be focused on ourselves and do better than last season.”

Mikel Arteta has already insisted Arsenal are “hungry” for more trophies and that winning mentality has clearly spread to the rest of the dressing room.

Arsenal set to announce striker transfer as target sends farewell message READ MORE :

Alan Shearer makes Julian Alvarez transfer prediction as Arsenal target nowhere to be seen READ MORE :

They have never won the Champions League before and European success is a clear target for Arsenal as they look to enjoy a period of domination beyond last season’s title. Arteta has already delivered a pep talk to his players about winning more - and the players have bought in to their manager’s message.

‌



Raya was named in the Professional Footballers’ Association Team of the year along with teammates Jurrien Timber, Declan Rice, William Saliba and Gabriel. That was a remarkable achievement to dominate the votes from their fellow pros and Raya says it was a reflection of how strong they were in the Premier League last season.

The Gunners ended their long wait for a title while they also reached the Champions League final where they lost out to French giants Paris Saint Germain.

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta has added more quality to his Arsenal squad (Image: Getty Images)

‌



But Raya says winning the title was hugely important for the club as it will give them extra belief and was also recognition of how good they were.

Raya said: “The season was incredible, collectively and individually. I think we deserved to be there and be champions, so that was the most important thing. Every season is very, very long with ups and downs, but I think we dealt with everything that was thrown at us and it was an incredible season to lift the trophy, to give Arsenal the Premier League after 22 years, so, yeah, an amazing season.”

Arsenal have spent big already in the window with Bruno Guimaraes coming in from Newcastle for £75m plus Christos Tzolis. Gunners boss Arteta has also strengthened the meanest defence in the league by bringing in Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa in a deal worth £55m.

‌



Raya said: “I think we defensively – not just the defence but I think all the players from the striker to me – have a good defensive willingness in that way. Of course, Ezri coming, adding to the squad, is going to add a lot of competitiveness inside the team, which is incredible and is really, really good for the whole squad.”

View 3 Images Arsenal fell narrowly short in the Champions League - but are determined to take the final step (Image: Getty Images)

Raya won the Golden Glove for a third consecutive season with 19 clean sheets from 37 league appearances. That was Raya’s third successive Golden Glove, with just a trio of fine goalkeepers claiming that same hat-trick in the past, Pepe Reina (2006/08), Joe Hart (2011/13) and Ederson (2020/22).

‌



But Raya paid tribute to his teammates for their contribution to his personal achievement. Arsenal had three of the four defenders make the PFA Team of the Year with Timber, Gabriel and Saliba all getting recognition. Raya has already one clean sheet under his belt this season after the 3-0 win over Coventry and is targeting many more.

He added: “It’s not just me. I’ve always said the same, it’s collective stuff. “Obviously I’ve been part of it and it’s the third time consecutively, but we cannot stop there. We want to do one more and another one because that means that it’s easier to win games when you keep those clean sheets, so keep them coming and hopefully more Golden Gloves coming our way.”

Sports.title: 'He's the one we wanted': Newcastle sign Gonzalez from Man City
Sports.content:
Newcastle have signed Nico Gonzalez from Man City.

The deal for the 24-year-old midfielder is set to reach £50m after add-ons. He will wear the No 6 shirt at St James' Park.

The midfielder said his goodbyes to his City team-mates on Tuesday morning before travelling to Newcastle and completed a medical on Wednesday, before he was presented to the club's fans ahead of their Carabao Cup clash with West Brom.

The Spaniard has become Matthias Jaissle's second signing as Magpies head coach after Amar Dedic joined last week.

Former Spain U21 international Gonzalez joined City from Porto in February 2025 and played 59 times for the club, scoring four goals.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nico Gonzalez was spotted in Newcastle ahead of his medical on Wednesday

'He's the one we wanted'

Newcastle sporting director Ross Wilson said Gonzalez had been the Magpies' primary target, in a summer where they have lost Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali to Arsenal and Tottenham, given his experience already with Barcelona, Porto and in the Premier League with Manchester City.

He said: "We've worked patiently on this transfer for a number of weeks. This was the one we wanted, and we're delighted to welcome Nico to Newcastle United this evening. He was an ambitious target but following our discussions, he was so keen to join this club.

"He fits the exact criteria we set for this position and we weren't prepared to compromise on that. He's 24 years old, with an abundance of elite experience across Manchester City, FC Porto and Barcelona. He's already already shown his quality in the Premier League and we're sure there is more to come here in a black and white shirt."

Sports.title: Humphries out to deny Littler historic clean sweep after winning PC28
Sports.content:
Luke Humphries beat Brendan Dolan in the final to win his third Players Championship title of the season on the second day of action in Leicester.

Humphries, who reclaimed the world No 2 position in the PDC rankings from Gian van Veen during the course of the day, beat Ireland's Dolan 8-6 to win PC28 for his first title in the series since PC17 in May, also held at the Mattioli Arena.

Dolan had defeated Luke Littler 7-4 in their semi-final to deny the world No 1 a blockbuster meeting with Humphries.

Humphries beat Mike De Decker 7-4 in his semi-final, two rounds after surviving six match darts against Danny Noppert to win that match 6-5.

Littler was making just his second Players Championship appearance of the season after a quarter-final defeat to eventual PC27 winner Jermaine Wattimena on Tuesday.

Having sat out the first 26 Players Championship events this year, Littler is aiming to make the top 64 on the Order of Merit over the tournaments that remain to qualify for the finals in Minehead in November amid his bid for a historic clean sweep of PDC major titles this season.

A quarter-final and semi-final appearance in Leicester mean he now sits in 125th place in the Order of Merit, £16,750 behind 64th place. Six events remain before the finals with Littler needing to play, and play well, in further events if he is to have a chance of making up the further ground required to qualify.

He still needs to win the World Series, World Grand Prix, European Championship, Grand Slam of Darts and Players Championship Finals this season in order to achieve something no one has ever managed in the sport.

The World Series event takes place in Amsterdam on September 17-20 and finishes two days before the next Players Championship double header gets under way in Den Bosch, by which time Littler will know whether or not he remains on course for the clean sweep.

Image: Littler has won every PDC major title so far in 2026

Littler has won every major title on the PDC circuit so far in 2026 - the World Championship, Masters, UK Open, Premier League, World Cup of Darts and World Matchplay.

On Wednesday in Leicester, Littler made light work of Stephen Rosney in the first round, winning 6-4, before his day nearly ended in the next round as he survived six match darts against world number 107 Benjamin Pratnemer, eventually winning a final-leg decider.

Quickfire wins against Martin Schindler, Andy Boulton and Krzysztof Ratajski sent him through to the last four, but Dolan was too good for him

'I don't want him to have the clean sweep' - Humphries keen to deny Littler major history

Humphries returned to competitive action this week for the first time since his shock round-one exit to Cameron Menzies in the World Matchplay on July 20.

He lost 6-3 Cam Crabtree in Tuesday's first round in Leicester but returned on Wednesday to win all seven of his matches.

Humphries was only playing in his ninth such floor event the year, although he has now won three times after victories at PC4 and PC17.

He sits 13th in the standings and with £52,000 won so far is effectively assured of featuring in Minehead.

"To be honest, I know it sounds crazy being one of the best players in the world, I just came here for a bit of practice. Just to get myself in and feel normal again," said Humphries.

"I've only played that matchplay in two months so I just had to get myself back into it. I didn't want to go straight in to the Euro Tour this weekend with no practice.

"Obviously that's the reason I was here but once you get to the latter stages you're like 'right, ok, you can go on and win this now'. I must admit, I didn't really think I'd go on and win one this week because of the lack of practice, but I've had two good days, a lot of practice and hopefully in the next couple of weeks or couple pf months I can keep building on that.

"I'm going to get back on the practice board at home as much as I can now and I'm going to dedicate the rest of the year to trying to be my best and trying to push Luke - and not just Luke, but everyone else because I want to stay at No 2. Whether that happens or not, I'm going to fight for it because I'm going to try my best.

Asked whether the win would give him an extra boost heading to the Hungarian Darts Trophy this weekend, Humphries replied: "One hundred per cent. It's good confidence because I didn't really play my best but I still managed to go on and win.

"I don't think a lot of people have played their best these last two days, to be fair. It's been funny. Luke hasn't played his best either. Had a couple of good runs, he won't care.

"Obviously, I'm kind of just looking about trying to get a bit of practice and I've done that so for me now it's about putting in the dedication for the rest of the year because I want to go on and win a major.

"I don't want him to have the clean sweep. As much as everyone would love to see it, I'd love to win one this year and go to the Worlds in a bit of confidence.

"So this will do me good and I'm going to enjoy tonight and enjoy the moment."

Sports.title: FIA confirms Mercedes granted engine upgrades despite Red Bull complaints
Sports.content:
The FIA has confirmed that Mercedes have been granted the opportunity to make upgrades to their engine despite protestations from rival teams.

Following the introduction of all-new engines for the 2026 season, Formula 1's governing body implemented an Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) system, designed to allow manufacturers to catch up to the performance of the leading power unit during the rules cycle.

It was revealed in June after the first round of performance assessment, which included the first five rounds of the season, that the FIA had adjudged Red Bull to have the strongest engine and had granted upgrades to Mercedes, Ferrari, Audi and Honda.

The FIA never revealed their findings to the media, but teams and drivers confirmed the outcome publicly, while a document revealing the results was also leaked.

The ruling was seen as controversial because the consensus in the paddock was that Mercedes, whose works team had won the first six grands prix of the season, were being given an upgrade, while Red Bull, who had managed just a single podium in that time, would potentially lose more ground to their rivals.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix.

Red Bull driver Max Verstappen spoke out against the findings, while Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff raised further questions over the FIA's processes when he said in July that his team have "the most powerful power unit".

The FIA refrained from publicly confirming the results while a review was carried out, but now, following the second round of assessment, which concluded with the Hungarian Grand Prix ahead of the sport's summer break, the findings from both periods have been announced.

An FIA statement said: "For the first period: Mercedes were determined to be in the two to four per cent window, and will thus be allowed one additional homologation in 2026 and an additional one in 2027, together with corresponding cost cap and dyno testing increases.

"Audi, Ferrari and Honda were determined to be above four per cent, and will thus be allowed two additional homologations in 2026 and two in 2027, together with corresponding cost cap and dyno testing increases."

While this part of the FIA's statement was confirmation of information that had been leaked in June, their findings for the second period provided a further blow for Red Bull.

Had upgrades made by any of the other teams since June been adjudged to have propelled their performance beyond Red Bull's, the Milton Keynes squad could have been granted their own upgrade opportunity.

However, the statement said: "For the second period, no additional homologations were granted to any of the Power Unit Manufacturers."

That means that Red Bull are at the very least seen to be performing within two per cent of the best engine, and may well still be adjudged to have the strongest power unit.

Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli leads his team-mate George Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton by 59 points at the top of the drivers' standings, while Verstappen is 130 points back from the Italian in sixth.

Mercedes are 87 points clear of Ferrari at the top of the constructors' standings, while third-placed McLaren, who use a Mercedes engine, have found form with reigning world champion Lando Norris winning the last two races.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on the Sky Sports F1 Show podcast, Bernie Collins believes Lando Norris is still in the title fight after his recent improvement with two back-to-back wins.

Mercedes have been free to use their 2026 upgrade since the first-round results were communicated in June, but are not thought to have done so yet. Ferrari, Audi and Honda are thought to have each introduced one of their two upgrades for 2026.

FIA director of single seater Nikolas Tombazis said: "The FIA has undertaken thorough and exhaustive analysis as part of our ADUO review process.

"With the release of the findings of period two, we are confident that, based on the quality of the data, its analysis is incredibly robust, giving us a high level of confidence in our findings.

"We also have to respect the confidentiality and intellectual property of the teams and their Power Unit Manufacturers in disseminating any details from the findings.

"This is the first year of ADUO so naturally there are areas which we may evolve over time, in discussion with all the PU Manufacturers"

The third ADUO review period commenced with the Dutch Grand Prix over the weekend, and runs until the Mexico City Grand Prix on November 1.

Sports.title: Villa agree Watkins sale, Jackson lined up as replacement
Sports.content:
Aston Villa have agreed a deal to sell Ollie Watkins to Al Hilal, and are set to replace him with Chelsea forward Nicolas Jackson.

The deal for Watkins is understood to be worth £50m, with Jackson set to join from the Blues in a transfer which could reach £65m.

Watkins is keen on the move to Saudi Arabia, and at least one bid was previously rejected by Villa. They did not want to sell the England international, but have now accepted Al Hilal's latest offer.

Chelsea's plan all summer has been to sell Jackson and Liam Delap. Atletico Madrid also want Jackson, but may not be able to offer as much as Villa. Jackson worked with Villa manager Unai Emery when they were both at Villarreal.

Jackson, who joined Chelsea from Villarreal in 2023, spent last season on loan at Bayern Munich.

The Bundesliga champions had an obligation to buy the forward included in the deal worth £56.25m, but Jackson did not reach the number of appearances required to exercise the option.

Sports.title: 'Zero per cent chance' - Atleti shut down Barca's Alvarez plea amid Arsenal interest
Sports.content:
The noise around Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez refuses to go away - so where are things after a chaotic few days surrounding the in-demand Argentine?

Alvarez did not train with his Atletico team-mates on Wednesday, though this was officially put down to a stomach bug and a poor night's sleep rather than anything to do with his future.

The 26-year-old wants to join Barcelona, who again went public with their desire to sign him on Wednesday in a video interview with president Joan Laporta.

The truth is that we're very interested in the player," he told their club channels. "We'd like our offer to be accepted, and we say this with all due respect for Atletico Madrid."

However, Atletico's stance remains that they categorically do not want to sell him - and even more emphatically that he will not be sold to Barcelona in particular. Not only because the two are rivals, but also due to bad blood between the clubs over previous transfers.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Friday Night Football panel discuss whether Arsenal are still shy of a world-class attacker that would see them get over the line to win their first UEFA Champions League title.

Atletico have not commented directly but Marca, Spain's biggest sports newspaper, have received on-the-record quotes from the club saying: "The player is being portrayed as the victim, but we are the only victims in this case.

"[Barcelona] have harmed us both financially and socially. There is a zero-per-cent chance of selling him to Barcelona - it's not about money, it's about dignity."

The situation around Alvarez's future has become "extremely tense", according to Atletico expert and journalist Ruben Uría.

His public desire to leave has made him so unpopular with the club's supporters that he was booed off after their 2-2 draw with Villarreal on Sunday.

"Neither Miguel Gil Marín (CEO of Atlético Madrid) nor the Apollo board want to sell the player to Barcelona," Uría told Sky Sports News. "The entire Apollo board supports Gil Marín's decision. Alvarez has been told."

According to Uría, Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta has remained in contact with his former Atletico employers in recent days after Alvarez was booed off by supporters in the opening LaLiga game against Villarreal.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the Transfer Talk podcast, Sam Tighe and Daniel Storey debate whether Arsenal should gamble on signing Julian Alvarez despite the striker clearly wanting to sign for Barcelona.

The Gunners remain interested in Alvarez and would be prepared to break their transfer record, the £105m paid out for Declan Rice three summers ago, to bring him to the Emirates Stadium - but the player himself does not want to move to London.

Could Arsenal still end up signing Alvarez?

Sky Sports News senior reporter Rob Dorsett:

"I think even if Arsenal are outsiders at the moment, and the official word is that Arsenal aren't holding out great hopes of making this deal happen.

'But if Alvarez thinks his future needs to be away from Atletico Madrid after upsetting his supporters and they won't sell him to Barcelona, his only option is to join Arsenal, the Premier League champions.

"At the moment, he says he doesn't want to do that. But there are still six days of the window left."

Sports.title: Chelsea in talks with Martínez’s camp as Aston Villa close on striker Jackson
Sports.content:
Chelsea have been offered Emiliano Martínez and are considering a bid for the goalkeeper. The club are in talks with Martínez’s camp, and are also braced for a bid from Manchester City for the World Cup winner’s Argentina teammate Enzo Fernández.

Martínez has told Aston Villa he wants to leave but a move to Juventus collapsed last week after Villa had signed his replacement, Zion Suzuki, from Parma for £30m.

Goalkeeper has been a problematic position for Chelsea in recent seasons, with Robert Sánchez mainly the No 1 but prone to mistakes. Mike Penders, 21, is being lined up to become the first-choice, but the Chelsea manager, Xabi Alonso, selected Sánchez for Monday’s win against Fulham when two Sánchez errors led to goals.

The availability and offer of Martínez has intrigued Chelsea and they are mulling whether it is too good an opportunity to turn down. The 33-year-old is a vastly experienced serial trophy winner. He won the World Cup in 2022 and reached the 2026 final. He also lifted the Europa League with Villa last season and the FA Cup with Arsenal in 2020.

Martínez was not in the squad for Villa’s heavy opening-weekend defeat at Brighton. Marco Bizot started in goal with Suzuki on the bench. Martínez joining Chelsea may solve a problem for both clubs.

Chelsea and Villa have, meanwhile, have agreed a £65m deal for striker Nicolas Jackson to join the Midlands club.

The Senegal international was also a target for Atlético Madrid but is poised to join Villa as a potential replacement for Ollie Watkins, who is expected to join the Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal for a £50m fee. Villa also want a centre-back and may target West Ham’s Jean-Clair Todibo.

City are expected to make an offer for Fernández and any deal would leave Chelsea seeking a replacement before Tuesday night’s transfer deadline. Chelsea previously told City to pay £120m by 14 August or miss out, but the midfielder remains a priority target for City’s manager, Enzo Maresca, who he worked with at Chelsea. Alonso started Reece James and Roméo Lavia in central midfield at Fulham, introducing Fernández from the bench.

City continued their midfield rebuild on Wednesday by buying Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in a €100m (£85.7m) deal and selling Nico González to Newcastle for £52m.

Sports.title: Uefa to lift boycott threat after Fifa promises no World Cup sale repeat
Sports.content:
Uefa is to drop its threatened boycott of Fifa competitions after receiving concrete guarantees that the global governing body will never attempt a repeat of Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell stakes in the World Cup.

European teams have been cleared for participation in the upcoming Under-20 Women’s World Cup, along with subsequent tournaments, after Fifa provided the binding assurances that no equivalent of its president’s ill-fated scheme will be put on the table.

Uefa had threatened the ­boycott after Infantino’s Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal was revealed and ­doubled down after it was ­withdrawn, saying the condition that “such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again” had not been met.

Quick Guide How do I 

Despite exchanging barbs in ­public, Uefa and Fifa are understood to have been having private ­discussions over the terms of ­removing the ­boycott threat for several weeks, with the European governing body finally ­getting the reassurances it required.

When Fifa confirmed its decision to abandon FFE four days after it became public it neglected to pledge that a similar privatisation plan would not be repeated, but it has now done so in private correspondence.

The decision to drop the boycott allows England, who named their squad for the under-20 tournament last week, to travel to Poland in time for the opening game against Canada on 5 September. France and Spain had also listed their travelling party in anticipation that the boycott would be lifted. Portugal, Italy and the host nation are the other European countries due to compete.

View image in fullscreen England’s under-20s will travel to the World Cup in Poland. Photograph: Carlos Rodrigues/The FA/Getty Images

Fifa welcomed the end of the boycott on Wednesday, saying: “Fifa is pleased that all qualified teams ‌will be participating in the upcoming Fifa Under-20 Women’s World Cup. Fifa strongly believes that football has the power to unite, even in challenging circumstances, and looks forward to welcoming all teams and players to Poland.”

The boycott is yet to be publicly dropped by Uefa, whose executive committee and federation chiefs meet in Monte Carlo on Thursday. The 55 heads of Uefa’s member associations will convene before the Champions League draw during what is traditionally a significant few days in the European football calendar.

Uefa’s position that Infantino must be replaced has not changed and further steps regarding its stance towards the Fifa leadership will also be discussed at the meeting.

Italy’s football federation (FIGC) on Wednesday became the latest to publicly withdraw support for Infantino. “This decision is intended to clearly and transparently express the FIGC’s position … regarding the recent initiatives promoted by the Fifa president concerning the governance and development of international competitions,” it said.

There will be relief in some quarters that younger players, in particular, will not become embroiled in the volatile battle for football’s future. But the fact that Fifa has been forced to mitigate for its president’s actions is another humiliation for a persistently scandal-hit organisation.

Sports.title: Ayyoub Bouaddi: maths student, chess fan and Manchester City’s new Rodri
Sports.content:
“He’s like a computer,” the former Lille head of academy recruitment, Mathieu Frison, says of the €100m (£85.7m) Manchester City recruit Ayyoub Bouaddi. “You teach him something, he learns it and can do it immediately.” Bouaddi has the mountainous challenge at his new club of replacing the world’s best central midfielder. It would be difficult for anyone but at 18 it feels monumental, although those who know the Morocco international best would not bet against him.

Bouaddi has known only Lille and Ligue 1 but is entering one of the biggest clubs in the world where a season without a trophy is deemed a failure. For someone so young, however, he has plenty of experience. He made his European debut three days after his 16th birthday and has played three full seasons in the first team, culminating in a place at the World Cup this summer.

At 13, Lille beat off competition from France’s elite to sign Bouaddi, after showing his parents the pathway he could follow to the first team. There was never lengthy discussion over money, just what would be best for a boy who wanted to reach the highest level. Lille’s track record is impressive, the club bringing through Bouaddi’s soon-to-be Premier League rivals Carlos Baleba and Leny Yoro, among others, in recent times.

Frison visited the Bouaddi family in Creil, an hour north of Paris, to explain why a move to Lille would be beneficial after scouts spotted Bouaddi playing for his home town team in a tournament. “He was not here at the beginning of the meeting with his parents, and he came in the house with the ball on a string,” Frison recalls. “He did a very good trick; he always had this ball in his hand and he always played in his house, so he was already very talented technically.”

City have faith in him, although plenty of the expenditure is based on promise rather than a finished article. He is not someone who creates highlight reels, but does the dirty work and plays for the team. Others may have sought someone with more miles in their legs, but Enzo Maresca is rebuilding a midfield for the long term after Rodri’s departure for Barcelona and with a £52m deal agreed for Nico González to join Newcastle. The 23-year-old Elliot Anderson arrived from Nottingham Forest as the first cog in the machine, and Enzo Fernández is also wanted by his former manager at Chelsea.

Bouaddi, the only boy of four siblings, passed all his exams a year early, is studying for a mathematics degree remotely and speaks English. He is a deep thinker, someone able to cut out the distractions at home and on the pitch. “On the bus, while everyone is watching YouTube videos or listening to music, he will play chess for one or two hours,” Frison says. “In the evening when all the players played Fifa or were on their phones, he studied mathematics, physics, science. His parents didn’t need to push him to do this – he wanted to learn.”

View image in fullscreen Ayyoub Bouaddi plays for Morocco after representing France, the country of his birth, up to under-21 level. Photograph: Mauro Pimentel/AFP/Getty Images

Bouaddi represented the country of his birth, France, from under-16 to under-21 and is regarded as a huge loss for Les Bleus. “Bouaddi, for me, is one of the smartest players I’ve known in my coaching career,” says the former France under-18 coach Landry Chauvin, who had Bouaddi in his squad for the Lafarge tournament in Limoges in 2024. “He reminds me a lot of Yoann Gourcuff, who I saw in Rennes a few years ago. As soon as the tournament was over, I told Les Espoirs [France’s Under-21s] that he should have nothing more to do with me, that he had to continue to progress and go above and beyond.”

Rodri has won everything worth winning over the past decade while Bouaddi was growing up. Emulating the Spaniard will not be straightforward for a player who is a long way from being fully developed. “When Maresca asks him to do something tactically, he knows that 100% Ayyoub will take the best position for the team,” Frison says.

View image in fullscreen Ayyoub Bouaddi celebrates Lille’s Champions League victory over Real Madrid on his 17th birthday. Photograph: Benoît Tessier/Reuters

“He will respect the game model with intensity, even when he is tired; he will respect the process. Everyone wants a player who can make the difference individually because they can help you to win the game but you need reliable players who you can trust 100% during 60 games of the season. And Ayyoub, he’s this kind of player.”

View image in fullscreen Ayyoub Bouaddi and his family chose Lille because of the pathway to the first team. Photograph: Sameer Al-Doumy/AFP/Getty Images

Bouaddi has consistently mixed with – and surpassed – older players, quickly improving as he rapidly went through each step to the top. He was 16 when he featured for Chauvin’s France Under-18s and on his 17th birthday he faced Real Madrid in the Champions League, playing 90 minutes in a 1-0 win against Jude Bellingham et al.

“A very intelligent boy who adapts quickly, capable of playing in every position in the middle, capable of evolving in a changing environment, permanently working hard, but also always with his head held high,” Chauvin says. “He has the ability to scan the actions very quickly, to take the information before the others. Very comfortable technically, he always has the right position on the field. And on top of that, he’s a boy who’s charming in everyday life; very respectful, very well educated, who knows all the rules.

“The man who hides behind the footballer is simply a very beautiful person. Every time I went to Lille, I would send him a little text, and immediately he came to greet me, even though he was already a pro. Many in his place would have snubbed the under-18 coach, but not Ayyoub.”

Sports.title: Football Daily | Celtic raise the bar for calamitous capitulations in Europe
Sports.content:
LASK ONE LAUGHING

When Celtic opened the scoring against Lask courtesy of a low Callum McGregor shot after 21 minutes on Tuesday night, the Scottish champions looked to have exorcised their Bigger Cup demons from 12 months ago. Four goals ahead of their Austrian hosts on aggregate, it seemed utterly inconceivable that Martin O’Neill’s side could emulate, let alone eclipse, their humiliation at the hands of Kairat Almaty last August and the match commentator intoned as much. “And with that moment, this tie surely moves beyond the grasp of Lask,” soothed Bill Leslie, as the Celtic skipper’s deflected daisy-cutter fizzed past the home goalkeeper and rippled the Austrian champions’ net. While one could argue Bill has commentated on enough fitba over the years to know better than to count unhatched chickens, not even the combined forces of Mystic Meg and Nostradamus could have foreseen the calamitous capitulation that was about to unfold. From a position of apparent indomitability, Celtic proceeded to ship five goals without reply to endure what is arguably the Grand Old Team To Play For’s greatest European embarrassment yet.

“We should have been out of sight by half-time,” wailed Martin O’Neill at the end of a 5-1 second leg pasting that actually flattered his side. “We scored a goal, which was great. We missed two great, great opportunities. And then we give them a lifeline just before half-time and then one just after it. And they come roaring back. And obviously we conceded, from our viewpoint, not good goals at all. But that’s my team and that’s my responsibility.” Of course, O’Neill’s was just one of many angry post-mortems with Celtic grandees such as Chris Sutton, Kasper Schmeichel, Stiliyan Petrov and Neil Lennon all queuing up to stick the boot in, having apparently forgotten their contributions to various Euro horror shows for the club down the years.

While Celtic’s exit at the same stage of Bigger Cup last season was attributed to a famously parsimonious board’s reluctance to spend money on players until after qualification for the league phase had been secured, the same accusation cannot be levelled this time around. Having parted with £23m – a decent wedge by fitba standards – on four new players over the summer with more due through the door, club bean-counters are now being criticised for selling top players Arne Engels and Daizen Maeda before qualification had been secured. Unable to do right for doing wrong, Celtic’s owners must now mull over the loss of a series of Bigger Cup paydays that could cost them as much as £40m. It will be a source of constant regret that Tuesday’s second leg wasn’t played at Celtic Park, where the timely and now traditional pitch invasion would almost certainly have denied Lask the 90th-minute goal that took the tie to extra time.

While Celtic’s humbling is also an embarrassment for Scottish fitba, there will be little or no sympathy from rivals who will view their misfortune as karmic retribution for a title acquired through a combination of highly questionable refereeing and some atrocious fan behaviour during that final-day title decider against Hearts. “We got what we deserved,” seethed McGregor after the game. “Now we’ll see what people are made of,” he added, having just shown what he and his teammates were made of. After Tuesday’s shambles, one suspects it will take more than a home win over Falkirk on Saturday to ease the pain.
