Sports.title: Sunderland weigh up Jack Grealish loan with Marseille’s Igor Paixão also a target
Sports.content:
Sunderland are exploring a potential loan move for Jack Grealish, but formal negotiations with Manchester City are yet to take place.

For the moment sources say the former England winger remains one of a number of “players of interest” on Régis Le Bris’s transfer window shortlist, with Sunderland’s manager also keen on Igor Paixão of Marseille.

The 26-year-old Brazilian winger is understood to be receptive to a transfer to the Stadium of Light but Marseille and Sunderland remain locked in talks over a fee for the former Feyenoord player. Paixão scored 12 goals and contributed eight assists in 43 appearances for Marseille last season but the French club’s financial difficulties mean they are prepared to sell one of their prize assets.

It is possible that Sunderland could acquire both Paixão and Grealish, although a deal for the latter would involve a degree of haggling about the percentage of Grealish’s wages – believed to total £300,000 a week – that Sunderland would be willing to pay. With the 30-year-old out of contract at City next summer, any loan agreement would almost certainly include an option to buy.

Grealish is understood to be open to a move to Wearside. The winger spent much of last season sidelined by a foot injury during a loan stint at Everton, and has recently been spotted out and about in the north-east with Jordan Pickford.

The pair struck up a friendship during Grealish’s time on Merseyside and Pickford, a former Sunderland goalkeeper, delighted in showing his friend a few favourite haunts.

Everton are expected to try to re-sign Grealish on loan but Sunderland can offer one of English football’s “forgotten men” the added attraction of Europa League football.

Grealish would be far from a typical Le Bris signing – young players with potential signed, mainly, from Europe – but his presence could help raise the club’s international profile at a moment when Sunderland’s commercial department are pursuing off field deals as far afield as the United States and Africa.

Nottingham Forest are in talks over the €15m (£12.8m) signing of the Celta Vigo right-back Javi Rueda, which would probably be their final move of the window after signing Liam Delap from Chelsea.

Oliver Glasner has been seeking someone who can play right wing-back and the 24-year-old former Real Madrid academy player fits the desired profile.

The former Spain youth international joined Celta three years ago from Madrid, who will receive half the fee. He made his first-team breakthrough last season, playing 26 La Liga games and 11 in the Europa League, helping his side to reach the quarter-finals.

Forest confirmed on Wednesday yesterday that the wing-back Eric da Silva Moreira will spend the season on loan to the Dutch side Excelsior to aid his development.

Chelsea have agreed to sell Delap to Forest in a deal worth £50m and have loaned Axel Disasi to Crystal Palace for the season. Disasi has also been loaned out to Aston Villa and West Ham since he signed for Chelsea from Monaco.

The defender said: “I know that it’s very tough to play against Palace at Selhurst Park – so I’m looking forward to being on the other side now.”

Brentford have struck an agreement with West Ham to sign El Hadji Malick Diouf for £35m plus up to £5m in add-ons. The left-back has been keen to leave West Ham since their relegation.

Southampton have contacted West Ham about bringing their former captain, James Ward-Prowse, back to the club. The 31-year-old is out of favour at West Ham and Saints, who were beaten by Nuno Espírito Santo’s side in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday, are keen to strengthen in midfield after the £30m sale of Shea Charles to Fulham. Ward-Prowse, who joined Southampton aged eight and made his first-team debut at 16, is one direct free-kick shy of matching David Beckham’s Premier League record of 18 free-kick goals.

Additional reporting from Will Unwin, Jacob Steinberg and Ben Fisher.

Sports.title: Raheem Sterling charged with dangerous driving and nitrous oxide possession
Sports.content:
Raheem Sterling has been charged with dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide after a crash involving a Lamborghini on the motorway, police have said.

Hampshire and Isle of Wight constabulary said the charges followed a single-vehicle collision on the M3 southbound, near Minley interchange, on 28 May. The 31-year-old former England forward is accused of dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen.

The force said that no other vehicles were involved in the collision and no injuries were reported. Sterling, from Berkshire, is due to appear at Basingstoke magistrates court for a hearing on 15 September.

Quick Guide How do I 

He scored 20 goals in 82 appearances for England, helping Gareth Southgate’s side to reach the 2018 World Cup semi-finals and the Euro 2020 final. Sterling came through the academy at QPR before joining Liverpool, where he made his senior debut and moved in 2015 to Manchester City, with whom he won four Premier League titles, five League Cups and the FA Cup.

Sterling left for Chelsea in 2022 but after falling out of favour he spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Arsenal. After leaving Stamford Bridge, he joined the Dutch club Feyenoord on a short-term deal until the end of last season. He is now without a club.

In the 2021 Queen’s birthday honours, Sterling was made an MBE for services to racial equality in sport after fronting anti-racism and discrimination campaigns and speaking out strongly against racism on and off the pitch.

Sports.title: Rangers finalize deal for Portland Timbers striker Kevin Kelsy
Sports.content:
Rangers have acquired forward Kevin Kelsy from Major League Soccer’s Portland Timbers, a source with direct knowledge of the deal told the Guardian on Wednesday. That source requested anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly on the agreement. The deal, worth $13m (£9.5m) – potentially more if Kelsy hits certain performance goals for Rangers – also includes a sell-on fee for the MLS club.

The Athletic’s Tom Bogert first reported details of the deal on Wednesday morning.



Portland acquired Kelsy from Ukrainian side Shakhtar Donetsk last January, paying $6m for the Venezuela international. The 22-year-old has been erratic but ultimately productive for the Timbers, scoring 16 times in 43 appearances.

Rangers manager Derek McInnes has been vocal about wanting another striker before the end of the summer transfer window after losing Portuguese striker Youssef Chermiti to an ACL tear in early August. Portland had little intention of moving Kelsy this window, a source said this week, but the fee, a club record for an outgoing transfer, proved impossible to turn down. The Timbers already added a center forward this summer – former Tottenham and Monterrey striker Vincent Janssen – and may make other moves before the window closes.



Portland sit ninth in MLS’s Western Conference, only narrowly in position for the final play-in spot to the playoffs. They have already navigated a coaching change earlier in the season, with Phil Neville dismissed during the World Cup break. Former Leicester City and QPR boss Martí Cifuentes took over in July.



Rangers are ninth in the Scottish Premiership after a tumultuous opening to their season which has seen them yet to win in the opening two games of league play and drop into the Uefa Conference League after losing a Europa League qualifying tie to Polish side Jagiellonia Bialystok.

An anemic attack has seen McInnes push the club to sign reinforcements, including Japanese winger Daisuke Yokota. The former Girona winger Kim Min-su is expected to join the club this week.



Kelsy will travel to Glasgow this week to finalize the deal and undergo a medical and will join the team permanently when his visa is sorted. A source said on Wednesday that Kelsy is highly unlikely to feature for Rangers this weekend, when the club takes on eighth-place Aberdeen on Sunday.

In other news, Nicolas Raskin has not travelled with Rangers for their Conference League playoff tie against Czechia side Jablonec due to a potential move away from the club in this transfer window.

The 25-year-old Belgium international, who signed from Standard Liége in 2023, also missed the first leg at Ibrox last week which Rangers won 1-0. Raskin has been linked with a move to Turkish club Galatasaray.

Sports.title: Aston Villa's striker merry-go-round! Ollie Watkins set to jet off to Saudi Arabia to seal £50m switch to Al Hilal - with Nicolas Jackson heading to West Midlands for medical ahead of £65m move from Chelsea
Sports.content:
Aston Villa's striker merry-go-round! Ollie Watkins set to jet off to Saudi Arabia to seal £50m switch to Al Hilal - with Nicolas Jackson heading to West Midlands for medical ahead of £65m move from Chelsea

Ollie Watkins is poised to travel to Saudi Arabia this week to clinch his £50million move to Al Hilal – paving the way for Nicolas Jackson to join Aston Villa for a fee of up to £65m.

Watkins will collect a huge pay rise when he moves to the Pro League while Jackson is set to reunite with Villa boss Unai Emery after leaving Chelsea.

Jackson, 25, is due for a medical this week and could make his Villa debut against Arsenal on Monday.

The end to the Watkins saga will be a relief for all concerned. Watkins did not play against Brighton last Sunday, despite being Villa’s only fit striker, and the team were beaten 4-0. Emery did little to dispel the notion that Watkins had chosen not to play.

Ollie Watkins is poised to travel to Saudi Arabia to seal a £50m move to Al Hilal, while Nicolas Jackson is set for a medical at Aston Villa

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery has seen several key figures leave the club this summer

He becomes the fifth senior player to leave Villa this summer after Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne, Morgan Rogers and Ezri Konsa. Goalkeeper Emi Martinez has also been offered to Chelsea.

Daily Mail Sport reported last month how Jackson was interested in a potential switch to Villa to work with Emery again, after their time together at Villarreal.

Jackson’s name came up during conversations between Chelsea and Villa centred on Morgan Rogers, who moved to Stamford Bridge for a club-record £117m. Alejandro Garnacho joined Villa on loan from Chelsea this summer also, leaving only a permanent move as a possibility for Jackson due to rules.

Villa have long been admirers of Jackson, the 25-year-old who has also had interest from clubs across England and Europe, such as Tottenham Hotspur and Atletico Madrid.

Sports.title: Embattled LIV Golf lays off majority of staff with rebel golf tour in crisis after Saudi backers cut funding
Sports.content:
Embattled LIV Golf lays off majority of staff with rebel golf tour in crisis after Saudi backers cut funding

LIV Golf reportedly informed the majority of its staff that their jobs had been terminated on Wednesday amid the increasing uncertainty shrouding the embattled tour's future.

The circuit is battling for financial survival after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund announced it would stop funding beyond the 2026 season.

Its 2026 season came to an end at the weekend with its Indianapolis. The conclusion of the season came a week earlier than scheduled after LIV canceled its season finale - the team championship in Michigan - which had been slated for this week.

Now, just days later, the tour has laid off the majority of its staff, according to a report from Golf Digest.

The terminations were not a surprise with the tour's chiefs reportedly informing employees in July that layoffs would be coming in the following months.

The specific number of employees impacted by the layoffs is currently unknown or in which departments they work. LIV is believed to have a workforce of around 300 staff members.

LIV Golf reportedly informed the majority of its staff that their jobs had been terminated

The circuit is battling for survival after Saudi Arabia's PIF announced it would stop funding

'The funding commitment announced by PIF earlier this year will reach its conclusion,' a LIV spokesperson told Golf Digest. 'As a result, we are scaling back operations as we transition to the next chapter of LIV Golf and work toward making LIV 2.0 a reality.

'This week, we informed many of our colleagues that their employment under LIV 1.0 will end in the first week of September. We are grateful to our employees for their hard work and dedication in building LIV Golf, and we remain committed to supporting those affected through this transition.'

The rebel golf circuit, which launched in 2022 with the financial backing of the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia, paid nine-figure bonuses to lure top players like Brooks Koepka, Dustin Johnson, Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm away from the PGA Tour, offering $20m prize funds.

But it all began to fall apart earlier this year when PIF said it would no longer fund it after the 2026 season. One event in New Orleans already was scrapped.

Scott O'Neil, the chief executive of LIV, revealed last week that an investor had been lined up to fund the league's operations in 2027.

'LIV Golf has an agreement in place with a lead investor, signed by the investor and approved by the Board, to anchor the transaction and play a key role in supporting the path forward for the League’s next era, driven by and for the players,' he said.

'We’re also seeing strong interest from more than a dozen additional parties to potentially serve as minority investors, creating a multi-partner model built for long-term stability and growth.

'Notably, our next chapter will make our players the majority equity holders in LIV Golf, a first for a major global sports league, and gives the League the foundation to keep growing the game worldwide.'

Bryson DeChambeau is pictured at LIV's final event of the season in Indianapolis last weekend

However, the identity of said investor has not been yet been officially confirmed.

Golf Digest reports that BC Partners, a private equity firm based in London that has ties to GSE Worldwide - the agency that represents a sizable portion of LIV’s roster - is believed to be the investor.

The plan for what is being referred to as 'LIV Golf 2.0' is for 10 team events each year, five of them in the United States and five others around the world.

It also wants to stage events leading into the majors and having a schedule that allows its players to compete on other circuits. Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton already play on the European tour. The PGA Tour still has a one-year ban for anyone competing on LIV.

Sports.title: Chelsea offered Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa - who Juventus bid just £6m for - to fix their goalkeeper problem after Robert Sanchez shocker
Sports.content:
Emiliano Martinez has been offered to Chelsea as Aston Villa seek a new club for their want-away goalkeeper.

After his move to Juventus collapsed earlier this month despite an initial £6million offer, Martinez is now one of three senior keepers in the Villa squad following the arrival of Zion Suzuki at Villa Park.

Martinez is also Villa's top earner following the departure of Youri Tielemans to Manchester United in July, and Unai Emery intends to press ahead with Suzuki and Marco Bizot.

Earlier in the summer, Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso indicated he was happy with keepers Robert Sanchez and Mike Penders.

But Sanchez's shaky display in Chelsea's 3-2 win at Fulham raised more question marks about the Spaniard.

Aston Villa have replaced Emiliano Martinez with Zion Suzuki and he is available for transfer

Asked about Sanchez on Wednesday, Alonso said: 'Normal conversations. We have talked more about the team thing, about what we did well and what we have to do better. It was more about understanding the context.

'Every game is going to be important because we are in this process that we still need to develop things, we need to make adjustments that are more team-related.'

Chelsea have brought 21-year-old Belgian Mike Penders into their squad after a successful loan at Strasbourg last season.

Alonso today suggested he is likely to start Thursday's Carabao Cup game against Luton Town. 'He's in the squad and will have an opportunity,' he said.

The Blues rate the former Genk youth shot-stopper, who has been likened to former Chelsea man Thibaut Courtois, very highly.

A move for Martinez, at 33 years old, would not be viewed as blocking Penders' progress.

The Argentina goalkeeper has been training with Villa since returning from the World Cup and his club say he is not injured.

Robert Sanchez's position as Chelsea No 1 is under threat after his recent errors

Emery confirmed he has once again asked to leave.

'We have signed Suzuki not for the future, but for now,' the Villa boss said. 'He has shown his capacity and that he can play at our level.

'Martinez transmitted to us the possibility to have another challenge in his career, not just now and even last year, and he was thinking in case he had a possibility to change his challenges, but he stayed and performed fantastic.

'This year, again, he transmitted to us for a new challenge, and we signed Suzuki to replace him. But the scenario we have is that we have two great goalkeepers.

'(Marco) Bizot as well, when we needed him, he responded fantastically. My ideal scenario with the goalkeeper is really fantastic, but maybe we can still change something.'

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes names the Man United starlet he coached while completing his badges... and reveals why he can't stand English tea!
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes names the Man United starlet he coached while completing his badges... and reveals why he can't stand English tea!

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Bruno Fernandes has revealed Manchester United team-mate Shea Lacey was under his tutelage when he was completing his coaching badges.

Fernandes did his UEFA B diploma through United, along with Juan Mata and Nemanja Matic, and said he coached United starlet Lacey when the now 19-year-old was in the club's Under-14 side.

'His technical ability was never in doubt,' Fernandes told the Men in Blazers Media Network.

'I often joke with him because I coached him when I was taking my coaching badges, and I remember he was in the U14 team then.

'So, Juan Mata and I basically coached him for a day. I told him he's much better now than he was at 14. He is much more mature, doing very well.

'I think what they all need they want to be part of the team and play for the team is to treat every training session like a game.'

Bruno Fernandes has revealed he coached Shea Lacey when he was doing his badges

Lacey made his debut for the United first team against Aston Villa in December and was a second-half substitute in the shock 2-0 defeat by Hull on Saturday.

He has been widely tipped for success at Old Trafford and captain Fernandes believes the team have already seen a different player compared to the star who broke through last season.

'I think Shea Lacey came with a completely different mentality this season in terms of movement off the ball,' added Fernandes.

'I think that's great, and it's what I talked to him about after returning from vacation, because I watched their three games. He plays in the same position as me, which requires a high level of running and emotional intelligence in covering space and assisting teammates in attack, and he has done very well.'

Fernandes was this week crowned PFA Player of the Year after a stellar campaign at Old Trafford, which included breaking the Premier League assists record.

The 31-year-old has spent six and a half years in England after moving to United from Sporting Lisbon in January 2020.

Asked whether there was anything Mancunian about him now, he said: 'I would say not much.

'The only thing is that I now really like going to coffee shops. To be honest, I used to go in Portugal, but only for breakfast. Now, at any time of day, I can go for a coffee, which I wasn't used to doing.

The Man United captain was speaking in an interview on the Men in Blazers Media Network

'I still don't drink English black tea; I can't mix water with milk, sorry, and then tea. That's not for me yet. But Tom Heaton always has a cup of tea in his hand at any time of day. But if he calls me for a coffee I will always go. Maybe not tea, maybe a cappuccino, maybe another kind, like a latte, I don't know, but not English tea yet!'

United will aim to bounce back from the loss at Hull when they face another newly-promoted team in Ipswich at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Fernandes fumed at his team-mates after the 2-0 reverse at the MKM Stadium, blasting the side for making the 'same mistakes as last season'.

The comments prompted ex-United midfielder Paul Scholes to tell the Portuguese midfielder he 'needs to keep his mouth shut'.

Sports.title: Man United's kit clanger: Club's opening game shirt falls foul of Premier League laws as Red Devils are reminded of little-known rule after Hull City defeat
Sports.content:
Man United's kit clanger: Club's opening game shirt falls foul of Premier League laws as Red Devils are reminded of little-known rule after Hull City defeat

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United have fallen foul of Premier League kit rules after one game of the season.

The Old Trafford outfit went into the current campaign without a sleeve sponsor, following the expiration of a £20m per year deal with DXC Technology which dates back to 2022.

However, Premier League rules dictate that clubs without a sleeve sponsor should display the competition’s badge on both arms.

And eagle-eyed observers have pointed out that United did not comply during their opening day defeat at Hull City, with one sleeve left blank.

While both the Premier League and United declined to comment, Daily Mail Sport understands that the club was given a polite reminder of the rule.

Premier League rules dictate clubs without a sleeve sponsor should display the competition’s badge on both arms - but Manchester United did not

The Premier League badge was shown on the other arm of United's shirts

It is also understood that the top-flight badge will be on both sleeves when United return to action against Ipswich at Old Trafford on Sunday.

United are seeking a new shirt sleeve sponsor, having had one for the past eight seasons.

The rule-break came on a chaotic opening day for United and manager Michael Carrick, with the surprise defeat by Hull drawing plenty of criticism - including from captain Bruno Fernandes.

After the match, the United captain complained to the media that his side had made the 'same mistakes as we did last season (in away matches)'. The Portugal midfielder added: 'Every away game we give too much of the ball to them. In the first 20 minutes, the goalkeeper was the one with the most touches.

'We needed to press more, be more aggressive, and then again we need to work on set plays and not concede these types of goals. Against these types of teams, they are waiting for that moment.'

Club legend Paul Scholes, however, took issue with Fernandes' comments on his podcast The Good, The Bad & The Football.

'I'd be interested to know what he means by them. What mistakes were they giving away?' the 51-year-old former player said.

'Especially when you perform the way he did as well, I think it's probably best to keep your mouth shut. He didn't have his best performance either.'

Scholes and former United forward Dion Dublin went further, suggesting that Fernandes, alongside team-mate Luke Shaw, who also claimed after the match that United went into the fixture underprepared, had undermined manager Michael Carrick.

Bruno Fernandes - pictured without the Premier League logo - was left disappointed

Shaw had said after the match: 'It’s not us and we knew it was coming. I think as a whole, as a group, collectively, we could prepare better. Especially knowing how good they are at set plays and what their dangers are.'

Reacting to the left-back's comments, Scholes said: 'Luke Shaw always says something. And that's a slight on your staff. That's a slight on your manager. If one of your players is saying that you'd be like f***ing hell, you'd have them in on Monday morning.'

Dublin said: 'You want silence. If your skipper has to speak then he has to speak, but then you make sure he says the things that don't open a can of worms. You just don't give anyone any ammunition because the ammunition is there from your performance.'

Scholes added: 'Those comments are not so much about respect but you speak about fear of managers and the things they've said, they're a slight on the manager and staff. As a player if we did that about Sir Alex, "we weren't prepared", f***ing hell, you'd be right in and he'd probably single you out in front of the full team.'

Sports.title: PGA Tour golfer handed six-month ban after getting caught gambling on tournaments
Sports.content:
Golfer Matt Gogel has been suspended by the PGA Tour for violating its integrity program, the organization announced on Wednesday.

Gogel, 55, was handed a six-month ban from any PGA Tour-sanctioned event after being found to have gambled on tournaments.

While the professional did not place bets on any event he was competing in, the gambling on PGA Tour competitions violates the Tour's policy.

Gogel competes on the PGA Tour Champions, the PGA Tour-sanctioned senior tour open to golfers age 50 and over.

He will now be unable to compete in any tournament sanctioned by the PGA Tour until February 22, 2027.

Gogel, who said he 'unknowingly' violated Tour policy with his gambling, cooperated fully throughout the process, the PGA Tour stated.

Golfer Matt Gogel has been suspended by the PGA Tour for violating its integrity program

The 55-year-old was handed a six-month ban from any PGA Tour-sanctioned event

'In 2024 and 2025, I unknowingly violated the PGA TOUR policy by placing small recreational wagers on golf,' Gogel said in a statement.

'I want to be clear that these wagers were not placed on regular PGA TOUR events, PGA TOUR Champions events or any tournament in which I participated.

'I would never knowingly violate the integrity of the game of golf. I made an honest mistake and I look forward to playing in 2027 on the PGA TOUR Champions.'

Gogel has competed in 18 events on the Champions Tour in 2026, earning prize money of more than $760,000.

He currently stands 20th in the Tour's season-long Charles Schwab Cup points race, which culminates with the Charles Schwab Cup Championship on November 12-15.

His ban came into effect on Sunday, the day on which Gogel finished tied 30th in the Rogers Charity Classic on the senior circuit.

The player was found to have placed bets on PGA Tour-sanctioned tournaments

The PGA Tour Integrity Program prohibits wagering on any Tour-sanctioned event around the world by members, but also by anyone in their immediate circle who receives credentials to tournaments, including family, caddies and agents.

'Any Covered Person, directly or indirectly, Betting on the outcome or any other aspect of any PGA TOUR Event, any other professional golf competition or any elite amateur golf competition (including Olympic Golf) anywhere in the world ('Professional Golf Event'),' the tour's rules state.

The manual defines 'betting' as '(A) placing any money or other thing of value on the occurrence of an uncertain outcome with the expectation of return or (B) participating in any fantasy or other game that awards a prize of value, including any free-to-play, paid or daily fantasy game, unless expressly approved by the PGA TOUR.'

Penalties range from mandatory education to fines up to $500,000, suspension to lifetime bans.

Sports.title: Carabao Cup third round draw LIVE: Arsenal, Man Utd and Liverpool set to discover opponents
Sports.content:

Michael Schumacher plan teased by Ferrari before Italian Grand Prix

Ferrari are set to pay tribute to legendary former driver Michael Schumacher at the Italian Grand Prix

View 2 Images Michael Schumacher became a legend at Ferrari (Image: Getty)

Ferrari have hinted at a special tribute to iconic former Formula 1 driver Michael Schumacher at the team's home Italian Grand Prix. The German is considered one of F1's all-time greats having secured a record-equalling seven driver's world championships throughout his career.

‌



Schumacher is only rivalled by current Ferrari driver Lewis Hamilton, who surpassed his record for race victories in 2020. The F1 legend claimed five consecutive world titles for Ferrari from 2000 to 2004 and racked up 72 of his 91 race triumphs with the Scuderia, before announcing his first retirement straight after winning the 2006 Italian GP.

‌



Schumacher made his F1 comeback with Mercedes in 2010, before hanging up his helmet for good two years later. The 57-year-old sustained serious head injuries in a skiing accident in December 2013 and has not been spotted in public since.

‌

Lewis Hamilton's sarcastic Dutch GP radio remarks addressed by Ferrari boss READ MORE :

And Ferrari are apparently preparing to pay homage to Schumacher's contribution by running its SF-26 cars in a special livery honouring the German. Multiple clues have appeared on social media from the Italian outfit.

Next week's Grand Prix at Monza represents the 30th anniversary of Schumacher's maiden victory with Ferrari in 1996. It also arrives 20 years on from his final F1 triumph in 2006.

‌



The complete details regarding Schumacher's medical situation following his accident 13 years ago have been kept private by his family and updates concerning the German have been limited.

Former racing driver and close friend of Schumacher, Christian Danner, opened up about the ex-Ferrari legend during a recent interview with OLBG.

View 2 Images Michael Schumacher is one of F1's greatest-ever champions (Image: Getty)

‌



He said: "However Michael looks, or under whatever conditions he's alive - I don't know - I want to see him again.

"The fact that he's not appearing anywhere indicates that he's probably not very well. But Formula 1's prepared for that. Formula 1's prepared for everything.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua informed of crucial mistake made before Tyson Fury fight
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua informed of crucial mistake made before Tyson Fury fight

Anthony Joshua looks set to finally face long-time rival Tyson Fury later this year, but the Brit has been told he's making a huge mistake ahead of the contest

View Image Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua

Anthony Joshua has been slammed for linking up with Oleksandr Usyk's team just months before his proposed clash with Tyson Fury.

‌



While an official venue or date is yet to be confirmed for Joshua's mammoth meeting with Fury, the clash looks set to take place on November 20 at Madison Square Garden, New York - much to the disappointment of the UK faithful.

‌



For the last few months, Joshua has been getting fight-ready with the Ukrainian's camp. The pair famously fought twice in 2021 and 2022 - with Usyk winning both encounters. But they are now close friends - with Joshua joining his good friend's team ahead of his fight with Jake Paul back in December.

‌



The Brit would go on to secure a knockout victory in a rather dull and uninspiring encounter. 'AJ' returned to the ring last month - seven months after being involved in a tragic car crash. The 36-year-old survived two knockdowns before going on to topple Kristian Prenga in the second round.

Joshua once again had Usyk's long-time coaches in his corner, but the cornermen took some harsh criticism after the fight for the advice they gave their star man at the end of the opening stanza against Prenga.

‌



Former world champion Carl Froch believes some of the criticism Joshua's team received was justified. Speaking to NewBettingSites.uk, Froch said: "Team Usyk is probably the right team to get him fit and maybe get him in a good mental place. Are they the right team for the corner work after what I watched in that last clip? No, because there is a language problem.

"There is a communication barrier. Some of the stuff they were saying, I didn’t even understand what they meant by it. It was a bad attempt at a motivational speech."

"Should he have Rob in the corner? I think he should have always stayed with Rob McCracken in the corner. Rob McCracken is a man of principles. He is not a man motivated by money. He is motivated by boxing, loyalty, honesty and integrity, and he has got your back.

Sports.title: Ronnie O'Sullivan sets retirement date in clearest hint at quitting snooker yet
Sports.content:
Ronnie O'Sullivan sets retirement date in clearest hint at quitting snooker yet

Ronnie O'Sullivan has been out of form for several years and conversations with former greats has made it clear to him when he needs to retire from snooker

View 2 Images Ronnie O'Sullivan's potential retirement is looming

Ronnie O'Sullivan has suggested he'll retire from snooker in two years after taking advice from Steve Davis and Stephen Hendry - two of the sport's titans.

‌



O'Sullivan is arguably the greatest man ever to pick up a snooker cue but insists he's miles off the level he could once produce. He last won the World Championship back in 2022 and has only made the final of one tournament since 2024.

‌



'The Rocket' will turn 51 in December and has spoken to some of snooker's greats about the timing of their retirements. Perhaps tellingly, O'Sullivan has now revealed that both Hendry and Davis felt they played on for almost a decade longer than they should have.

‌



Both thought they could still produce the level of years gone by before subsequently accepting they should have walked away sooner - and O'Sullivan is adamant he won't repeat their mistakes.

He said: "I asked Stephen Hendry and Steve Davis, I spoke to them a couple of times and they said they probably played 10 years longer than they should have done. Because you always have this feeling, I want to play like I used to, because it’s a nice feeling.

‌



"I’m not going to waste 10 years. I’ve wasted three or four, in my opinion, three or four years where it’s been not great. I’ll give myself another year-and-a-half, to see if I can find something. If I can’t I think it’s good to draw a line under it and move on to other things that are more suitable to me."

He's currently competing at the Wuhan Open, where he is stunned to have won three games. Despite that he insists his run is destined to end in the last eight when he plays Mark Selby. So far he's got the better of Ashley Carty, Yao Pengcheng and Stephen Maguire but has ruled out any hope of victory.

View 2 Images O'Sullivan has been out of sorts for several years

Article continues below

"No. Absolutely no chance," he said when quizzed on his chances of glory. "I was happy to win a match. When I won two matches I was over the moon. To win three, for me, was a miracle at the moment. I’ve probably gone as far as I can go.

"If anybody plays well against me, they win, it doesn’t matter where they’re ranked. If they play poorly then I have a chance, but I don’t expect anyone from now to play poorly.

"My game is now very, very poor. I’m not playing to a good enough level. My technique is so rubbish I don’t have a clue where the balls are going, it’s like hit and hope snooker. I’m delighted to have won three matches, I can’t believe it really. I just hope for some improvement in the future. I’m playing more for the future, to hopefully find something."

Sports.title: Chelsea weigh up shock Emi Martinez transfer as Xabi Alonso stance becomes clear
Sports.content:
Chelsea weigh up shock Emi Martinez transfer as Xabi Alonso stance becomes clear

Chelsea could yet sign Emi Martinez with the Aston Villa goalkeeper offered to the Blues as he looks to find a way out of Villa Park following his failed Juventus move

View 2 Images Emi Martinez's days at Aston Villa look to be numbered (Image: Cerberus Sport/Shutterstock)

Chelsea could sign Emi Martinez in the final week of the transfer window with the Aston Villa goalkeeper offered to the Blues.

‌



Villa have already seen a host of last year's starting XI leave for pastures new and Martinez, who was tipped to leave for Manchester United last summer but stayed, is free to leave Villa Park in the coming days. Plans have already been made for his departure with Unai Emery's side agreeing to sign Zion Suzuki from Parma. Martinez had looked set to join Juventus before talks broke down, leaving him in limbo.

‌



Chelsea, now under Xabi Alonso's guidance, have yet to sign a new goalkeeper with last year's No 1 Robert Sanchez remaining as the club's first choice, despite his error count. He was held responsible for at least one of the goals the Blues conceded in their 3-2 win at Fulham on Monday.

‌



It has now emerged that Chelsea have been offered the World Cup winner's services with The Telegraph reporting that Alonso is prioritising the signing of a new first-choice goalkeeper.

Those mishaps could now prompt Chelsea to act, especially with a goalkeeper of Martinez's calibre on the market. The shotstopper has been among the Premier League's top goalkeepers and is also a World Cup winner.

‌



Sanchez conceded from Josh King, beaten at his near post after criticism of his positioning. He could also only palm out a Timothy Castagne strike which allowed Gonzalo Garcia to score from close range.

When asked if he and Sanchez had spoken about Monday night, Alonso said: "No, normal conversations. We have talked more about the team thing, about what we did well and what we have to do better. It was more about understanding the context. Every game is going to be important because we are in this process that we still need to develop things, we need to make adjustments that are more team-related."

Chelsea have already dealt with Villa this summer to secure the record signing of Morgan Rogers, who scored on debut earlier this week.

During their five previous Premier League triumphs, the most recent of which coming in 2017, the Blues have had world class goalkeepers in between the sticks in Petr Cech and Thibaut Courtois.

The Blues have already spent big this summer with Rogers and Maxence Lacroix the new signings who started at Craven Cottage on Monday. Pep Chavarria and Geovany Quenda appeared off the bench.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua fight at risk of falling apart as deadline set
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua fight at risk of falling apart as deadline set

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua have been tipped to fight later this year, but as of yet, an official date or venue has still yet to be confirmed

View Image Tyson Fury is due to fight Anthony Joshua (Image: Tyson Fury/Instagram)

Tyson Fury could move on from his fight with Anthony Joshua if an agreement has not been made by the end of next week.

‌



The pair came to verbal blows back in April after Fury's comeback win over Arslanbek Makhmudov. And while Joshua refused to enter the ring and face off with his long-time rival, both men signed to fight on the dotted line just days later.

‌



But they were both tasked with come through respective warm-up fights first. Last month, Fury forced Polish boxing veteran Mariusz Wach to quit on his stool in a behind-closed-doors fight in Thailand, while a day later, Joshua survived two knockdowns to stop Kristian Prenga.

‌



They are due to fight later this year, but a venue has yet to be set. Their contract is said to stipulate a stadium in the United Kingdom. However, it is believed there is a push for fight to take place at Madison Square Garden, New York. Broadcasters Netflix and the fight's Saudi backers are spearheading the change in location.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan

Semi-final: Wales vs Bosnia and Herzegovina

Final: Wales/Bosnia and Herzegovina vs Italy/Northern Ireland - Tuesday, 7.45pm kick-off

Play-off Path B:
