World.title: El PSOE busca una salida al choque entre Robles y Marlaska por los informes del CNI en Ceuta: “Las dos cosas pueden ser ciertas a la vez”
World.content:
El portavoz del PSOE en el Congreso, Patxi López, ha salido este miércoles en la Cámara baja a coser las versiones enfrentadas de Fernando Grande-Marlaska y Margarita Robles sobre los informes del Centro Nacional de Inteligencia (CNI) previos a la crisis de Ceuta. Donde las declaraciones de los ministros dibujan un choque entre Interior y Defensa, el PSOE trata de salvar la contradicción sosteniendo que ambas versiones pueden ser ciertas. “Las dos cosas pueden ser verdad a la vez”, ha defendido López ante las preguntas de los periodistas.

Según su explicación, el CNI pudo alertar de que se estaba produciendo un movimiento de personas —algo que ya circulaba por redes sociales— sin llegar a anticipar la magnitud de lo que finalmente ocurrió. “Probablemente el CNI avisa de que puede haber un paso de personas porque parece ser que era lo que se estaba moviendo en redes, pero puede ser que no se diese cuenta de la dimensión de lo que venía”, ha señalado. Y ha añadido que, de haber contado el Gobierno con información sobre el verdadero alcance de la crisis, “la previsión y los medios de la Guardia Civil y del propio Ejército hubiesen sido infinitamente mayores de los que se pusieron”.

Preguntado expresamente sobre si, con su explicación, estaba trasladando la responsabilidad al CNI, López ha rechazado esa lectura: “No le estoy echando la culpa a nadie”. “Quizá no se calibró la dimensión extraordinaria de lo que iba a ser”, ha matizado. Pese a los esfuerzos del portavoz del PSOE, la tensión había quedado expuesta el martes: mientras Robles defendía en el Congreso que Inteligencia había advertido de lo que podía suceder, Marlaska sostenía desde la sala de prensa del Consejo de Ministros que no hubo ningún informe que alertara de que algo de la magnitud de 80.000 personas cruzando de golpe la frontera pudiera ocurrir.

El cruce de versiones ha llevado a la portavoz del PP, Ester Muñoz, a hablar de una “guerra civil” dentro del Gobierno. Ahora López intenta coser esa grieta con una tercera explicación: el CNI pudo advertir del movimiento de personas, pero no de su dimensión. El portavoz socialista también ha aprovechado su rueda de prensa para lanzar un mensaje a Ceuta, donde la tensión sigue en aumento. “El Gobierno ha estado y va a estar todo el tiempo que sea necesario (...) y se hace cargo del estado de ánimo de los ceutíes”, ha asegurado.

Pero López ha querido matizar que el Gobierno “también se hace cargo del drama humanitario”. “No podemos olvidar que son casi 100 muertos los que ha habido y que todavía hay cientos de personas, muchos de ellos menores, que permanecen en las calles”, ha señalado. Desde esa doble perspectiva, ha defendido que la actuación del Ejecutivo se ha articulado en torno a dos “vectores imprescindibles”: “Uno es la legalidad y otro la humanidad”. El primero, ha explicado, era “frenar el flujo”. “Más de 70.000 personas entraron ilegalmente en Ceuta en 48 horas y el 95% de esas personas volvieron a cruzar esa frontera”, ha apuntado. El segundo, ha añadido, pasa por “atender esas situaciones y la asistencia humanitaria necesaria para las personas que permanecen en Ceuta”.

López ha insistido además en la necesidad de “recuperar la normalidad” en la ciudad autónoma. Para ello, ha defendido “repatriar a todos los que no tienen derecho a permanecer en nuestro país y acoger a aquellos que sí tienen derecho de asilo”. Un proceso que, ha advertido, llevará tiempo porque “es un proceso individual, no uno colectivo”.

Otro de los asuntos sobre los que ha sido preguntado el portavoz socialista ha sido el adelanto de la comparecencia de Pedro Sánchez en el Congreso. El presidente del Gobierno comparecerá finalmente el 3 de septiembre, tal y como ha decidido este miércoles la Junta de Portavoces, en lugar del día 9 que propuesto inicialmente por el Ejecutivo. El cambio de fecha llega después de que varios grupos parlamentarios presionaran para adelantar la comparecencia. López, sin embargo, ha esquivado cualquier confirmación sobre esa presión. Su respuesta ha sido breve: “No, simplemente había grupos que pensaban que había que adelantarla y se ha adelantado, sin más”, ha zanjado.

World.title: Las protestas toman las calles de Ceuta: “Vivimos en cuatro manzanas”
World.content:
Cada hora que pasa Ceuta eleva un poco más el enfado colectivo en el que vive desde hace 27 días. La indignación inicial ha dado paso a una ira que ha encontrado en las redes el perfecto altavoz, en el Gobierno el centro de ataques y en los migrantes el objetivo más fácil. Miles de ceutíes salieron el miércoles a la calle en una protesta masiva que comenzó frente a la Delegación del Gobierno de Ceuta al grito se “invasores expulsión” y “delegado, dimisión”. Ataviados con banderas de España y camisetas donde se lee “Ceuta no se vende, Ceuta se defiende”, se trata de una de las manifestaciones más multitudinarias desde la entrada hace 26 días de 80.000 emigrantes de los que entre 5.000 y 8.000 continúan en la cuidad autónoma.

La posibilidad de utilizar los polideportivos como centros de acogida, una medida anunciada en un Real Decreto a la que luego se dio marcha atrás, fue la gota que desbordó un vaso al límite. Por esta razón el ministro y mando único encargado de la normalización de la Ciudad Autónoma, Ángel Víctor Torres, insistió en su llamamiento a frenar cualquier incidente. “La violencia no conduce a nada. Esta situación saca lo mejor y peor de las personas”, insistió Torres. “La violencia no va a ningún lado y retrasa la normalización de la ciudad”, dijo tras reunirse con varios ministros.

Durante la protesta hubo momentos de mucha tensión cada vez que los manifestantes se cruzaban con alguien a quien consideraban uno de los marroquíes recién llegados y la policía tuvo que emplearse a fondo para frenar varios linchamientos.

“Se han apoderado de las playas, han hundido el comercio y han extendido el miedo en los barrios. Ahora dicen que tampoco podremos hacer deporte y aún no sabemos si podrá comenzar el curso escolar. No hay derecho a que se apropien de una ciudad de esta manera, vivimos en cuatro manzanas”, dice Jaime Barrios, funcionario destinado en Ceuta.

Raquel Gonzalo, de 39 años, cuenta que un grupo de inmigrantes intentó entrar en casa de sus padres, situada cerca de la playa de El Trampolín. “Lo hicieron por la terraza. Mi madre ha perdido seis kilos y mi padre tiene ataques de angustia. Yo no me atrevo a hacer deporte en la calle. Me da miedo. Se han apoderado de la ciudad y no tenemos seguridad”, dijo.

Si el martes hubo un ensayo de la protesta con unos cientos de personas en la calle, este miércoles la movilización fue masiva y recorrió amplias zonas de la ciudad. A la misma se sumaron los barrios más populares cansados de la situación. El presidente Pedro Sánchez, Gobierno y el actual Delegado del Gobierno fueron el centro de los ataques. Mientras tanto, los rumores se multiplicaron y durante todo el día corrían de teléfono en teléfono llamamientos para organizarse, organizar patrullajes nocturnos o dirigirse a las zonas de El Trampolín o de Loma Colmenar, donde se concentra la mayoría de migrantes añadiendo más tensión al ambiente.

La protesta masiva fue el remate a un día que comenzó con un minuto de silencio de todos los trabajadores que terminó con gritos de “viva Ceuta, viva España y viva el Rey” con el que los trabajadores públicos quieren llamar la atención sobre la situación en Ceuta.

Por el momento, la movilización más fuerte ha estado enfocada en boicotear cualquier lugar donde estuviera el recién nombrado mando único. Da igual que sea el hotel, un restaurante o la Delegación de Gobierno. Cada vez que el ministro se desplazaba, decenas de personas acudían frente a la puerta para insultarle.

La ira y la agresividad no se ha limitado a cualquier persona con chanclas y aspecto de marroquí que se cruzara con los manifestantes. La paranoia se extendió a cualquier persona que grabara un teléfono móvil. Un hombre se libró por poco de ser linchado cuando alguien lo acusó de ser espía marroquí tratando de grabar a la gente. El hombre se libró gracias a que se encerró en una panadería y solo salió cuando apareció la policía. La cólera se ha extendido a los medios de comunicación y fueron varios los episodios de violencia hacia algunos de los periodistas que cubrían la manifestación. En medio de este clima, este jueves el expresidente José María Aznar llegará a Ceuta.

World.title: Aznar viaja a Ceuta este jueves en plena crisis
World.content:
José María Aznar vuelve a Ceuta, más de dos décadas después de su última visita, en plena crisis por la entrada masiva de 80.000 inmigrantes por la frontera con Marruecos a finales de julio. El expresidente del Gobierno del PP solo visitó la ciudad autónoma durante su mandato en enero de 2000, dos años antes del conflicto de Perejil, en el Estrecho. Aznar vuelve a Ceuta este jueves, según han confirmado fuentes de FAES, en un momento en el que el Ejecutivo trata de atajar la crisis por los miles de migrantes que aún permanecen en territorio español y mientras mantiene una línea de apaciguamiento con Marruecos.

La visita de Aznar, inusual en el contexto de una crisis que todavía está abierta, supone un desafío a la estrategia del Gobierno de Pedro Sánchez, que ha apostado por la colaboración con el reino alauí, al que agradece el apoyo en el retorno de los migrantes. Tras el conflicto de Perejil, Aznar quedó identificado como un perfil de firmeza frente a Marruecos. Su viaje a Ceuta conecta ahora de forma inevitable aquella crisis con la actual.

En un comunicado hecho público el pasado 31 de julio, un día después de la entrada masiva, FAES defendió la presencia del Ejército en Ceuta para contener una “emergencia nacional” y denunció la “actitud claudicante del Gobierno español”. “Ceuta y Melilla”, denunciaba el texto, “han sido literalmente abandonadas”. La fundación que preside Aznar cargó también contra “la connivencia y la pasividad culpable de las autoridades marroquíes” en la entrada a nado de 80.000 migrantes.

Como presidente del Gobierno, Aznar vivió los momentos de mayor tensión con Marruecos desde la Marcha Verde, con la crisis de Perejil. El 11 de julio de 2002, un destacamento de gendarmes marroquíes desembarcó en el islote de Perejil, una pequeña roca deshabitada situada frente a la costa marroquí y muy cerca de Ceuta. Tras contactos diplomáticos infructuosos, el Gobierno de Aznar ordenó la Operación Romeo-Sierra, ejecutada el 17 de julio de 2002, por la que fuerzas especiales españolas desalojaron a los ocupantes marroquíes, que fueron detenidos y posteriormente entregados a Marruecos.

Aznar, en el documental Perejil que Movistar Plus+ estrenó el año pasado, revela que le dijo a su esposa Ana Botella que si aquella operación salía mal, dimitiría. Durante sus intervenciones en la serie, desvela también que el primer ministro marroquí no había sido informado de la toma del islote, ordenada directamente por el rey Mohamed VI; que el entonces presidente francés, Jacques Chirac, dio alas a la intervención marroquí y vetó un consenso a favor de España en la Unión Europea; y que su buena relación con el presidente George W. Bush, que le había visitado el año anterior en Madrid, decantó la mediación de Estados Unidos en favor de las tesis españolas. “Di la orden para enviar un mensaje claro”, remacha al término de la serie el exjefe de Gobierno conservador, “de que cuando se hacen estas cosas [violar el statu quo], España interviene”.

World.title: Meta pagará casi 18.000 millones de dólares para resolver las demandas por la adicción de los adolescentes a sus herramientas
World.content:
El acuerdo incluye un límite de tiempo de conexión a Facebook e Instagram de dos horas diarias para los menores, que tampoco podrán acceder a las plataformas durante la noche

Hasta 18.000 millones de dólares. Es la cifra que Meta ha acordado pagar como parte de un acuerdo para resolver las demandas presentadas por los fiscales que representan a estados de todo el país, en las que se alegaba que la empresa diseñó sus aplicaciones Facebook e Instagram para generar adicción en los niños, engañó a los consumidores sobre la seguridad de estas plataformas y recopiló indebidamente datos personales de menores que las utilizan.

El acuerdo, que aún debe ser aprobado por el tribunal, se alcanzó durante un juicio federal en Oakland (California) sobre las demandas presentadas por 29 Estados, con cuatro de ellos como abanderados, que ha acabado durando menos de una semana. Con el entendimiento se evitará uno de los litigios de mayor repercusión hasta la fecha en torno a las acusaciones de que las empresas de redes sociales perjudicaban a los usuarios jóvenes, y en el que se calculaba que las reclamaciones podrían alcanzar hasta 1,4 billones de dólares en daños y perjuicios, así como cambios drásticos en las plataformas del gigante tecnológico.

El pacto añade presión ahora a otros gigantes dueños de redes sociales que también estaban ya bajo escrutinio judicial y político, por cómo sus plataformas exponen a los menores a contenido o contactos inapropiados, e incluso hacen que desarrollen adicciones a la conexión a través de las pantallas. Los términos del acuerdo condicionan parte de la compensación que tendrá que pagar Meta —y la duración e intensidad de las medidas a las que se compromete para limitar el enganche de los menores— a que sus rivales TikTok y Alphabet (por ser dueña de YouTube) accedan a adoptarlas también y a pagar 5.300 millones de dólares en compensaciones.

En concreto, la compañía fundada por Mark Zuckerberg solo tendrá que pagar el 70% del total de la compensación acordada si logra que sus competidores también den el visto bueno a un límite de una hora diaria para los usuarios adolescentes y accedan a pagar a los Estados esos 5.300 millones de dólares. En caso de que TikTok y YouTube no accedan, Meta pagará también el otro 30% restante, otros 5.300 millones, del acuerdo.

“Anunciamos hoy un acuerdo con un grupo de 52 fiscales generales, de los dos partidos, en estados y territorios estadounidenses, incluido el Distrito de Columbia, para avanzar en nuestros constantes esfuerzos por apoyar a los adolescentes y empoderar a los padres”, ha declarado Meta en un comunicado.

Cambios en los controles de uso

Como parte del acuerdo, Meta pondrá en marcha una serie de cambios en los controles de uso, que incluirán un límite automático al tiempo que puedan estar conectados sus usuarios adolescentes: dos horas diarias, que solo se podrán ampliar si los padres dan un permiso expreso. Ese plazo se reducirá a una hora si esos rivales de Meta, TikTok y Alphabet, acceden a aplicar también esa restricción. Los menores tampoco podrán acceder a las plataformas entre la medianoche y las seis de la mañana, a menos que, igualmente, sus padres consientan. Del mismo modo, no podrán recibir notificaciones en horario escolar, entre las ocho de la mañana y las tres de la tarde.

La compañía también bloqueará el acceso de los niños al número de “me gusta” o a las reacciones a las publicaciones, reforzará sus medidas para impedir que puedan ver contenido inapropiado y pondrá más herramientas a disposición de los padres y responsables de los menores. Mientras estén conectados, los niños recibirán avisos periódicos sobre el tiempo que llevan en la plataforma.

“El hecho es que los adolescentes se mueven fluidamente entre docenas de aplicaciones cada día. Todas las plataformas deberían empoderar a los padres y apoyar a los menores aplicando las mismas medidas, porque sabemos que cuando se imponen restricciones a los adolescentes en una aplicación, simplemente se cambian a otra”, apunta Meta en su comunicado sobre el acuerdo. “Para que puedan producirse avances de verdad, instamos a TikTok y a YouTube a unirse a nosotros y a los fiscales generales para adoptar estos nuevos estándares, para garantizar que los menores usan las redes sociales de manera sana y responsable”.

El consejero delegado de Meta, Mark Zuckerberg Tom Williams (CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)

La mayor parte de las restricciones estarán en vigor durante una década. Las más estrictas —el límite diario y el bloqueo nocturno— tendrán inicialmente una vigencia de cinco años. Si las compañías rivales también las adoptan, el límite diario quedará establecido en una sola hora, y el toque de queda será más amplio: de las diez de la noche a las siete de la mañana.

El pago de la compensación se distribuirá a lo largo de una década, en desembolsos anuales a 48 Estados y cuatro jurisdicciones: el distrito de Columbia, Puerto Rico, la Samoa estadounidense y las islas Marianas del Norte. Nuevo México, que había presentado su propia demanda contra el gigante tecnológico, y Florida no están incluidas en el acuerdo.

Meta calcula que el gasto legal del acuerdo le supondrá cerca de 10.000 millones de dólares en el tercer trimestre del año.

Los estados acusan a Meta de infringir la Ley federal de Protección de la Privacidad Infantil en Internet, que prohíbe la recopilación de datos de menores sin el consentimiento de sus padres. También la acusan de engañar a los consumidores al promocionar la seguridad de sus plataformas, a pesar de que al mismo tiempo sus directivos eran conscientes de los riesgos que suponía la plataforma para los jóvenes, riesgos que habían debatido y estudiado internamente. En consecuencia, desarrollaron productos adictivos, que han llevado a algunos jóvenes a tener problemas de salud mental, como ansiedad y depresión, y que en algunos casos hasta han llevado al suicidio.

En su comunicado, Meta ha declarado sobre el acuerdo: “Garantizar que los adolescentes disfrutan de una experiencia segura y productiva en nuestras plataformas es un imperativo absoluto para nosotros. Queremos hacer lo correcto para los padres y los adolescentes, y por ello colaboramos con los fiscales generales de los Estados para establecer nuevos estándares en el sector”.

Con el acuerdo, Meta evita lo que hubiera podido ser un largo y carísimo juicio y el posible pago de una compensación mucho mayor. Con el fin del proceso en el tribunal que presidía Yvonne González Rogers, tampoco tendrán que declarar los altos ejecutivos de la tecnológica, encabezados por el propio Zuckerberg.

Este martes había llegado a comparecer el director general de Instagram, Adam Mosseri. El ejecutivo defendió que las medidas de protección de los usuarios menores de edad aplicadas por su plataforma han mejorado con el tiempo, aunque reconoció que su efecto ha sido limitado. “No existen soluciones mágicas para problemas como este”, dijo.

También declaró Francesco Fogu, director de diseño de producto de Instagram. Fogu admitió que las medidas que había puesto en marcha esa plataforma —como el modo noche o la función Tomarse un descanso, que envía avisos visuales para que pares de usar la aplicación cuando llevas 10, 20 o 30 minutos de navegación—, son opcionales y el usuario elige si las activa o no, pese a que la compañía sabía que si hubieran sido automáticas serían mucho más efectivas.

Fogu también reconoció que, en caso de haberlas implantado por defecto, posiblemente el número de usuarios de la plataforma habría caído.

World.title: El jefe de Instagram asegura en el juicio a Meta que no existen “soluciones mágicas” para proteger a los menores
World.content:
Adam Mosseri es el primer alto ejecutivo de la tecnológica en declarar en la causa por la demanda de 29 estados de EE UU contra la compañía

El director general de Instagram, Adam Mosseri, defendió este martes ante un tribunal de California que las medidas de protección de los usuarios menores de edad implementadas por su plataforma han mejorado con el tiempo, aunque reconoció que su efecto ha sido limitado. La suya fue la primera declaración de un alto cargo de Meta, la empresa matriz de Facebook o Instagram, en el proceso abierto por la demanda de 29 estados de EE UU contra la compañía que dirige Mark Zuckerberg, que también deberá testificar estos días.

Mosseri reconoció que, aunque Instagram ha reforzado la protección a los menores con medidas de control parental o restricciones que limitan temporalmente el uso de la aplicación por parte de los adolescentes, no ha cambiado demasiado la frecuencia de uso de la plataforma por parte de los menores ni cuánto tiempo pasan en ella. “No existen soluciones mágicas para problemas como este”, dijo.

Los estados acusan a Meta de infringir la Ley federal de Protección de la Privacidad Infantil en Internet, que prohíbe la recopilación de datos de menores sin el consentimiento de sus padres. También la acusan de engañar a los consumidores al promocionar la seguridad de sus plataformas, a pesar de que al mismo tiempo sus directivos eran conscientes de los riesgos que suponía la plataforma para los jóvenes, riesgos que habían debatido y estudiado internamente. En consecuencia, desarrollaron productos adictivos, que han llevado a algunos jóvenes a tener problemas de salud mental, como ansiedad y depresión, y que en algunos casos hasta han llevado al suicidio.

El abogado de la acusación presentó ayer un documento interno de Meta en el que se decía que las herramientas de seguridad para adolescentes de la empresa no resultan “eficaces para reducir determinados comportamientos”. Preguntado sobre si eso le sorprendía, Mosseri respondió que no.

Además de Mosseri, que está citado en el juzgado otra vez este miércoles, también declaró Francesco Fogu, director de diseño de producto de Instagram. Fogu admitió que las medidas implementadas por Instagram, como el modo noche o la función Tomarse un descanso, que manda avisos visuales para que pares de usar la aplicación cuando llevas 10, 20 o 30 minutos de navegación, se implantaron como opcionales (es decir, el usuario elige si las activa o no), pese a que la compañía sabía que hubieran sido mucho más efectivas si fueran automáticas. También reconoció que, de haberlas implantado por defecto, posiblemente hubiera caído el número de usuarios.

Si Meta es declarada culpable, deberá pagar compensaciones por valor de 200.000 millones de dólares (unos 171.000 millones de euros) e introducir cambios en el diseño de sus aplicaciones para hacerlas más seguras de cara a los menores. De ahí que muchos analistas consideren que este juicio es clave para el futuro de las redes sociales: si Meta se ve obligada a cambiar sus productos, eso tendría un efecto arrastre en el resto de plataformas.

La batalla legal contra las redes

El caso que se está juzgando estos días en Oakland forma parte de la cascada de demandas interpuestas por familias, instituciones educativas y fiscales generales de varios estados en las que sostienen que las plataformas de Meta pueden causar una adicción en los menores similar a la de las máquinas tragaperras o el tabaco.

Meta, por su parte, ha negado que haya evidencia científica que confirme que sus plataformas causan adicción. También se acoge a una normativa federal que protege a las empresas de cualquier responsabilidad sobre los contenidos que cuelguen en redes los usuarios.

A principios de mes, un tribunal de Nuevo México impuso a la compañía una multa de 567 millones de dólares, que se dedicarán a financiar instituciones que velan por la salud mental de los menores. Esa resolución, que Meta anunció que iba a recurrir, exige también por primera vez cambios concretos a una tecnológica, y argumenta que, igual que sucede con las empresas que contaminan, cuyas externalidades negativas no perjudican a una serie de individuos, sino a toda la sociedad, las plataformas deben hacerse cargo de los daños que ocasionan a la ciudadanía, no solo a los usuarios de las redes.

World.title: Real Madrid - Real Sociedad en directo | Vinicius marca el tercero y encarrila el encuentro para el Madrid
World.content:
Kylian Mbappé celebra tras anotar su segundo tanto contra la Real Sociedad.

Mbappé marcó un doblete para poner en dos ocasiones a los blancos por delante, que vieron empatado el partido antes del descanso con un gol de Sucic

El Real Madrid está ganando a la Real Sociedad este miércoles en la jornada 1 de la Liga, atrasada por la disputa del Mundial. Empezó el partido con la posesión para la Real Sociedad, aunque sin apenas peligro. El Madrid dio un paso adelante y encadenó posesiones largas con buena movilidad de balón que pusieron en aprietos a los de Matarazzo, que sobrevivieron y volvieron a tener la pelota. Se empezaban a escuchar algunos tímidos pitos en la grada y entonces llegó el gol de Mbappé. Condujo Valverde desde el centro del campo y cuando se vio encimado soltó el balón con un pase para el francés, que se orientó la pelota para su pierna izquierda en el área y sacó un disparo a la escuadra imposible para Remiro. Parecía que moría el primer tiempo con el Madrid por delante, pero llegó Sucic para devolver el runrún al Bernabéu. En un pase largo para Ochieng a la espalda de la defensa, el futbolista keniano disparó contra las piernas de Konaté y el rechace le cayó al futbolista croata que, sin marca, remató cruzado para marcar el gol del empate.

World.title: MPs want to scrap far-right TV show over “Hitler was right” item
World.content:
TV broadcaster Ongehoord Nederland (ON!) is facing fresh calls to have its licence revoked in the wake of an online panel show that presented Nazi leader Adolf Hitler as an anti-globalist crusader.

The segment, Let’s Twist Again, featured a clip of Hitler delivering a tirade against a “rootless international clique”, prompting one person in the crowd to shout out: “Jews!”

Presenter Arlette Adriani then asked the two panellists, Joost Niemöller and Raisa Blommestijn, to comment on the statement: “The cosmopolitan elite is compelled to take an essentially hostile position towards the ordinary indigenous people”. Both said they agreed.

MPs from the coalition parties CDA and D66, as well as the left-wing opposition party Pro, tabled questions in parliament asking culture minister Rianne Letschert if ON! should be taken off the air.

The public broadcasting ombudsman Margo Smit said she had received around 20 complaints about the item since it was put online on July 31, most of them in the last week.

“This fragment is proof that this broadcaster is deliberately flouting basic standards,” Pro MP Mohammed Mohandis told RTL.

“Nazi propaganda”

Oufa Oualhadj, for D66, said: “This thinking is bound up with Nazi propaganda and the depiction of people such as Jews as the enemy by presenting them as a rootless international force that supposedly undermines national communities.”

ON!’s director-general Peter Vlemmix said Niemöller and Blommestijn had made it clear during the broadcast that they felt “nothing but disgust for Hitler’s regime and the barbaric consequences of it”.

But he admitted that the channel had “not paid enough attention to the sensitivities around this subject”. “We should have approached them more carefully in this video.”

ON! has faced repeated calls to have its licence withdrawn since it started broadcasting in 2022. It has been fined for broadcasting misleading information and was found to have used discriminatory language when it advertised the post of editor-in-chief with the words: “man or woman, no X”.

Blommestijn received a criminal conviction for discrimination for a social media post in which she used the term “negroid primates” to describe a group of black men who were filmed assaulting a white man.

“Complex” position

Last month a majority of MPs from all three coalition parties and Pro called on Letschert not to renew the broadcaster’s licence next year.

Erik van der Maas, of right-wing liberal party VVD, said: “There is no place in the public network for a broadcaster that is funded by taxpayers’ money but systematically breaks the rules and is not prepared to keep to them.”

But the minister said the legal position was “complex” because the public broadcasting service NPO had not asked her to withdraw ON!’s licence. “That does not take away the concerns about Omroep Nederland,” she said.

The channel’s future is due to form part of a debate in parliament on September 24.

World.title: Hundreds evacuated in Apeldoorn after suspected drugs lab found
World.content:
Around 220 people were evacuated from three apartment blocks in Apeldoorn on Wednesday morning after police found a suspected drugs lab in one of the buildings overnight.

Residents of about 100 homes on the Eburonenstraat were ordered out at around 10am. Officers were alerted after someone reportedly threw fireworks from a balcony, and went on to find weapons and what they believe was a drugs lab inside one of the flats.

One resident has been arrested and is being questioned.

Specialist units are on the scene, including the national dismantling service (LFO), which is called in when chemicals pose a risk to the surrounding area, and a police explosives-safety officer.

Police said they could not yet tell whether there was any danger of an explosion, and the area around the building has been sealed off. A few officers reported feeling unwell from chemical fumes and were checked by ambulance crews, but none needed hospital treatment.

Residents of the two outer blocks were allowed home in the early afternoon. Those in the middle block, where the find was made, are still waiting to return.

The evacuation comes as Dutch police warn that drug producers are increasingly setting up labs in residential areas, bringing the dangers of volatile chemicals into densely populated buildings.

World.title: Dutch tourist believed missing after flooding in Nepal kills 31
World.content:

A Dutch national has been reported missing after severe flooding left on the border between Nepal and Tibet at least 31 people dead and nearly 400 unaccounted for.

The Nepalese tourism authority said a total of 384 visitors were missing in the region, including 291 foreigners. More than 90 people were injured when flash floods engulfed whole villages along the Bhote Khoshi, Trishuli and Narayani rivers.

The Dutch tourist was one of two non-Nepalis, along with an Australian, in a party of 17 travelling with a Kathmandu-based tour operator. Around one-quarter of those unaccounted for are from India.

Nepal’s foreign minister said the floods were triggered by a combination of an earthquake in Tibet and high water in the Bhote Khoshi river, which had been swelled by melting snow.

Bhotekoshi Flash Flood

SITUATION UPDATE -2

Date: August 26, 2026 Preliminary Details of Missing Tourists pic.twitter.com/gxWJfVfKuX — Nepal Tourism Board (@nepaltourismb) August 26, 2026

The earthquake, measuring 4.4 on the Richter scale, caused an avalanche and a heavy mudslide that poured into the river.

Surveillance footage from the Gyirong County border crossing showed buildings around the checkpoint being submerged by mud and water. Around 4,000 people live in the region, which is a trading hub and a popular base for hikers.

Chinese president Xi Jinping has ordered search and rescue workers to conduct “all-out” efforts to find the missing visitors after state media outlet CCTV reported “major casualties” in the region.

The Dutch foreign affairs ministry said it was monitoring the situation closely. “We are ready to offer consular help if it is necessary,” a spokesman said.

Dutch citizens in the area have been urged to contact their friends and family or call the government’s emergency number on +31 247 247 247.

World.title: Utrecht death shows West Nile virus is circulating in NL
World.content:
A person in Utrecht province has died in hospital after catching West Nile virus in the Netherlands, the public health institute RIVM has said.

The fact it was caught in the Netherlands means the virus is now circulating in the local mosquito population. It is one of three such infections RIVM has recorded so far in 2026, the others infected are still in hospital.

RIVM said it would not release details about the person who died out of respect for the family. A spokesperson described them as elderly and in poor health. The death is not connected to last week’s case in a Utrecht blood donor, the first human infection caught in the Netherlands since 2020.

This year the virus has been detected in Utrecht, Noord-Brabant and Zuid-Holland – in horses, mosquitoes and birds – and RIVM has asked doctors across the country to watch for patients with symptoms of West Nile fever.

Not the start of a pandemic

A single death, even a local one, does not signal a pandemic in the making, because West Nile virus is not the type to cause one. It does not pass from person to person.

People and horses can fall seriously ill, but they are dead ends for the virus: they do not carry enough of it in their blood to reinfect a biting mosquito, so the chain stops with them.

The death does however mark the establishment of the virus in northern Europe, which scientists are linking to warmer weather. It first reached people in the Netherlands in 2020, in a small cluster around Utrecht and Arnhem.

Who is at risk

Most infections go unnoticed, and around 80% of people who catch the virus have no symptoms at all and roughly 19% develop flu-like illness. About 1% go on to serious neurological problems such as inflammation of the brain, and a small number of those die.

Mosquitoes carrying the virus are most active at dusk. In the affected provinces, covering up in the evening lowers the chance of being bitten – though RIVM stresses the odds of catching the virus in the Netherlands, let alone falling ill from it, remain very low.

Separately, the regional public health service GGD Drenthe reported last week that a woman had probably died of West Nile fever after catching it on holiday in south-eastern Europe. That was an imported case, unlike the Utrecht death.

World.title: Cabinet and mayors agree to prosecute motorway protesters
World.content:
Anyone who blocks a motorway or railway line will in principle face criminal prosecution, the country’s regional mayors, prosecutors and police chief have agreed with justice minister David van Weel.

The joint statement, issued on Tuesday, says the rules apply to everyone “from farmers to climate activists”, though local authorities can still make exceptions case by case.

“Demonstrating is a fundamental right and we protect it,” it reads. “But expressing your opinion is something other than making the motorway or the railway unsafe.”

The move follows a fatal crash during recent farmers’ protests. Two people died and six were injured when a car ran into the back of a tractor-related tailback on the A59 earlier this month.

Nijmegen mayor Hubert Bruls, who chairs the regional mayors and had asked for national rules, said nothing had changed legally – tractors were already banned from motorways – but the confusion had now been removed.

Climate group Extinction Rebellion said it had no intention of stopping. “As long as the government and big business fail to do what is needed, we will continue with peaceful civil disobedience,” the group said, adding that it is already facing prosecution, with a court case due on August 26.

XR, which has blocked the A12 in The Hague dozens of times, said the measure was a distraction. Its activists have been treated far more harshly than farmers over the summer: around 270 were arrested on the A12 last month, while some 80 farmers escaped fines on the A35 because their number plates were taped over.

World.title: Worst drought in 700 years turns wetland into graveyard for fish
World.content:
The summer drought has dried up the Zeezuiper, a wetland reserve in Noord-Brabant, for the first time in 700 years, leaving behind hundreds of dead fish.

Forest ranger Erik de Jonge was shocked when he returned from holiday to find the area, usually teeming with geese and wetland birds, had become a barren scrubland, with just a few scattered puddles remaining.

“We’ve seen a lot of droughts here in the last 10 years, but this beats everything,” De Jonge told Omroep Brabant. “This hasn’t happened since 1300.”

Stepping over a pile of dead and rotting fish, he explained: “We can see the fish retreated to the deepest water, but they died because even here the water has disappeared. There are deer running around. It’s unprecedented.”

The leaves have started to fall early because woodland trees such as birch, beech and maple are suffering from heat stress, De Jonge explained. “It looks like autumn, with all the fresh leaves, but it’s the old beeches reacting to the drought.”

Between 60% and 80% of the surrounding heathland is dried up, while the usually abundant berries are sparse and shrivelled.

Migrating birds

That will have an impact on migrating birds that pass through in autumn, De Jonge said. “These are vitamins for the birds that are coming in the next few weeks. Usually they can expect a buffet, but the buffet has dried up.”

Wetlands also play an important role in absorbing CO2 from the surrounding area. “A swamp captures more CO2 than a forest, so this will have negative consequences for the climate,” he said.

Water levels in the Zeezuiper have been falling steadily since the 1970s, but the trend has accelerated in recent years. De Jonge is urging authorities such as the water board to take steps to ensure the area retains as much water as possible when the rain finally returns.

“We’ve been calling for this for years, but we can’t ignore it any longer,” he said.

World.title: Netherlands to miss gas target: What it means for households
World.content:
The Netherlands will miss its target for filling its gas reserves before this winter, national gas network operator Gasunie has confirmed.

The shortfall, first reported by NU.nl, would not leave homes cold in a normal winter, Gasunie said, but it does make the country more vulnerable to an exceptionally cold spell or a sudden disruption in supply.

Dutch underground storage sites were about 45% full in late August, compared with roughly 94% at the same point in 2023 and 63% a year ago.

The government’s target, set on Gasunie’s advice, was to fill the reserves to about 80% of capacity by November 1. Levels are currently stuck near 45%, and the minimum EU target is 74%.

Is there enough gas?

For an ordinary winter, Gasunie says supply is secure. Gas continues to arrive through pipelines from Norway, through terminals for liquefied natural gas (LNG), and from small Dutch fields.

The concern is what happens when several things go wrong at once: a long cold spell that also drives up demand in neighbouring countries, for example, alongside a fault at a pipeline or an LNG terminal.

“Under normal conditions I am not extremely worried about the amount of gas in storage,” energy expert René Peters of research institute TNO told broadcaster NOS. “The risk lies mainly in situations where several problems occur at the same time.”

Why are reserves low?

The main reason the reserves are low is that commercial energy firms have stored almost no gas. Summer gas prices have been higher than the expected winter price, so storing gas now to sell later does not pay off. Traders have linked the higher gas prices partly to the war around Iran.

To make up the gap, the state has stepped in. State energy company EBN is storing gas on the government’s instruction in Bergermeer, Norg and Grijpskerk, and says it is on schedule to reach its 80 TWh ceiling. Gasunie warned in June that filling was going too slowly.

The cost to households

For most households the effect will be on price rather than supply. Refilling reserves with expensive summer gas feeds through into energy costs, and households on variable or dynamic contracts tend to feel that first, which is worth bearing in mind when choosing an energy contract.

Gasunie has urged the government to create a strategic gas reserve for emergencies. One option being discussed is keeping part of the Groningen gas field – shut down in 2024 after extraction triggered hundreds of earthquakes – available purely as an emergency supply, a politically contentious idea in a region still dealing with the damage.

The cabinet is due to update parliament on the reserves, and on possible further steps, in September.

World.title: Mondriaan painting set to fetch €30m at auction later this year
World.content:
A painting by the Dutch artist Piet Mondriaan is expected to sell for more than €30 million when it goes under the hammer later this year.

The work, Composition III, dates from 1920, the year Mondriaan returned to Paris to develop his distinctive abstract style of Neo-Plasticism.

The painting, which has been in a private collection for the last 25 years, is expected to fetch the highest price this autumn when London auction house Christie’s puts it up for sale on October 14.

“It is a very rare work from the year that you really see Mondriaan finding his feet and developing his neoplastic theory as an artist,” Keith Gill, head of impressionist and modern art at Christie’s said.

Mondriaan finished just eight paintings in 1920, five of which are owned by major museums such as the Stedelijk Museum in Amsterdam, the Tate in London and the Museum of Modern Art in New York.

Christie’s estimates it will sell for between £20 mln and £20 mln (€23 mln-€35 mln), but Gill said that could prove to be a conservative estimate.

“Given the importance of this masterpiece and the outstanding condition it is in, it could easily fetch more,” he told the Telegraaf.

The record price for a Mondriaan was set in November 1922, when Composition no. II sold for $51 million (€49.4 mln) at Sotheby’s in New York.

The United States has donated $2.1 million worth of equipment for border protection, including drones and thermal imaging cameras, to Poland under an agreement signed on Tuesday. The Polish border guard says that the package is part of a wider US programme, worth an estimated €12 million, to support Poland and the Baltic states in response to the migration crisis engineered by Russia’s ally Belarus on their borders. Stronger border security strengthens our shared security. Today in Warsaw, the United States and Poland marked the donation of more than $2 million in U.S.-funded equipment to the Polish Border Guard @Straz_Graniczna . The donation, funded by the State Department’s @StateINL and… pic.twitter.com/8Mh1eHLo0t — US Embassy Warsaw (@USEmbassyWarsaw) August 25, 2026 “Stronger border security strengthens our shared security,” declared the US embassy in Warsaw, announcing the donation of equipment, which includes 45 drones and nine advanced thermal imaging cameras. “This is just the next step in our security partnership,” they added. “Additional equipment, training, and expertise will follow.” The Polish border guard also confirmed that the support includes training packages and bilateral study visits, as well as the delivery of 15 snowmobiles to Poland next year. On Tuesday, it also hosted a delegation of senior figures from the US Border Patrol and US Customs and Border Protection for talks on “exchanging experiences, strengthening cooperation, and implementing advanced technologies in response to migratory pressures”. Since 2021, Belarus has been encouraging and assisting migrants – mainly from Africa and Asia – to attempt to irregularly cross into the European Union over its borders with Poland, Lithuania and Latvia. Tens of thousands of attempted crossings have been reported each year. In response, Poland has strengthened physical and electronic barriers along the border with Belarus. It has also eased rules on the use of firearms by uniformed officers to protect the border, and has temporarily banned asylum applications by people who irregularly cross from Belarus. As a result of such efforts, attempted illegal crossings are down 98% so far this year, while Poland also claims to have a 100% success rate in apprehending migrants who do manage to cross. The number of attempted illegal crossings by migrants from Belarus to Poland fell from 15,500 in the first half of 2025 to 235 this year – a drop of over 98% Poland also now claims a 100% success rate in apprehending migrants who manage to cross illegally https://t.co/RFZkd7CeIk — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 20, 2026 After meeting with American officials on Tuesday, the Polish border guard said that the head of the US delegation, Jason E. Schneider, acting chief patrol agent for the US Border Patrol’s Rio Grande Valley sector, had praised Poland as a “model and benchmark” for dealing with migratory pressures. It also noted that Stephanie Holmes, the deputy chief of mission at the US embassy, had noted Poland’s role “protecting the entire eastern flank of NATO and [acting] as a guarantor of transatlantic security”. Belarus is a close ally of Russia, and the migration crisis engineered by Minsk on the EU and NATO’s eastern flank is seen as one element of the so-called “hybrid warfare” being waged by Moscow against the West. 🤝 Polska i USA wspólnie dbają o bezpieczne granice i stabilność całego regionu! 🇵🇱🇺🇸 W Warszawie odbyło się spotkanie kierownictwa polskich i amerykańskich służb, w tym U.S. Border Patrol. Wydarzeniu towarzyszyło podpisanie umowy z Departamentem Stanu USA, dzięki której na… pic.twitter.com/rN9umTfPfU — Straż Graniczna (@Straz_Graniczna) August 25, 2026 The Polish border guard reported that, as well as donating equipment, the US has since 2024 been providing and funding “advanced tactical and technical training”, including “courses in border protection tactics”, for Polish officers. Next month, they will provide training in operating the newly donated drones, which are being provided as part of a broader $12 million US programme to support Poland and the Baltic states in “direct response…to the situation on the Belarusian border”, said the Polish border guard. In January this year, Polish officials also conducted study visits to El Paso and Detroit in the United States to “learn about methods used for counteracting illegal migration on the US borders with Mexico and Canada”. A further visit to the southern US border is scheduled for November. Poland says that “specialists from the Middle East” have been brought to Belarus to dig tunnels under the border for migrants to cross into Poland. Four such tunnels have been discovered this year, including one last week that was used by 180 migrants https://t.co/4ConkQnj8z — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 16, 2025 In 2024, the EU itself announced that it would allocate €170 million to help member states neighbouring Russia and Belarus “counter hybrid threats from the weaponisation of migration”, which it said was being used “as a political tool to destabilise EU society”. Poland was allocated the largest share of the fund, with €52 million. Last year, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen visited Poland’s border with Belarus, where she thanked Warsaw for defending Europe from “cynical hybrid attacks” being orchestrated by Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom she called a “predator”. Prosecutors are investigating possible criminal offences relating to financing by Zondacrypto, a cryptocurrency firm that collapsed earlier this year, of organisations and individuals linked to Poland’s right-wing opposition. Among those named in an announcement by prosecutor general Waldemar Żurek, who also serves as justice minister, are Zbigniew Ziobro, a deputy leader of Law and Justice (PiS), the main opposition party, and the Polish edition of CPAC, an American conservative political conference. Meanwhile, a lawyer representing Przemysław Kral, who was Zondacrypto’s head when it collapsed, has revealed that his client is cooperating with prosecutors. That lawyer, Roman Giertych, is also a prominent politician in Poland’s main ruling party, Civic Coalition (KO). Mamy przełom w śledztwie dotyczącym ZondaCrypto. Połączyliśmy w jedno wielowątkowe postępowanie sprawy oszukanych inwestorów oraz sprawę zaginięcia S. Suszka, prześwietlając nielegalne strumienie finansowe płynące w stronę polityków i powiązanych z nimi podmiotów. Więcej w… — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) August 25, 2026 Zondacrypto came under scrutiny in April after customers began reporting being unable to access their funds. By late July, prosecutors had received several thousand notifications of suspected criminal activity connected with the exchange. Potential losses have been estimated at at least 350 million zloty (€81.4 million). In a statement published on Tuesday, Żurek said investigators had secured extensive evidence, questioned numerous witnesses, and carried out proceedings involving suspects who have already been formally charged, though he declined to identify them or disclose the charges. However, he added that there had now been a “breakthrough in the investigation”, including “looking into illegal financial flows towards politicians and entities associated with them”. Polish prosecutors have so far identified hundreds of possible victims and potential losses of at least 350m zloty relating to troubled crypto exchange Zondacrypto. The firm's oversight board resigned last week and many users say they cannot access funds https://t.co/ib4bGhzg2m — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 21, 2026 Żurek revealed that, “based on the evidence secured in the case, the prosecutor’s office is verifying information…regarding the possibility of crimes being committed in connection with the financing by Zondacrypto of” individuals and entities associated with the right-wing opposition. They included the foundations of Ziobro and Przemysław Wipler, a former PiS politician now associated with Confederation (Konfederacja), a far-right group; conservative broadcaster Republika and its head, Tomasz Sakiewicz; the CPAC conference; and Radosław Piesiewicz, head of the Polish Olympic Committee. CPAC and the Olympic committee were previously sponsored by Zondacrypto, while Republika sold extensive advertising space to the crypto firm. Żurek also said they were investigating potential financing by Zondacrypto of actions taken by individuals who helped fugitive former PiS deputy justice minister Marcin Romanowski. Both Ziobro, who served as justice minister when PiS was in power, and Romanowski are currently on the run from criminal charges in a separate case. They were initially given asylum by Hungary, then in May Ziobro fled to the United States. Romanowski’s current location is not confirmed, but he is believed to be in Transnistria, the pro-Russian breakaway region of Moldova. Prime Minister @donaldtusk says that, based on intelligence sources, Poland is now “99% certain” that fugitive opposition politician Marcin Romanowski is in Transnistria, a breakaway region of Moldova that has close links to Russia https://t.co/mdvmJpkFf7 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 18, 2026 Meanwhile, on Tuesday, Giertych confirmed that he was the defence counsel for Kral, who reportedly fled Poland after reports of wrongdoing at Zondacrytpo began to emerge. In an interview with state broadcaster TVP, Giertych said that his client is “cooperating with the justice system as best he can” and that his “motive is to mitigate his sentence”. Giertych is himself an MP for KO, the centrist party led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk. Giertych has previously acted as a lawyer for Tusk as well as members of his family. Kral had previously been represented by Bartosz Lewandowski, a lawyer who represents Ziobro and Romanowski. Giertych told TVP that he had been representing Kral pro bono since May. “I made a commitment to my voters that I would hold PiS to account,” he said. “Drawing people out from that side is the most effective way of holding them to account.” 🗣️ "Ta afera ujawni, czym było PiS. Ziobro accused the current authorities of being too lenient towards Kral because he had “become politically useful”. “This is the desperation of a regime fighting for its own future impunity…This is being done even at the expense of the victims and the recovery of their money,” Ziobro said. During a speech in parliament in April, Prime Minister Donald Tusk alleged that the company’s financial success was “rooted not only in Russian money linked to…one of Russia’s most powerful mafia groups, but also to the Russian security services”. Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun has been charged with denying Nazi crimes, a criminal offence in Poland that carries a prison sentence of up to three years. The charges relate to statements last year in which Braun, who has a long history of promoting antisemitic conspiracy theories, suggested that the gas chambers at Auschwitz, which was the Nazis’ main killing centre during the Holocaust, are “fake”. Komunikat o przedstawieniu posłowi do Parlamentu Europejskiego zarzutów publicznego i wbrew faktom zaprzeczania zbrodniom ludobójstwa popełnionym w niemieckim nazistowskim obozie koncentracyjnym i zagłady KL Auschwitz-Birkenau w Oświęcimiu. https://t.co/nLq3XKnXCK — IPN Kraków (@ipn_krakow) August 25, 2026 On Tuesday morning, Braun was summoned to appear as a suspect at the Kraków branch of the Institute of National Remembrance (IPN), a state historical body that has the power to prosecute crimes relating to the periods when Poland was under Nazi and communist rule. A group of his followers gathered outside the building to express their support for Braun, who finished fourth in last year’s presidential elections. Since then, his Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP) party has risen to around 9% in polls, making it a potential kingmaker after next year’s parliamentary elections. After meeting with Braun, IPN prosecutor Robert Janicki announced that they had presented him with charges for “publicly and contrary to the facts denying the crimes of genocide committed by officers of the Third Reich in the German concentration and extermination camp KL Auschwitz-Birkenau”. The charges relate to two interviews Braun gave in July last year. He declared that “Auschwitz with its gas chambers is unfortunately a fake” and said that claims about the use of gas chambers are part of a “propaganda narrative” supporting a “quasi-religious cult”. In fact, gas chambers were used at Auschwitz, which was located in German-occupied Poland, to kill around 900,000 people, the vast majority of them Jews. Janicki noted that Braun’s remarks “clearly contradict common historical knowledge based on documents, witness accounts, perpetrators’ statements and findings from past criminal proceedings”. Far-right leader Grzegorz Braun says the gas chambers at Auschwitz are “fake” and it is a “fact” that Jews have committed ritual murder. Prosecutors have launched an investigation into whether he violated Poland's law against denying Nazi crimes https://t.co/7UUKzH5ndG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 10, 2025 When Braun originally made his remarks, they were widely condemned in Poland, which suffered enormously under German occupation during World War Two. Justice minister Waldemar Żurek asked the European Parliament, where Braun sits as an MEP, to lift his legal immunity so he could be charged. “For me, it is a scandal that, in a country that suffered such enormous war losses, there is a politician who can deny historical facts that are so painful for Poles,” said Żurek at the time, quoted by the Onet news website. “I won’t let this go. We must bring such people to justice.” In March, the European Parliament approved Żurek’s request, allowing Braun to face charges in relation to his Auschwitz comments, as well as for other alleged crimes. The European Parliament has again voted to strip Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun of immunity to face further charges for Holocaust denial as well as various antisemitic, anti-Ukrainian and anti-LGBT incidents during last year's presidential campaign https://t.co/4EHVEuSDnM — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 26, 2026 On Friday last week, the district prosecutor’s office in Warsaw charged Braun with those other crimes, including the theft of Ukrainian and EU flags he tore down and vandalism of an LGBT+ exhibition being displayed in parliament. In a separate case, in February this year, Żurek also asked the European Parliament to strip Braun of immunity to face charges of denying Nazi crimes over another incident in which he called the gas chambers at both Auschwitz and Majdanek, another Nazi-German camp in occupied Poland, “fake”. Meanwhile, Braun is already on trial in Poland for four other alleged crimes, including using a fire extinguisher to attack a Jewish Hanukkah ceremony in the Polish parliament in December 2023. The trial of Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun for his attacks on a Hanukkah celebration in parliament and a Holocaust lecture has begun. Polish state defence firm Mesko has signed an 8 billion zloty (€1.9 billion) agreement to supply its Piorun man-portable air-defence systems to the armed forces of Poland, Norway, Lithuania and Latvia. The deal is being financed through the European Union’s SAFE mechanism. The agreement represents the largest-ever purchase of Pioruns, which have become an export hit for Mesko after proving their worth during Ukraine’s defence against Russian aggression. Previous buyers include Sweden, the United States, Belgium, Estonia and Norway itself. Nowy etap #PolskaSAFE. Rozpoczynamy wspólne zakupy i to znów w polskim przemyśle! Polska🇵🇱, Litwa🇱🇹, Łotwa 🇱🇻i Norwegia 🇳🇴 kupują wspólnie polskie pioruny. To 63 umowa w ramach polskiego SAFE. Dziś 8 mld zł. Mesko od maja zwiększyło zatrudnienie o 200 osób. To jak to było,… pic.twitter.com/YIDWBGBvpm — Magdalena Sobkowiak (@magdasobkowiak) August 24, 2026 The deal will see the firm provide “several hundred” launchers and “several thousand” missiles for its shoulder-fired Piorun systems, which target low-flying aircraft such as planes, helicopters and drones. Over 80% will be supplied to Poland’s armed forces, with the remainder going to its three NATO allies. The purchase is being funded through SAFE, which provides loans at preferential terms for defence spending. While SAFE can be used individually by countries to make purchases for their own armed forces, some funds are designated for joint procurement by groups of countries (including non-EU member Norway). “Our partners from Lithuania, Latvia and Norway have decided to purchase from Poland,” declared deputy defence minister Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka, who oversees Poland’s participation in SAFE. “We are a leader in the SAFE mechanism and are the first to create such agreements. For the first time, the [Polish defence ministry’s] Armaments Agency is making purchases not only for the Polish armed forces, but also for those of our allies.” “This is a measure of the success of the Polish arms industry,” declared defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, as the deal was announced on Monday. “This is the moment when Poland can proudly say: we are a European leader.” He noted that Mesko’s production capacity is now 2.5 times larger than it was when the current government took power in December 2023. Since SAFE launched in May, the firm’s staffing, which stood at 3,200 by the end of last year, has increased by around 200, added the minister. Poland is by far the largest recipient of SAFE funds, with around €44 billion. The government says that SAFE will not only bolster Poland’s defence capabilities but also provide a boost to the domestic defence industry, where around 90% of the funds will be spent. However, the programme has been opposed by the right-wing opposition and opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki, who argue that it will give Brussels too much influence over Polish defence spending and burden Poland with decades of debt on uncertain terms. Wiceminister @magdasobkowiak: Dzisiaj rozpoczynamy etap wspólnych zakupów. Wiele było pytań o to, czy to zrealizujemy, a może będziemy kupować w Niemczech. I widzicie, co się wydarzyło. Nie dosyć, że te umowy realizujemy w polskim przemyśle zbrojeniowym, to jeszcze nasi partnerzy… pic.twitter.com/hFL8M2Laah — Ministerstwo Obrony Narodowej 🇵🇱 (@MON_GOV_PL) August 24, 2026 In 2022, Pioruns were among the large quantities of military equipment Poland provided to Ukraine to help its eastern neighbour defend itself from Russia’s full-scale invasion. The systems were successfully used to take down a variety of Russian aircraft. In that same year, Mesko announced that the US government had ordered “several hundred” Piorun systems, while Norway also put in a similar order. Last year, Belgium and Sweden announced that they would purchase hundreds of Pioruns, while Ukraine itself also revealed that it had requested a €120 million loan from Poland to help fund the purchase of Polish-made weapons, including Pioruns. Earlier this year, Mesko, which belongs to the state defence holding group PGZ, announced the best financial results in its 100-year history. The firm’s revenues of 2.3 billion zloty in 2025 were up 33% year-on-year, driven by international demand for Pioruns. World.title: Regulation on recognising foreign same-sex marriages comes into force in Poland
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. All registry offices in Poland can now recognise same-sex marriages conducted in other European Union countries, after a government regulation issued in May went into force. The decision came in response to a ruling by the Court of Justice of the EU (CJEU) requiring Poland to recognise such unions. Deputy prime minister Krzysztof Gawkowski expressed his “great joy, because finally in Poland we have a law that gives the right to dignity”. The government’s plenipotentiary for equality, Katarzyna Kotula, warned local authorities that they will be breaking the law if they refuse to comply with the new rules. However, the mayor of one town in a conservative region has already declared that his administration will not recognise such marriages. He argues that doing so would violate Poland’s constitution, which mentions marriage as a union between a man and a woman. Od jutra polskie państwo będzie lepiej chronić godność i prawa swoich obywateli. Nowe wzory aktów małżeństwa umożliwią transkrypcję zagranicznych aktów małżeństw jednopłciowych z pełnym szacunkiem dla par. To koniec administracyjnej fikcji i niepewności, z którą przez lata… pic.twitter.com/mRZYkEg9W4 — Krzysztof Gawkowski (@KGawkowski) August 22, 2026 Polish domestic law still does not allow any form of same-sex unions to be formed. However, last year, the CJEU ordered that the country recognise same-sex marriages conducted in other EU member states. That was followed by a similar ruling from Poland’s own Supreme Administrative Court (NSA). One obstacle to implementing those decisions was that, previously, Poland’s civil registry only allowed male-female marriages to be entered. But, under a regulation issued by the government in May, the system now allows either mixed-sex or same-sex marriages. Even before that went into force on Sunday, some Polish cities, starting with Warsaw and Wrocław, had already begun transcribing same-sex marriages conducted abroad into their registries. They simply listed one spouse in the “man” section and the other as a “woman”, even though that was not accurate for one of them. But some local authorities have refused to do so, pointing to article 18 of Poland’s constitution, which states that: “Marriage, being a union of a man and a woman, as well as the family, motherhood and parenthood, shall be placed under the protection and care of the Republic of Poland.” Such doubts were cited by the mayor of Zakopane, a town in southern Poland, last week when he announced that his administration did not intend to begin recognising foreign same-sex marriages after the regulation came into force. “We will not be issuing such transcriptions in Zakopane,” said Łukasz Filipowski, quoted by local news service Nasze Miasto. He argued that doing so would “not be in accordance with the constitution”, adding that, while Zakopane is “tolerant”, it “promotes the traditional family model…[as] our foundation”. Filipowski pointed to a ruling in July by the Constitutional Tribunal (TK), which found that the government’s regulation conflicts with the constitution’s definition of marriage. However, the government considers the TK to be improperly constituted and therefore regards its rulings as invalid. Poland's Constitutional Tribunal has ruled that a new regulation allowing foreign same-sex marriage certificates to be registered in Poland is unconstitutional. The government says it will not implement the rulinghttps://t.co/xDAzLjcJQ4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 28, 2026 In response to Filipowski’s remarks, Kotula told broadcaster TVN that officials who refuse to recognise foreign same-sex marriages “will be breaking the law”. She said that the personal views of officials cannot “translate into what [legal] actions they take” and that the government would be monitoring the situation. Gawkowski – who, like Kotula, is a leading figure in The Left (Lewica), a junior member of Poland’s ruling coalition – also warned municipalities against issuing refusals. He noted that, as well as the CJEU ruling, Polish courts have also issued orders to recognise foreign same-sex marriages. “In the end, these local authorities will lose [a court battle], so why embarrass themselves? Let’s not look for legal tricks. Let’s just implement something that has been done in other, normal countries for years,” Gawkowski told Polsat News. However, even once same-sex marriages are transcribed into Polish civil registries, there remains uncertainty about what legal consequences that will have in practice, especially given that Poland’s domestic law does not allow for any legally recognised form of same-sex union. Legal experts say that it may take years – and potentially many more legal challenges by same-sex couples – for the situation to be clarified. Separately, parliament earlier this year approved a bill, proposed by the ruling coalition, that would have granted same-sex couples in Poland certain rights normally granted to married couples. However, the law was vetoed by President Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition. Poland has begun recognising foreign same-sex marriages. But the legal consequences for such couples remain unclear, especially as Polish law does not allow any form of same-sex union We asked five experts for their view on what this will mean in practice https://t.co/h2KHmW8sMI — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 19, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Ukraine to establish new national pantheon as Poland warns against honouring massacre figures
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. President Volodymyr Zelensky has signed a law establishing a new national pantheon to commemorate Ukrainian historical heroes. While it is not yet known which figures will be honoured there, Poland has expressed concern that they will include nationalist leaders associated with massacres of Poles in World War Two. On Sunday, a Polish deputy foreign minister warned that Kyiv “will have a huge problem” integrating with the European Union if it celebrates such individuals. But Zelensky reiterated that “only Ukrainians will decide who is a hero to us”. The establishment of the pantheon has taken place against the backdrop of a diplomatic crisis triggered in May by Zelensky’s decision to name a military unit after the “heroes of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA)”. Parts of the UPA were responsible for the so-called Volhynia massacres during World War Two, in which Ukrainian nationalists killed around 100,000 Polish civilians, mostly women and children, as part of an ethnic cleansing operation. Poland regards the episode as a genocide, though Ukraine strongly rejects that label. Many Ukrainians hold the UPA in high regard for the role that it played in fighting for independence from Moscow-backed Soviet rule. Poland condemned Zelensky’s decision and stripped him of the country’s highest honour, the Order of the White Eagle. In response, the Ukrainian president announced in late June that he would seek to create a new national pantheon, because “no one will dictate which heroes we should honour”. A bill creating the pantheon was subsequently approved by the Ukrainian parliament in July, and, on Saturday, Zelensky signed it into law, just ahead of today’s celebrations of Ukrainian independence day. “A Ukrainian pantheon will definitely be established, and only Ukrainians will decide for themselves who our heroes are,” declared Zelensky at a meeting with military veterans on Saturday. “All our true heroes…who fought for Ukraine, for our independence…deserve due honour.” However, the introduction of the law only now begins the process of building the pantheon itself – where the remains of those chosen as national heroes will be reburied – and the establishment of an advisory body that will decide which figures should receive such an honour. It therefore remains unknown for now who will be included in the pantheon. However, on Sunday, Polish deputy foreign minister Marcin Bosacki warned against honouring figures associated with the Volhynia massacres. “Every nation and its government has the right to choose the heroes they deem appropriate,” emphasised Bosacki in an interview with broadcaster TVP. “However, if individuals responsible for mass crimes against civilians, such as [Stepan] Bandera or [Roman] Shukhevych, are included in Ukraine’s national pantheon, it would significantly worsen Ukraine’s relations not only with Poland but with Europe in general,” he added. Bandera was the leader of a faction of the Organisation of Ukrainian Nationalists (OUN-B), which in turn founded the UPA. Shukhevych was a military leader of the UPA. Both figures continue to be honoured in Ukraine, often prompting protests from Poland. 🇵🇱 Polskie MSZ ostrzegło Ukrainę przed „ogromnymi problemami” z Europą z powodu Bandery i Szuchewycza „Ukraina wie, że z tymi, którzy zabijali nie tylko Polaków, ale także Ukraińców, Czechów, Żydów i Romów, na swoich sztandarach będzie miała ogromne problemy z integracją… pic.twitter.com/hyujMppbEw — NEXTA Polska (@nexta_polska) August 24, 2026 “Ukraine knows that, with those who murdered not only Poles, but also some Ukrainians, Czechs, Jews and Roma, on its banners, it will have a huge problem integrating with Europe,” added Bosacki. However, the deputy minister also emphasised that, “strategiaclly, the interests of Poland and Ukraine remain very close” and that Poland must continuing “supporting Ukraine in defeating the aggressive Russia”. “We do not differ much with the Ukrainians, only with certain parts of the Ukrainian authorities after their absolutely erroneious decision to name a unit after the ‘heroes of the UPA’.” The proportion of Poles who hold a negative view of relations with Ukraine has risen to the highest level ever recorded by state research agency CBOS Meanwhile, the proportion who believe reconciliation with Ukraine is possible is at its lowest ever level https://t.co/YYBCFkVxNr — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 12, 2026 Polish government figures have previously made it clear that, if Ukraine honours figures associated with historical massacres, that will make it harder for the country to achieve its ambitions of joining the EU. In June, deputy prime minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz warned that “you can’t build a pantheon to those who destroy European cooperation”, and that countries seeking EU membership should “not build national identity…on events, people or systems that in some way raise objections or pain among EU partners”. Kosiniak-Kamysz declared that, just as Zelensky said no one will tell Ukraine who they can honour, “no one will tell us how to vote on the entry of any state into the European Union”. That was an allusion to the fact that Poland, like all other EU member states, can veto Ukraine’s accession to the bloc. Polish and Ukrainian media have widely quoted Poland's deputy PM as saying: “With Bandera, Ukraine will not enter the EU.” However, he did not actually speak those words. We explain what @KosiniakKamysz actually said and how it came to be misinterpreted https://t.co/S3bozRIJTA — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 1, 2026 ​ Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Rising US sprint star Sam Blaskowski seeks to switch allegiance to Poland
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A rising US track star has declared his intention to represent Poland, the country of his ancestors. Sam Blaskowski’s personal-best 100 metres sprint time of 9.89 seconds is more than a tenth of a second faster than the current Polish national record. “I plan to make Poland the finest sprinting nation in the world. I want to win medals for Poland,” the 23-year-old told Polish broadcaster TVP Sport. Sam Blaskowski przed naszymi kamerami mówi o tym, dlaczego chciałby reprezentować Polskę! 🇵🇱 Więcej o tej sprawie 👉 https://t.co/oC8MJ4moV6 pic.twitter.com/Nw1i7YqrIp — TVP SPORT (@sport_tvppl) August 23, 2026 Blaskowski says that two of his ancestors, Franciszek and Julian, left Poland in 1905, at a time when the country was still partitioned between Germany, Austria and Russia. “My last name is Polish. But for a long time, I didn’t understand that these were my roots. Everything changed recently, because my parents and I talked a lot about our roots,” he explained to TVP Sport. He was contacted by Piotr Maruszewski, coach of the Polish sprint team, after clocking a time of 9.89 seconds in May, which is the joint-ninth-best run by anyone in the world this year. The Polish 100m record is still held by Marian Woronin, who ran 10.00 in 1984. View this post on Instagram A post shared by D3 Glory Days | D3 Running Podcast & News (@d3glorydays) Maruszewski has since been persuading and helping Blaskowski to apply for citizenship, including hiring lawyers to obtain documents proving the sprinter’s heritage. Under Polish law, people who have a Polish parent, grandparent or great-grandparent who was born in or lived in Poland after January 1920 are themselves regarded as holding Polish citizenship. That means Blaskowski’s ancestry may not be enough to qualify. However, it could be enough to convince Poland’s president, Karol Nawrocki, who has discretion to grant citizenship to anyone he wishes. Last year, Nawrocki granted citizenship to Vladimir Semirunniy, a speed skater who fled from Russia to Poland. Semirunniy now represents the Polish national team, including at this year’s Winter Olympics, where he won a silver medal. Given that Blaskowski last represented the United States as a junior over four years ago, he is not subject to World Athletics’ mandatory waiting period for athletes transferring national allegiance. At yesterday’s Silesia Diamond League meeting in Chorzów, Poland’s biggest annual athletics event, Blaskowski told Citius Mag that he expects to be able to represent Poland at next year’s World Championships in Beijing. “I want to inspire the next generation… to make an impact on people around me, and I think the best way to do that is to go and represent Poland,” he told TVP Sport at the same event. “Not only do I have heritage there, but people [in Poland] are very aware of your talent and they give so much appreciation for our sport, and I think it’s a great place.” He added that he and his parents plan to visit their ancestors’ hometown of Sompolno in central Poland on Monday before he again competes in Szczecin on Wednesday. In Chorzów, Blaskowski came fifth in his semi-final against some of the world’s sprinters, just ahead of European champion Romell Glave. Poland’s current top male sprinter, Dominik Kopeć, finished ninth and last in 10.32. The final was won by Jamaica’s Oblique Seville in 9.83 seconds, ahead of another American with a Polish surname, Kenneth Bednarek, who was adopted as a child by a woman with Polish heritage. “The love and support I received from Poland today were truly incredible,” Bednarek wrote on social media after competing at the same event two years ago. “I’m thrilled to have run here for the first time and can’t wait to return with my mom, who has Polish roots.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by Kung Fu Kenny (@kenny_bednarek) Blaskowski would not be the first sprinter to switch allegiance to Poland. Belarusian runner Krystsina Tsimanouskaya received Polish citizenship in 2022, having been granted a humanitarian visa the previous year after the Tokyo Olympics. This month, high jumper Maria Żodzik, another Belarusian who was granted Polish citizenship in 2024, won silver at the European Championships, adding to another silver at last year’s World Championships. At the 2024 Summer Olympics in Paris, Poland’s athletes disappointed, finishing with just one bronze medal in track and field events and one gold and ten medals overall, the country’s worst result since 1956. ​ Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers.
