World.title: Court rejects request by convicted traitor for early release
World.content:
Harju District Court ruled on Tuesday that it will not grant convicted traitor Deniss Metsavas's request for early release under electronic monitoring.

The Prosecutor's Office does not support Metsavas's conditional early release, and the prosecutor maintained that position during the hearing. Tallinn Prison likewise does not support allowing the inmate to continue serving his sentence under electronic monitoring supervised by a probation officer.

Metsavas's defense argued that through his conduct and efforts, he has shown that he has drawn the necessary conclusions from his crimes and that continued imprisonment is not strictly necessary to guide his behavior.

When deciding on conditional early release, the court considers the circumstances of the crime, the offender's personality and prior life, behavior during imprisonment — including participation in activities that reduce the risk of reoffending or willingness to participate in such activities during supervision — as well as living conditions and the potential consequences of early release.

The court reviewed the submitted materials, written opinions from the prosecutor and defense, and heard the prosecutor, the convict and his attorney. Based on this, the court concluded that early release would be premature and unjustified.

The court agreed with the defense that Metsavas has several positive factors supporting early release: a stable place to live, supportive family members, vocational training completed during imprisonment, work in various positions such as librarian and instructor of math and yoga groups, no unpaid claims, and savings in his release fund.

However, the court noted that these positive factors alone do not guarantee lawful behavior after release. Metsavas also had a job, home, family and supportive relatives before imprisonment, yet still committed serious crimes.

The main substantive condition for early release is a reliable forecast that the inmate will behave lawfully in the future. Despite the positive aspects, the court considers the risk of reoffending to be high.

This assessment is supported by the seriousness of Metsavas's first‑degree crime, committed over a long period. In the court's view, the risk of new offenses has not been sufficiently reduced.

The ruling has not yet entered into force.

The court convicted Metsavas of treason in 2018 and sentenced him to 15 years in prison.

World.title: Systematic thefts jump 25% in first half of year
World.content:
Compared with other crimes, systematic thefts grew the fastest in the first half of this year, Justice Ministry says. They were registered a quarter more often than during the same period last year.

A systematic theft is a petty theft committed at least three times within a short period. Most of these are shoplifting cases.

Mari‑Liis Sööt from the Ministry of Justice said this rise in systematic thefts is not unique to Estonia. The same trend is troubling Europe more broadly, where shoplifting and organized retail theft have reached their highest levels in decades.

"If we look at Finland, the UK and several other countries, theft numbers have increased there as well," Sööt said.

Mari-Liis Sööt. Source: Ministry of Justice

As for why theft has increased, she said we can only speculate. One reason may be that the cost of living has risen.

"Criminal networks have also become more professional. Interpol and Europol say this," Sööt added.

Taivo Rosi from the Tartu Police Department said repeated petty thefts have kept police busy for years. It is difficult to claim they have suddenly surged.

"In grocery stores, people pay for part of their goods and leave some items unscanned. When such reports reach the police, it becomes clear fairly quickly that this is no longer a case of customer forgetfulness but intentional behavior — a kind of invoice optimization. They pay for the cheaper goods, leave the expensive ones unscanned at self‑checkout and walk out of the store with a straight back and a proud face," Rosi said.

Politsei. Autor/allikas: Martin Dremljuga/ERR

According to him, people still steal the same things as before: expensive food and alcohol from grocery stores, and costly construction and gardening tools from hardware stores.

"We can also mention the well‑known light vehicles and bicycles, which the police have been talking about for years," Rosi added.

Ministry of Justice statistics show that a total of 14,600 crimes were registered in the first half of the year — a six‑percent increase compared with last year.

World.title: Estonian defense company to invest €200 million in Latvian plant
World.content:
Wolfram Europa will invest €200 million to build an explosives and warhead manufacturing complex near Jēkabpils, Latvia, with production set to begin in 2027, the company announced Wednesday.

The 40-hectare facility will be built on land secured under a long-term agreement with Latvia's State Forests (LVM). Construction and production are planned in three phases beginning in 2027, with around 200 skilled jobs expected once the complex is fully operational.

Wolfram Europa said the plant will produce military explosives, warheads and counter-mobility systems. At full capacity, it is expected to produce up to 300 metric tons of RDX or 100 metric tons of HMX annually, as well as assemble 100,000 anti-tank mines and 200,000 warheads per year.

Latvian Economics Minister Viktors Valainis said the investment would strengthen the country's defense industry while creating high-value jobs and increasing industrial capacity.

Wolfram Europa CEO Magnus-Valdemar Saar said the Jēkabpils facility would be the company's first major production site as it seeks to expand explosives manufacturing capacity in Europe.

The company said in its press release that Europe is producing far from enough explosives and that it aims to fill that gap. Its goal is to become Europe's largest explosives manufacturer.

"Over the past 35 years, Europe has steadily scaled back its explosives and ammunition industry, which has also brought technological development in the sector to a standstill. Europe is rearming, but investment remains focused primarily on platforms and final assembly. This is the explosives gap: weapons production is being scaled up faster than the explosives and warheads that make those weapons effective," Saar said.

World.title: Iraq’s central bank denies issuing banknotes with three zeros removed
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) officially denied reports that it has issued new banknotes with three zeros deleted.

The CBI said in a statement that allegations of producing new currency denominations are unfounded and have no official source.

Any future plans to redenominate the currency or eliminate zeros must go through extensive legal, regulatory, and technical processes, according to the statement.

The CBI urged citizens and media outlets to rely solely on official channels to avoid public misunderstanding and market speculation.

Lawmakers and government officials have lately discussed ideas to remove three zeros from the Iraqi dinar to return stockpiled currency to the legitimate banking system and combat corruption.

According to Jamal Kocher, a Kurdish member of the Iraqi parliament’s finance committee, Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has asked for the removal of zeros from invoices.

Kocher told The New Region that if the plan is implemented, 1,000 Iraqi dinars would be converted to one dinar, while 25,000 dinars would be equivalent to 25 dinars.

Earlier in August, Communications Minister Mustafa Sanad acknowledged the plan to eliminate the zeros and modify the currency.

Despite public discussion and declarations, the CBI has yet to publish a clear timeframe or complete a plan for any currency reform.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate against Iraqi dinar continues to fall
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar continued to decline on Wednesday in both Baghdad, the capital of Iraq, and Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate dropped in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,539.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,542.5 Iraqi dinars on Wednesday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,545 Iraqi dinars and 1,535 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate declined, fluctuating between 1,539.5 and 1,539 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq’s financial revenues decline by 42% in June 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s federal budget revenues plummeted to roughly 35.94 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $27.45 billion) in June 2026, down from 62 trillion Iraqi dinars (about $47.3 billion) during the same month in 2025, marking a 42 percent decline.

According to budget figures, the income generated from oil exports in June 2026 reached 28.5 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $21.76 billion), compared to 57.05 trillion Iraqi dinars (around $43.57 billion) in June 2025, representing a decline of around 28.54 trillion Iraqi dinars ($21.79 billion).

The country’s non-oil income climbed to almost 7.44 trillion Iraqi dinars (about $5.68 billion) in June 2026, up from 4.95 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $3.78 billion) in June 2025.

Oil’s proportion of overall revenues decreased from 92 percent in June 2025 to 80 percent in June 2026, while the contribution of non-oil revenues to the country’s budget climbed from eight percent to 20 percent.

The World Bank’s ‘Global Economic Prospects’ report, published in June 2026, highlights Iraq as a developing economy that relies significantly on commodity earnings, especially oil.

The World Bank has cautioned about the effects of commodity price volatility on the financial and economic stability of energy-exporting countries.

Commodity prices have been vulnerable to periodic shocks since the start of the current decade, the most recent being the huge disruptions caused by the Middle East conflict, which resulted in dramatic swings in global markets for oil, metals, and agricultural supplies.

Iraq’s economic output grew by 0.5 percent in 2024; however, according to estimates, it contracted by 1.5 percent in 2025 before continuing its downward trajectory in 2026. It is expected to rebound to a 12.2 percent growth rate in 2028.

The World Bank mentioned that Iraq’s economy is one of the most vulnerable to regional developments, with its growth forecast lower compared to several other Middle Eastern oil-producing countries.

World.title: Iraq’s Gulf Keystone revenue unchanged as oil prices balance output decline
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Gulf Keystone Petroleum, the operator of the Shaikan field, one of the largest developments in Iraqi Kurdistan, reported stable revenue during the first half of 2026.

The company’s revenues hit $82.8 million as higher oil prices balanced a 67 percent decline in output due to instability in the region.

The company’s shares rose by 9.6 percent following increased revenues and reduced operating costs.

The company’s revenues are nearly unchanged compared to $83.1 million in the first half of 2025.

Adjusted financial operating profitability increased by 26 percent to $51.7 million, driven by cost reduction and robust pricing.

The firm plans to increase output safely and begin a water handling project in the first quarter of 2027.

The Shaikan field is one of the largest oil fields discovered in the Kurdistan region of Iraq and serves as Gulf Keystone Petroleum’s principal asset.

The field covers around 280 square kilometers and is located about 60 kilometers northwest of Erbil, Iraqi Kurdistan’s capital.

The oilfield has an estimated 416 million barrels of proven reserves. It has been in commercial production since 2013.

World.title: President of Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council visits Iran
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The President of Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council, Faiq Zaidan, paid a high-profile, one-day official visit to Tehran on Tuesday to boost cross-border legal cooperation, develop bilateral judicial agreements, and address important security concerns.

Zaidan met with Iran’s senior executive, legislative, judicial, and security leaders, including the Iranian president, minister of justice, judiciary chief, speaker of the parliament, and secretary of the Supreme National Security Council.

The meetings focused on aligning judicial protocols and managing shared legal issues, strengthening legal relations, streamlining judicial procedures, activating cooperative security frameworks, reviewing legislative support for cross-border law enforcement, and addressing border stability and security measures.

Zaidan strongly opposed the foreign economic pressure against Iran, citing the latest US sanctions imposed under “Operation Economic Outcast.”

The Iraqi judicial chief indicated that Iraq will never forget Iran’s support during the US war against the country in 2003 and the war against ISIS terrorist groups.

Zaidan called for the full execution of existing bilateral legal and security agreements between Baghdad and Tehran.

The Iraqi official added that it is important to enhance intelligence cooperation, curb smuggling networks, streamline extradition protocols, and tackle the existence of anti-Iran groups along shared borders.

World.title: 30 Iraqi students join PetroChina Scholarship at China University of Petroleum
World.content:
Qingdao/ Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Thirty Iraqi university students are completing their preparatory semester at the China University of Petroleum (East China) in the coastal city of Qingdao, marking the inaugural cohort of the Pioneers of Excellence academic scholarship program.

The initiative represents the first time the Iraqi federal government has mobilized the state Training, Technology Transfer, and Scholarship Fund (TTSF) to sponsor undergraduate engineering scholars in China. Funded under the corporate social responsibility and capacity-building commitments of PetroChina Iraq – West Qurna 1, the program bridges bilateral energy development with engineering education.

The scholarship follows a customized “0.5 + 4” academic curriculum designed specifically by China University of Petroleum (East China):

Preparatory Foundation (6 Months): Intensive Mandarin Chinese language acquisition paired with foundation courses in advanced calculus, physics, and chemistry.

Undergraduate Degree (4 Years): Full Bachelor of Science degree tracks focusing on three core upstream disciplines: Petroleum Engineering: Reservoir management, well completion, and enhanced oil recovery (EOR). Mechanical Engineering: Industrial machinery design, refinery turbines, and pipeline hydraulics. Petroleum Geology: Geophysical seismic surveying, structural sedimentology, and basin modeling.



Selected through nationwide competitive examinations and panel interviews organized jointly by the Ministry of Oil and the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research, the students represent diverse Iraqi governorates.

Bilateral Diplomatic Patronage: During the program’s official inauguration ceremony in April, the Consul General of China in Basra, Chen Peizhong, and the Scientific and Educational Counselor at the Iraqi Embassy in Beijing, Dr. Mohanad Najah Jawad Al-Shorofi, addressed the cohort, highlighting the importance of developing native technical talent to lead Iraq’s domestic energy sector.

Student Commitment: Class representative Mohammed Al-Tawous reaffirmed the students’ commitment to mastering advanced engineering curricula to support the modernization of Iraq’s oil and gas infrastructure upon graduation.

Industrial Synergy: Since assuming the role of lead contractor at the giant West Qurna 1 oil field in 2024, PetroChina has prioritized local workforce upskilling, transitioning bilateral energy ties from traditional equipment procurement to joint human capital development.

Hydrocarbons form the foundation of Iraq’s national economy. By equipping domestic engineering talent with advanced training at premier international energy institutions, the Ministry of Oil aims to build a modern technical workforce capable of operating complex extraction assets, deploying artificial lift technologies, and managing next-generation energy infrastructure across southern oil fields.

World.title: Iraq and South Korea finalize financing for air defense missile system
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Minister of Finance Falih Sari met on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, with the South Korean Ambassador to Iraq, Lee Jae-myung, to finalize the financing mechanisms for the contracted air defense missile system between Iraq and South Korea.

The high-level meeting was attended by the Chief of Staff of the Iraqi Army, General Staff Officer Abdul Amir Rashid Yarallah, alongside the South Korean military attaché in Baghdad, according to an official statement issued by the Ministry of Finance and reported by the Iraqi News Agency (INA).

Key Financial & Operational Discussions

Contractual Financial Framework: The talks focused on operationalizing the payment schedules, legal frameworks, and treasury mechanisms required to fulfill bilateral contractual commitments without procedural delay.

Airspace Sovereignty Mandate: Minister Sari emphasized that securing Iraq’s airspace and modernizing territorial air defense capabilities remain national priorities to protect state sovereignty and critical infrastructure against external airborne threats.

High-Level Military Coordination: The presence of General Staff Officer Yarallah underscores operational synchronization between the Ministry of Defense’s procurement timetable and the Ministry of Finance’s budgetary disbursements.

Bilateral Commitment: Ambassador Lee Jae-myung and the South Korean defense attaché reaffirmed Seoul’s commitment to expediting technical execution and delivery timelines in line with agreed bilateral protocols.

The air defense procurement contract with South Korea represents a major technological leap for the Iraqi Air Defense Command.

By securing multi-tiered surface-to-air missile interception batteries, Baghdad aims to establish full sovereign control over its national airspace, replace legacy systems, and build an integrated radar and missile shield capable of intercepting advanced airborne threats, drones, and ballistic targets.

World.title: Chief Justice Zaidan and U.S. Envoy discuss post-coalition arms control
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The President of Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council, Judge Dr. Faiq Zaidan, received the Chargé d’Affaires of the U.S. Embassy in Baghdad, Joshua Harris, on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, to discuss judicial mechanisms and the enforcement of the rule of law following the scheduled conclusion of the International Coalition’s military mission.

According to an official statement issued by the Supreme Judicial Council and reported by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), the discussions focused on legal procedures regarding entities and individuals bearing arms in violation of the Iraqi Constitution and applicable laws, as well as institutional frameworks to enforce the rule of law universally across the country.

Key Discussion Pillars

Post-Coalition Legal Framework:Reviewing judicial and legal preparations ahead of the formal conclusion of the Global Coalition against Daesh/ISIS mission in Iraq on September 30, 2026.

Prosecution of Unregulated Arms:Outlining judicial measures against groups and individuals possessing, displaying, or utilizing unauthorized weapons outside the direct chain of command of state constitutional institutions.

Universal Rule of Law:Establishing judicial coordination mechanisms to ensure that legal statutes and constitutional provisions apply equally to all entities without exception.

The meeting comes as Iraq prepares for the transition of the U.S.-led international military mission into bilateral security partnerships.Restricting weapons exclusively to state custody remains a core pillar of the Iraqi government’s institutional program.

By coordinating judicial procedures alongside executive security measures, the Supreme Judicial Council aims to reinforce national sovereignty, enhance judicial oversight over armed actors, and solidify internal stability as the international military mandate concludes.

World.title: Low beam by default: Centre to tighten headlamp norms
World.content:
CURBING THE GLARE: The steps target a major cause of crashes â high beams can briefly blind motorists coming from opposite direction

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: From next April, automatic headlamps in new two-wheelers will work only in passing beam (low beam) mode, and headlamps of cars and other vehicles will have less intense illumination to reduce glare considering that such lights cause visual discomfort or impairs the vision of other road users.The road transport ministry has proposed these changes, along with the mandatory provision for buses and other heavy vehicles to use genuine reflective tapes to improve visibility at night and in bad weather, through draft amendments to Central Motor Vehicles Rules. The amendments in automotive vehicle standards are being made because efforts to persuade drivers and make them aware of the need to use low-beam mode have not yielded desired results.At present, the Automatic Headlamp On (AHO) system can switch on both low beam and high beam modes depending on vehicle settings. The proposed rule mandates that when the automatic system is active, the headlamp will be on low beam.As for high-intensity headlamps, the maximum permissible intensity has been reduced from 1.5 lakh candela or cd (official base unit of luminous intensity) to 1 lakh cd for two-wheelers.The maximum permissible intensity for four-wheelers (cars) has been reduced from 2.25 lakh cd to 1.5 lakh cd.Studies show that white light emitted from headlamps and front fog lamps with higher colour temperatures cause significant glare, leading to discomfort and reduced visibility for other road users. To address this issue, the maximum permissible colour temperature has been restricted to 6,500 Kelvin (K).It has also been proposed that the mounting height of main-beam headlamps be equivalent to that prescribed for passing-beam headlamps.These measures target one of the major causes of night-time road crashes in India â drivers using headlamps on high beam in urban areas, which can temporarily blind motorists approaching from the opposite direction, reducing visibility and increasing the risk of crashes.TOI has learnt the new-generation system will also include an audio alert to discourage unnecessary use of high-beam mode on city roads. If a driver manually switches to high beam in urban conditions, the vehicle will prompt them to shift back to low beam.However, the alert will be speed sensitive. Drivers travelling on highways at speeds above 60 kmph wonât receive the warning, since the use of high-beam mode may be necessary on poorly illuminated highway stretches. The feature is intended to promote safer driving behaviour in urban areas while ensuring that highway driving is not adversely affected, officials said.

World.title: Ahead of Xi Jinping’s visit, India & China announce 8-point consensus
World.content:
According to the joint statement, both sides agreed that any situation on the ground would be addressed promptly.

NEW DELHI: India and China jointly announced Wednesday that the special representatives dialogue on the boundary question â co-chaired by Ajit Doval and Wang Yi this week â had led to an eight-point consensus, signalling positive progress in boundary talks ahead of President Xi Jinpingâs visit to India next month.These included advancing consultations for an âearly and substantial harvestâ of boundary delimitation, setting up more meeting points and hotlines to improve border management, improving understanding of LAC and addressing the ground situation through diplomatic and military engagements, and expanding trans-border trade and river cooperation. The consensus was announced in a rare joint statement after the talks.Building upon the outcomes of the last round of talks in 2024, the two sides agreed that the expert group on boundary delimitation and the working group on border management would advance discussions on an âearly and substantial harvestâ of boundary delimitation and border management. The first task for both these groups would be to agree on their respective terms of reference, said the joint statement.India and China had agreed last year to set up an expert group under the working mechanism for consultation and coordination on India-China border affairs to explore early harvest in boundary delimitation.The formulation was changed to early and substantial on this occasion.Two additional meeting points for military talks and two more channels of border military hotlines were agreed upon to reinforce border management measures.âThe two sides underlined their commitment to advancing negotiations on a framework for the settlement of the boundary question in accordance with the Agreement on Political Parameters and Guiding Principles for Settlement of the India-China Boundary Question signed in 2005 and the consensus reached in subsequent special representative talks in pursuit of a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable solution,â said the MEA in a statement.According to the joint statement, both sides agreed that any situation on the ground would be addressed promptly through existing diplomatic and military channels to resolve outstanding issues along the LAC. âThe two sides discussed ways to improve understanding of LAC in appropriate areas, for better border management,â it said.Both sides also noted the progress on trans-border cooperation, with the Indian side appreciating the efforts made by the Chinese side to increase the number of batches of Kailash-Mansarovar Yatra in Tibet Autonomous Region.âBoth sides appreciated the reopening of the three designated border trading points. The two sides agreed to strengthen exchanges and cooperation in border trade, pilgrimage and other areas, with a view to working together to create an atmosphere featuring dialogue, peace, consultation and cooperation in the border areas,â said the joint statement.India and China agreed to hold the next meeting of India-China Expert-Level Mechanism on Trans-border Rivers in Sept and maintain communication on issues that include hydrological data sharing. They agreed to hold the 26th round of special representatives talks in India in 2027.

World.title: SC judge complains against Raj acting CJ; CJI Surya Kant seeks response
World.content:
CJI Surya Kant Wednesday said he has sought the ACJâs response (File photo)

Judge must get fair chance to respond: CJI Surya Kant

NEW DELHI: Responding to letters written by SC judge Sandeep Mehta complaining against Rajasthan high court acting chief justice (ACJ) Sanjeev Prakash Sharma and seeking his transfer outside the state, CJI Surya Kant Wednesday said he has sought the ACJâs response.Justice Mehta wrote three letters in as many weeks pleading for the transfer of Justice Sharma, who is retiring Sept 26, and appointment of a regular chief justice. Justice Mehta also complained as to why CJI Kant had not acted on his fervent pleas.Justice Mehta, who also hails from Rajasthan HC, has accused Justice Sharma of lacking in leadership qualities and alleged there was maladministration and malpractice on both judicial and administrative sides of HC.CJI Kant told TOI that the matter can be resolved only as per the established mechanism. âThe Supreme Court cannot allow individual complaints concerning judges to be determined through competing claims in the media,â he said. He also released a public statement Wednesday decrying the attempt to hold a public trial over allegations made by one judge against another.Contents of the letters cannot be adjudicated in public domain and that judge concerned must be given a fair opportunity to place his response before any conclusion is reached.The fact that allegations have been made, therefore, cannot by itself be treated as a finding against the judge,â CJI Surya Kantâs statement said.The established mechanism for inquiring into allegations of an Supreme Court or High Court judge is the constitution of an in-house committee â comprising judges â by the Chief Justice of India, if he finds the response of the judge accused of misdemeanour or corrupt practices unsatisfactory and feels the charges are serious enough to warrant a deeper probe.CJI Kant, who is on a three-day official visit to Germany, also told TOI that he has already sought a response from Justice Sharma following the letters from Justice Mehta, who has alleged that there is âclear evidence of favouritismâ by Justice Sharma. Justice Mehtaâs complaints are being examined, CJI Surya Kant said.

World.title: Wireless communication picked up; search operation launched in J&K's Samba
World.content:
The hilly area of Sumb is considered strategically important from a security perspective. (PTI photo)

JAMMU: Security forces launched a joint search operation in the remote, hilly hamlet of Sumb in J&Kâs Samba district after receiving information that a wireless set had been briefly activated in the area and satellite communication was detected around 1pm Tuesday.âThe reported activation of Iridium satellite sets raised suspicion among security agencies, following which a combined team of the Army, police, and personnel from other forces rushed to Sumbâs Makoli village and initiated extensive searches in and around the area,â an official said Wednesday.âTerrorists often switch off such communication devices after contacting their handlers across the border,â said a source, adding that Iridium sets can be used on smartphones through the âIridium GO!â mobile application, which creates a local Wi-Fi network that an iOS or Android phone can connect to.The operation continued until late Tuesday, but no satellite set or other suspicious material was found. Security was tightened along all routes leading to Sumb, with J&K Police and Village Defence Guards maintaining strict vigil, officials said.The hilly area of Sumb is considered strategically important from a security perspective as the route runs along the Basantar river and leads towards the India-Pakistan international border. Due to its proximity to the border, Samba district is a hotbed of terrorist activities. It serves as a gateway district for ultras heading towards Kashmir Valley via the upper reaches of Samba-Udhampur-Doda-Kishtwar.

World.title: 6 dead, 3 hurt as vehicle falls into gorge in J&K’s Poonch

JAMMU: Six people died and three others, including an 11-year-old boy, were injured after the vehicle they were travelling in skidded off the road and plunged into a deep gorge in Surankote in J&Kâs Poonch district on Wednesday.

World.title: 'Open dialogue, inclusive to all': RSS reacts to row over Mohan Bhagwat's New York event
World.content:
RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat will address the 'Universal Oneness Celebration' at Madison Square Garden on August 29.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Interfaith forum

A major RSS outreach event is being planned in New York, with Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat scheduled to address the "Universal Oneness Celebration" at Madison Square Garden on August 29.The event is being organised by American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue and is expected to bring together Hindu-American organisations and members of the Indian diaspora around the themes of shared heritage, interfaith dialogue and unity.The programme, however, has triggered a political controversy even before it takes place, with New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani publicly opposing Bhagwatâs appearance.Mamdani, New Yorkâs first Muslim and Indian-American mayor, said he did not support the planned rally, describing the RSSâs vision as exclusionary and contrasting it with his own understanding of India as a pluralistic country. At the same time, he acknowledged that the event is privately organised and said he was unsure whether the city had the legal authority to cancel it.The controversy is particularly significant because of Mamdaniâs own Indian heritage and his position as mayor of one of the world's most diverse cities.His criticism has also drawn support from groups opposed to the RSS, while critics of the mayor have questioned whether his position amounts to singling out a Hindu organisation.The RSS, meanwhile, has pushed back strongly against the criticism.RSS communications chief Sunil Ambekar said the New York gathering represents an interfaith forum where Bhagwat will engage with a âdiverse, multicultural, and multi-faith audienceâ.He said the event reflects what the RSS describes as the inclusive and welcoming nature of the Bharatiya ethos, and invited anyone interested in understanding the organisationâs philosophy to participate in open dialogue.The timing of Bhagwatâs visit is also important. The RSS is marking its centenary in 2025-26, and the New York programme forms part of a broader international outreach by Bhagwat covering the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom. The stated objective is to engage Indian-origin communities abroad and present the RSSâs views on India, Hindu society and its own philosophy.

World.title: Govt pushes to make SCADA systems in power sector Indian by 2030
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Govt wants to end imports of technology used to monitor and control Indiaâs power grid by 2030, reducing dependence on foreign companies for systems that are critical to keeping electricity flowing across the country.A committee set up by Central Electricity Authority (CEA) to draw up a roadmap for this has found that local content in these Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems is below 20%. It has warned that dependence on proprietary foreign systems can pose risks if there are disruptions in global supply chains or access to technology, upgrades and technical support is restricted.SCADA systems form the digital backbone of the country's load-dispatch network, linking power plants and substations with state, regional and national control centres. They allow grid operators to see what is happening across the network in real time and control equipment remotely.The committee found that software is the easier part of the transition: 36 of the 38 identified software modules can be developed domestically in the short term. But hardware, which accounts for about 75% of SCADA costs, will be a bigger challenge, with 16 of 25 key components expected to be ready for indigenous deployment within two years.The panel has also proposed establishing a dedicated testing platform within two years, including cyber-security validation. This would be followed by real-time pilots at load despatch centres, where indigenous systems would run in parallel with existing systems before being deployed across the grid.A senior power ministry official said the push is aimed not just at reducing imports but also at giving India greater control over the technology running its critical electricity infrastructure and reducing dependence on foreign vendors for upgrades and support.

World.title: SC youth’s death: CB-CID names six police officers as accused
World.content:
The CB-CID charge sheet filed in the Scheduled Caste youth Akash Delison’s custodial death case revealed that a murder case has been registered against six policemen, including a police inspector.

Delison, from Krishnarajapuram near Manamadurai in Sivaganga district, was arrested on March 5, 2026 in connection with a case in which two people were hacked during a dispute in Manamadurai. Delison was admitted to the Madurai Government Rajaji Hospital with injuries, but he died at the hospital.

The police had claimed that he was injured after falling from a bridge while trying to escape arrest, and that he died despite treatment after being admitted to the hospital.

However, alleging that Akash died due to police assault, his relatives staged continuous protests. Further, an autopsy revealed injuries at 28 places.

Police Inspector Dileepan and five other policemen were placed under suspension in connection to the death of the youth.

Subsequently, CB-CID police had been investigating the case under murder and SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, charges.

Meanwhile, the CB-CID police filed a chargesheet in the Madurai court on June 18. A copy of that chargesheet has now been received by Akash Delison’s family.

The document stated that the police took Akash to a eucalyptus grove near Manamadurai and assaulted him with an iron rod. He suffered a fracture on his right leg below the knee and above the ankle. Consequently, Akash Delison died due to a fat embolism in his blood vessels, it claimed.

‘Police hid rod used in assault’

Additionally, the chargesheet stated that the police hid the iron rod used in the assault and falsely recorded that he sustained injuries after falling while trying to escape from the police.

Six individuals — Inspector Dileepan, Sub-Inspector Guhan, and constables Kaleeswaran, Mahendran, Deiventiran, and Palaniappan — have been included as accused in this case.

‘Premeditated intent’

Akash Delison’s family alleged that the copy of the chargesheet was provided 68 days after it was filed, that it contained only 12 pages, and that all the documents recorded during the investigation were not fully provided.

The document added that the six police personnel had acted with premeditated intent, fully conscious of the victim’s caste.

World.title: Health institution’s TEDx event brings new perspective on innovation, social impact
World.content:
Noted classical dancer and choreographer Mallika Sarabhai has underlined the significance of health communication, with a focus on malnutrition, sexual and mental health, and empowerment of communities. Ms. Sarabhai addressed a TEDx event at a health institution in Jaipur, bringing together activists and changemakers.

The fourth edition of TEDx, organised by the Indian Institute of Health Management Research (IIHMR) University, brought a new perspective on health, innovation, entrepreneurship, social impact, culture, and the arts. A battery of activists working on the issues of child rights, disability and public health attended the event.

Ms. Sarabhai said the conversations around mental health and sexuality, which rarely happened in society, could bust the myths and move people’s consciences. “Talking about the unseen, about shame, and about malnutrition and violence is part of health communication,” she said.

“We have started going into the community, finding their myths, their songs, their stories, and putting a twist in the tale. We have managed to break down the fear and shame of speaking,” the Padma Bhushan recipient and Darpana Academy’s director said. An effective communication about health could resolve several issues, Ms. Sarabhai added.

The TEDx event was dedicated to the theme, “Ignite the unseen”. IIHMR University president P.R. Sodani said new ideas and experiences in the healthcare sector could challenge perspectives and inspire meaningful changes.

The speakers from diverse fields threw light on the concepts which are often overlooked but have the potential to shape the society. Besides public health and child rights, other subjects included performing arts, assistive technology, music, entrepreneurship, and wildlife conservation.

The participants included Om Prakash Gurjar, 2006 International Children’s Peace Prize laureate and founder of Paathshala Trust; musicologist Gauri Yadwadkar of Roundglass Music; disability rights advocate Prateek Madhav; and wildlife conservationist R. Udayan Lahiry.

World.title: Supreme Court judge seeks transfer of Rajasthan High Court acting Chief Justice, CJI says allegations can’t be treated as a finding
World.content:
In three letters to Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, Supreme Court judge Justice Sandeep Mehta this month asked why his “fervent appeals” for the transfer of Rajasthan High Court Acting Chief Justice (ACJ) Sanjeev Prakash Sharma have been “ignored” despite there being “clear evidence” of “favouritism”.

In a press statement released by the Supreme Court following media reports on August 26 about Justice Mehta's letters, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, who is currently abroad on an official tour, emphasised that he has already taken note of the concerns raised by Justice Mehta in his letters, and stressed that "allegations against a sitting judge must be dealt with strictly through the established institutional mechanism".

The CJI maintained that the contents of the letters cannot be adjudicated in the public domain and that the judge concerned must be given a fair opportunity to place his response before any conclusion was reached.

“Any decision regarding the continuation, transfer or other administrative action concerning the acting Chief Justice would be taken by the competent institutional authority after due consideration of the material… The Supreme Court cannot allow individual complaints concerning judges to be determined through competing claims in the media,” the statement read.

In his first letter on August 2, 2026, Justice Mehta had written to the CJI about the “grim and disturbing scenario” in his parent High Court in Rajasthan.

In the letter, he said the ACJ of the High Court, who is due to retire on September 26, displayed a total lack of leadership qualities and exhibited conduct unbecoming of a leader of the institution on more than one occasion. The Supreme Court judge reminded the CJI that he had been making repeated requests for the appointment of a regular Chief Justice to the High Court since the beginning of 2026.

“However, till date, the request to have a Chief Justice from another State in my parent High Court has met with no positive response,” Justice Mehta wrote.

He said there was maladministration and malpractices on both the judicial and administrative side of the High Court.

Cases were suddenly withdrawn and moved to the Bench of the Acting Chief Justice (ACJ) without any justifiable cause, Justice Mehta alleged. He said he was initially asked by the CJI to provide a list of these cases in writing, but was immediately thereafter assured that there was no need to place anything in writing and that suitable action would be taken.

The next letter, on August 10, noted that the CJI had asked Justice Sharma to respond to the shifting of cases, but said that no specific information was further available on the reply or facts of these cases.

Justice Mehta wrote that he had "positive information"that Justice Sharma called and humiliated judicial officers in Rajasthan to satisfy a “personal vendetta”. A full court meeting was organised to designate a “large number of favoured advocates as seniors”, that too, on a working day, he accused. He wrote that he had been "informed" of the preparation of a "fanciful plan" for a multi-storied tower with almost 100 rooms to function as a guest house for the High Court, calling it a “sheer waste of public money”.

Justice Mehta also wrote that anguished judges of the High Court have said they were “frequently threatened” with retributive action, including transfer, by the ACJ, who claimed “closeness” with the CJI.

The Supreme Court judge noted that the CJI’s Bench had recently observed the growing trend of judges passing orders for extraneous considerations in the autumn days of their careers.

“It is indeed ironical that on one hand, the Chief Justice of India is flagging corrupt practices by judges in the eve [towards the end] of their careers, and here we have an ACJ indulging in these very activities with impunity,” one of the letters said.

In his last letter on August 17, Justice Mehta uses terms like “rampant nepotism and favouritism” to describe the ACJ’s actions.

‘Long rope’

He said it was “beyond comprehension” why “such a long rope” was given to a judge whose request for repatriation to the Rajasthan High Court was not accepted by the Supreme Court Collegium in March 2023.

Justice Sharma, who had served in Patna and then the Punjab and Haryana High Court, was finally recommended for repatriation to the Rajasthan High Court in a Supreme Court Collegium meeting on May 26, 2025. He was appointed Acting Chief Justice of Rajasthan in September last year, and has been holding the post for over 10 months.

“I have been repeatedly requesting you to take a decision for appointing a Chief Justice from another State to the Rajasthan High Court so that this unfortunate situation can be prevented. Continued ignorance of the request, in my opinion, is wholly against the interest of the institution,” Justice Mehta wrote to the CJI.

World.title: Nepal flash floods LIVE: At least 157 dead, hundreds missing; India sends first tranche of relief materials
World.content:
At least 157 people were confirmed dead and more than 400, including around 133 Indians, were missing or out of contact after a massive flash flood in Nepal’s Bhotekoshi River swept through villages in Rasuwa, a district bordering China’s Tibet region, on Wednesday morning, authorities said.

Also read | At least eight killed in Nepal flash flood; multiple districts placed on high alert

“Several security personnel, government officials and employees of hydropower projects are also out of contact,” the PMO said. “The disaster has damaged 19 motorable bridges and 40 kilometres of road.”

Officials said the death toll could rise and that it would take days to assess the full extent of the damage.

Also read | At least 50 pilgrims from Tamil Nadu stranded as landslips disrupt route

Prime Minister Balendra Shah said in a social media post that he was left with a “heavy heart”. “The entire nation has been left shocked and deeply saddened by the loss of life and damage to property,” he added, describing the disaster as “sudden” and “massive”. Stating that the government immediately mobilised all its resources for rescue operations, he vowed that rescue operations would continue through the night.

World.title: SP announces Stree Samman Samriddhi Yojna, promises to open 26,000 closed schools across U.P.
World.content:
Samajwadi Party (SP) on Wednesday (August 26, 2026) announced it would implement the Stree Samman Samridhhi Yojna, under which women would receive ₹40,000 every year to help them become economically stronger, if the party forms government after the 2027 Assembly polls.

Addressing a press conference in Lucknow alongside party president Akhilesh Yadav, party Lok Sabha MP from Mainpuri, Dimple Yadav said, “Women’s power will develop not merely by talking about it, but by giving women true representation. Respect and prosperity of every woman included in the PDA as “Aadhi Abadi (women) is our resolve.”

Elaborating on the name of the scheme, Ms. Yadav said the word ‘Stree’ (woman) had been chosen because it represented gender without restricting it to any particular age group.

“While words such as girl, young woman or woman indicate an age bracket, the word ‘Stree’ represents a gender and, therefore, the scheme can apply to women of every age,” she said, adding that economic empowerment of women is important as it help to become self-reliant and contribute financially to their families, thereby increasing their equality within the household.

“The economic strength of a woman itself is her empowerment,” she said.

The Mainpuri MP added that the scheme would be implemented in phases and its functioning and success would be assessed periodically, with necessary improvements made based on the outcome.

Speaking on the announcement, the SP president Akhilesh Yadav described it as a resolution for the complete freedom of half the population. “This is a resolution for the complete freedom of half the population; the work of honouring them by giving them ₹40,000 every year will be done in the Samajwadi government,” said Mr. Yadav.

The SP chief alleged that for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), women’s empowerment has become just a slogan. “Women’s reservation has been passed; why is the Bharatiya Janata Party delaying it? It should be implemented in the next elections,” he said.

The SP president also announced that over 26,000 schools closed across the state during the merger process will be reopened if the SP is voted to power. “26,000 closed primary schools will be reopened. Someone who is suffering, sad, humiliated- that is PDA. In the future, girls who pass intermediate will be given laptops and given the opportunity to move ahead,” he said.

Mr. Yadav alleged most injustice is being done to daughters in Uttar Pradesh. “During the fire incident, the Chief Minister of our State was saying in front of the mother that he was not in the mood to listen to speeches, and that Khushi Dubey was humiliated by sending her to jail. Statistics show that the most injustice is being done to daughters in Uttar Pradesh,” said the SP president.

The SP president added that the future SP government will create a path towards respect and prosperity through digital media, financial assistance, education and training. “Through modern means of upliftment laptops, financial assistance, education and training, which will gradually teach women to stand on their own feet with dignity and confidence,” he said.

Mr. Yadav further accused the BJP of promoting communalism in education, adding that the fundamental concern related to education, teachers, students and jobs is not in the BJP’s imagination.

“The BJP sees communalism even in education. Education, teachers, students, and the jobs that come with education are not on the BJP’s agenda. We have to unitedly overthrow the corrupt regime; they are fundamentally against logic, reasoning, justice, democratic ideas,” said Mr. Yadav, urging all sections of the society to decisive defeat the BJP.

The party made the announcement on Women’s Equality Day, which is observed annually on August 26 in the United States to commemorate the adoption of the 19th Amendment to the US Constitution in 1920, which granted women the constitutional right to vote.

World.title: M.P. Minister’s remarks on sugar price surge draw Congress’ ire
World.content:
Madhya Pradesh Cabinet Minister and senior Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Kailash Vijayvargiya on Wednesday (August 326, 2026) appeared to defend the rising sugar prices as he said that it should “get very expensive” while advocating less consumption among people.

Mr. Vijayvargiya made the remarks in a light conversation with the media in Indore but ended up facing political backlash amid the recent surge in sugar prices ahead of the festive season. Various Opposition leaders have also blamed the Centre’s ethanol policy while alleging that sugar cane was being diverted for the production of ethanol, which is further blended into petrol.

Mr. Vijayvargiya said, “I guess it [sugar price] was ₹70/kg yesterday, and today it is ₹60. It will reduce further. Anyway, 90% of people don’t like sweets these days. I don’t eat sweets at all. So, it’s good. I would say that it should become very expensive. (Sugar) should only be available at cheap rates at government fair-price shops for children...The elderly should not be given sugar at all. The doctors do not consider sugar consumption after 40 years of age good.”

“If you are over 40, you can eat jaggery once in a while, but avoid sugar completely,” he said.

M.P. Congress president Jitu Patwari, however, termed the remarks “an insult” to the poor and the middle class people.

Claiming that the BJP leaders had in past promised sugar at ₹13/kg, Mr. Patwari said, “Those who came into power with slogans [to reduce inflation] are now advising people to consume less sugar. They are insulting and laughing at people after torturing them. The public will respond to their laughter in the coming elections.”

Amid criticism over the prices, the Union Government has said it is monitoring the situation closely while citing a various factors for the surge, including lower-than-expected domestic production, increased demand ahead of the festive season, weather-related damage to the sugar cane crop, tightening global sugar supplies, and speculation and hoarding by some sections of the industry.

World.title: Drawing lines: On the India-China 25th Special Representatives’ talks
World.content:
Following Tuesday’s talks between the Special Representatives (SRs) on the boundary question, India and China have agreed to substantial outcomes on managing the disputed border. According to an eight-point consensus released on Wednesday, both countries have agreed to advance discussions on “an early and substantial harvest of boundary delimitation”. They have agreed to hold next month a meeting of an expert-level mechanism on trans-border rivers and to maintain communication on sharing hydrological data, which India has been pushing for. Two additional meeting points to hold talks between top military commanders will be set up, along with two new channels of hotlines in the Eastern and Middle Sectors. National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and China’s Foreign Minister Wang Yi reaffirmed the efforts taken over the past two years to keep the peace along the Line of Actual Control, and committed to continuing the on-going normalisation in relations. That the NSA’s visit to Beijing took place before India hosts the BRICS Summit, on September 12, underlined both sides’ keenness to continue with this process of re-engagement, with the expected visit of Chinese President Xi Jinping after a gap of seven years. An October 2024 meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Mr. Xi kickstarted this calibrated effort towards normalcy, and a 2025 meeting in Tianjin helped continue the momentum. It is apparent that both sides see continued engagement at the highest level as key to sustaining this process of normalisation.

The dual tracks of the SR meetings and the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on border affairs, a body comprising diplomats and military officials, have worked well towards keeping the borders generally stable over the past two years. The latest outcomes will certainly help in keeping the peace. Less clear is how both sides intend to take up the task of border delimitation. Neither side has explained which parts of the border they plan to delimit, or whether they are reconsidering the 2005 agreement on Political Parameters and Guiding Principles, under which the SRs were tasked with first agreeing a framework to settle the boundary. While both sides in Beijing reaffirmed the 2005 agreement, Article 10 of its text notes that it is only on the basis of the framework that both sides can delineate the boundary. Tangible progress on the border dispute must certainly be welcomed. However, agreements made without public visibility, notwithstanding their merit, may invite suspicion. As India and China continue negotiating their long-running boundary question, it is imperative that they bring their publics along.

World.title: The glorious past of Chennai’s Shanti Theatre
World.content:
Today, when we cross Anna Salai in Chennai, we think of traffic, deadlines, and the rush to work. But for many in the city, the same road carries a different set of memories. There was a time when a theatre called Shanti stood here, attracting generations of moviegoers. The theatre became such a landmark that its name spilled beyond its walls and screens, and a bus stop nearby came to be known as Shanti.

The theatre was built by G. Umapathy and D. Shanmuga Raja, the erstwhile Raja of Sivaganga, and was opened in January 1961 by then Chief Minister K. Kamaraj. The inaugural show was Srinivasa Kalyanam, while the first film to be screened at the theatre was Thooya Ullam, starring Akkineni Nageswara Rao and Savitri.

According to an article published in The Hindu on January 13, 1961, the theatre, which cost ₹20 lakh, had a seating capacity of 1,200. C. Subramaniam, the then Finance Minister, who presided over its inauguration in 1961, said putting up a fine modern theatre was not sufficient. They should produce the right type of pictures that would entertain and educate the people without corrupting their minds, he said.

The theatre was later bought by legendary actor Sivaji Ganesan. “The promoters needed a fresh infusion of funds. They then approached Sivaji Ganesan, who invested in the theatre and eventually bought the shares,” said actor and writer Mohan Raman.

“When it opened, it was the largest single-screen theatre. It had the biggest balcony at the time, with nearly 400 seats. It was fully air-conditioned, and the car parking facility was very good. I would say it had a lavish car park. Everything about this theatre was good,” said film industry analyst Sreedhar Pillai.

More than 80 films starring Sivaji Ganesan found their way to the Shanti screen and many hit a 100-day run. The theatre has also screened films such as Gone with the Wind, Ivanhoe, and Drums of Destiny. In 2005, the theatre was renovated and began its new chapter with the film Chandramukhi, starring Rajinikanth and Prabhu, the youngest son of actor Sivaji Ganesan. The film ran for 888 days in the theatre, a record those days.

Ramkumar Ganesan, the eldest son of actor Sivaji Ganesan, recollected fond memories of the theatre, and said: “I remember attending the premiere of Karnan (starring his father). And whenever a Sivaji Ganesan film was released, I used to be among the first to buy tickets, often choosing seats in A row seat numbers 1-10.” “I also attended many celebrations there. There is one photograph from the time a South East Asian delegation visited the theatre. All the popular actors of the time, including M.G. Ramachandran, attended the event,” he reminisced. The theatre has now become a prime office space housing multinational firms,” he added.

The curtains eventually came down on Shanti Theatre, making way for a real estate development that transformed the spot that once echoed with whistles, applause, and film songs into a sprawling office complex.

World.title: 14 infants killed in fire at Pims' gynae ward in Islamabad
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Fourteen infants were killed in a fire that broke out in the gynaecology ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) early on Wednesday.

What has happened so far:

14 babies die after fire erupts in ward; initial reports say spark erupted from AC, blaze spread due to oxygen points

Bereaved families decry rescue teams arrived “too late”; witnesses report locked doors

Health secretary removed; inquiry panel formed on PM’s orders; separate fact-finding committee constituted

Health Minister Mustafa Kamal vows accountability; Tallal Chaudhry defends district administration

Condolences from across the nation, other countries pour in

Footage showed rescue workers using ladders to reach broken windows to access the affected area and grief-stricken women sitting on the ground outside the hospital. An AFP reporter saw a woman in tears and a man clear glass from two broken windows, as security guards stood at the entrance to the medical facility.

Several witnesses, their hands and faces blackened from the smoke, told AFP they waited hours for help from the emergency services. They were forced to smash through windows to try and get to the neonatal intensive care unit.

Others said they came across locked doors and alleged guards prevented those inside the building from leaving as the fire raged.

However, the hospital disputed this in a statement issued later in the evening. “All emergency exits were fully open and operational,” it asserted.

In a statement, the Islamabad administration said that the fire broke out on the third floor of the Mother and Child Hospital’s ward. It said that rescue teams rushed to the scene, with six fire brigade vehicles and four ambulances taking part in the rescue operation.

“The fire was immediately brought under control and the children were immediately shifted to the intensive care unit,” it said, adding that 14 children “were completely burnt”.

Pims Spokesperson Dr Aneeza Jalil told Dawn that 15 babies were in the ward. “At least one baby was saved by a doctor,” she said.

Health Minister Mustafa Kamal, who reached Islamabad from Karachi in the afternoon, vowed that “no one responsible for negligence, including me, will be spared”.

“The tragic fire incident at Pims MCH Centre, resulting in the loss of precious neonatal lives, is deeply heartbreaking,” the public hospital said.

Citing a preliminary report, the Pims statement said the incident was “initially caused by a spark inside nursery at 06:38am and within seconds a massive fire erupted due to oxygen points at each incubator”.

It said two doctors and two nurses on duty inside the nursery responded “immediately and called security staff, who joined in and tried to get in twice [to bring] babies out until 06:39am, when a huge blast occurred and ceilings fell down”.

The statement said the duty staff managed to rescue a baby in the nursery and four in an adjacent room, along with three mothers.

“Besides immediate response, staff managed rescue of 73 other admitted patients in the adjacent Gynae ward on the same floor within minutes,” it added.

The hospital asserted that “available fire safety equipment installed, including 35 fire extinguishers, were all utilised by the staff to contain the situation”.

Health minister vows accountability

Speaking to reporters in Islamabad, the health minister said he will present himself to his superiors for accountability.

Providing details of the incident, Kamal said: “At 6:38am, it can be seen in the CCTV footage that there was a spark in the AC, then a fireball could be seen erupting out of it and landing on the floor of the ward. In one minute, at 6:39am, four people, including two nurses and two doctors, could be seen rushing for help and around the same time, the whole room was engulfed in flames”.

The health minister said the incident was being investigated by “experts, different institutions including us”, adding that “nothing will remain hidden and all facts will be unearthed”.

He continued: “Apparently, it seems that 14 out of the 15 infants were connected to oxygen tubes and it was that oxygen which caught flame.”

Kamal reiterated that the “heart-wrenching” incident will be investigated and warned that “if there was any negligence, then as I said, we will not spare them, including myself”.

The minister further said that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had instructed him “not to speak about certain issues”. He said he would be meeting the premier and that the two had been in touch.

“Everyone is on board, and the findings will be presented,” he said.

On being asked if he was going to tender his resignation, the health minister said, “As I have said before, whoever is responsible [..] they will not be spared. I have said what I can, and I wish I could say more, but the prime minister is my boss, and whatever his orders will be, I can only say that.”

The federal minister was also questioned about fire safety standards at Pims, with a reporter pointing out that the hospital had been issued notices for the past eight years.

Kamal claimed that the hospital had ensured compliance each time a notice had been issued in the past, pointing out that the blaze was contained with “26 fire extinguishers available in the building”.

When a reporter asked about his early morning statement over the lack of adequate facilities at Pims and “why in his 2-2.5 years as a health minister, no improvement had been made”, the minister, getting visibly frustrated, said, “If it has been 2-2.5 years, then feel free to shoot me” and clarified that he had only been at his position for one year and two months.

“What I said in the morning has to be seen within a certain parameter. I was saying that even if this did not happen, there are still challenges at the hospital. It has a capacity of 200-300 OPDs, and today, it has a footfall of over 9,000 people”.

He maintained that he was merely presenting facts. “I am not saying that everything is ideal.”

When pointed out that it was his responsibility to upgrade the facility, Kamal acknowledged his role and said, “We have to do it, but things cannot be ideal given the current scenario, but if we go into that, the conversation will take a different turn”.

The minister reiterated that every responsible person will be held accountable. “If I am willing to present myself for accountability, then no one else is left.

“Wherever there has been negligence, we will fix it,” he said. Noting that such an incident should not have happened, he said: “Will get to its root cause and ensure prevention in the future.”

The minister was also asked about reports that the door of the ward was locked, to which he said that access to the ward was limited and guarded due to “instances of people stealing newborn babies a couple of years back”.

“You would not see that anywhere else in the world, but we have the issue, so the door had to be manned with a guard,” Kamal explained.

During his media talk, the minister got into a verbal altercation with an individual who asked when action would be taken against those responsible. As the individual got louder, the minister repeatedly gestured to him to come forward and said, “Sir, come here and talk to me.”

‘Give me my child back’

Malik Israr, whose niece was admitted to the gynae ward, told Dawn that it was unfortunate the nursery was housed in a building in which repair and renovation work was ongoing.

“After the fire erupted, they told patients to vacate the building. Women who had just given birth had to rush down the stairs from the second floor,” he said.

A worker removes broken pieces of a glass window after a fire broke out at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences hospital in Islamabad on Aug 26, 2026. — Reuters

Khurram Mehmood, 40, told AFP he lost his three-day-old daughter in the blaze and that rescuers took hours to arrive.

“I lost my daughter. She was only three days old,” he said. “My wife was in the ward. They took everyone out. We were sitting on the road waiting for help.”

He added, “The fire erupted at 6am, rescue and authorities reached at 9am; people were helping themselves.”

“Give me my child back,” Jaweria, who lost her newborn, said outside the hospital. “I want justice.”

She told AFP: “Rescue teams arrived too late. Police arrived after four hours and said they are here to investigate. To hell with you, rescue team and police. Babies burnt to death there, but nobody could save them.”

A grieving father reacts as his child’s coffin is transported in an ambulance following a fire outside the Mother and Child Health (MCH) ward at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) Hospital in Islamabad on August 26, 2026. — AFP

“For two hours I kept crying and wailing,” the mother said, questioning the action taken by hospital staff and emergency responders.

“Why did the doctors leave the children there? One nurse, one doctor, one gynaecologist, one paediatrician — there was nobody in the entire ward. Why were they not there?”

Mudasir, another parent who also lost his child, said all doors of the ward, except one, were shut and that there was “no fire security” in the ward.

A mother with black residue from the smoke on her hands stood crying outside the hospital as she held her 10-day-old baby in her arms.

“People were screaming. There was black smoke. We ran for our lives. Thank god my baby is safe,” Shagufta Parveen told AFP.

A man consoles a grieving father (C) as his child’s coffin is carried after a fire outside the Mother and Child Health (MCH) ward at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) hospital in Islamabad on Aug 26, 2026. — AFP

Ali Abbas, 20, was with his sister who was a patient in the ward.

“There was a short circuit in the nursery, in the children’s ward,” he said. “It was full of smoke.”

Eyewitness Abdul Ghafoor told AFP that there was “thick black smoke inside and patients were trapped”.

“I barged in to try to save as many people as I could, but we could not reach the ward where the patients were.

“The fire was in the nursing room, and we could not see anything. Some of us broke the windows to help people get out.”

Among the victims were the twin daughters of Bahadur Khan, a vegetable seller, The New York Times reported. He had left them with their mother to get some rest at home. Bahadur said his wife was recovering in Pims’ intensive care unit and was not aware of the deaths of their three-day-old daughters.

Alam Zaib, the father of a newborn child who was in another ward and remained safe, was quoted as saying that he tried to enter the ward where the fire broke out, but the door was locked.

Pims, established in 1985, is Islamabad’s biggest public sector hospital. It is one of the oldest health facilities in the federal capital and comprises several hospitals and teaching institutes.

Fires in large buildings are frequent in Pakistan, often due to poor safety laws and building codes as well as lax enforcement.

Health secretary removed; inquiry, fact-finding panels formed

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif took notice of the incident and directed the relevant authorities to investigate it. According to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), he expressed deep sorrow and grief at the incident and offered his condolences to the bereaved families.

“Such a situation involving children is unbearable,” the statement quoted him as saying.

“The circumstances that led to the incident should be thoroughly reviewed, those responsible should be identified, and the strictest possible action should be taken,” he said.

In a second statement, the PMO said the prime minister had suspended and removed federal Health Secretary Muhammad Aslam Ghauri.

The premier chaired a high-level meeting on the incident, where he expressed his anger and issued directives for “strict action”, the PMO said in another statement.

It also stated that the prime minister suspended the federal health secretary and asked him to leave the meeting.

The statement quoted the prime minister as saying: “I am heartbroken at this tragic incident and share the parents’ grief.”

Subsequently, Captain (retired) Muhammad Mahmood, a BS-21 officer of the Pakistan Administrative Service (PAS), was appointed to the post of health secretary for three months “or till the posting of a regular incumbent,” a notification issued by the Cabinet Secretariat said.

According to the PMO, a high-level inquiry committee, headed by former interior secretary Shahid Khan, has launched an investigation.

According to state-run Radio Pakistan, Major General (retired) Dr Khursheed Uttra, Establishment Division Secretary Dr Barrister Nabeel Awan and Islamabad Deputy Commissioner Irfan Nawaz Memon will serve as its members.

The inquiry committee will submit an interim report to the prime minister within 48 hours, containing recommendations for immediate action.

It will submit a comprehensive report within five days, containing the findings of the complete investigation and actionable recommendations.

The health ministry has been directed to immediately notify the inquiry committee and provide it with the necessary assistance.

According to the terms of reference (ToRs), the panel will ascertain the cause of the fire and review the rescue operations carried out by the hospital staff and relevant agencies such as Rescue 1122.

Besides conducting a detailed review of the fire safety infrastructure at Pims, the committee will also determine the responsibility and negligence, if any, of individuals involved in the incident.

It will recommend necessary reforms for Pims’s administrative system to help prevent such kind of incidents in the future.

Separately, a notification issued by the Islamabad district magistrate said that a seven-member fact-finding committee, headed by the additional deputy commissioner general (ADCG), had been formed to determine the facts behind the fire.

The members of the committee included the CES director general, the City police station superintendent, the assistant commissioner (Industrial Area), the director general of Capital Development Authority’s (CDA) Electrical and Mechanical wing, along with representatives from Pims and Islamabad Electric Supply Company.

The committee was tasked with determining the exact cause of the fire, assessing whether adequate and functional fire-safety measures were in place, and evaluating the response time and effectiveness of the rescue and fire-fighting operations.

The notification said that a report would be furnished within 24 hours.

Ambulances are parked outside a mortuary following a deadly fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences hospital in Islamabad on August 26, 2026. — AFP

Minister of State for Law Barrister Aqeel Malik assured in a post on X that a “complete, transparent, and impartial investigation of the incident will be conducted to determine the true causes of this catastrophe and any possible negligence”.

“In the event that negligence or failure is proven at any level, strict action will be taken against the responsible individuals in accordance with the law,” he added, extending his condolences to the bereaved families and expressing grief over the incident.

Meanwhile, PPP leader Nayyar Hussain Bokhari, who reached Pims along with Senator Sherry Rehman and others, demanded that the head of the MCH be removed.

Bokhari said it was not just negligence but rather criminal negligence and should not be ignored.

Rehman said the Pims’ executive director must “answer why the system here keeps being akin to gross negligence”.

“The health ministry now has no justification for taking public funds. It should be dissolved or devolved to the provinces,” she was quoted as saying by her party.

She insisted they were not visiting “to play politics” but were sent by the party leadership to raise questions on behalf of the public.

In a post on her X account, Rehman also shared a video of her visiting the ward.

“Totally gutted. People had to break windows and jump out. Emergency gate was closed, fire equipment not working, medical staff not present,” she wrote.

“Honestly, I would have resigned on the spot,” Rehman added later.

Tallal Chaudhry defends district administration

Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry insisted that there had not been any delay in the arrival of rescue teams and defended the district administration.

“After receiving information in the control room, they reached the hospital within six minutes,” the state minister said while speaking to the media in Islamabad.

He added that once the rescue teams assessed the situation, 19 people were rescued, including seven children, 1o mothers and two men.

He also said that administration officials “from the assistant commissioner to commissioner to the Islamabad IG” reached the hospital to monitor the situation. “Not only did they monitor but also assisted in the rescue operation,” he said.

Reiterating that rescue teams reached the site within six minutes, the state minister said, “There appears to be no negligence on the part of rescue services.”

However, he added, only the hospital administration could answer for the arrangements present within the hospital.

Chaudhry said that the bodies of all 14 infants had been handed over to their families.

He added that a report of the incident had been sent to the prime minister and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, who he said had been monitoring the situation.

On being asked if Pims met the CDA’s fire safety protocols, with a journalist also pointing out that his ministry had been issuing notices to the hospital for the past seven years, he acknowledged that notices had been issued.

“It is a huge institution, and notices were issued […] but what was complied with and what was not — as there are multiple buildings; we cannot conclude anything today, and an inquiry committee has been formed”.

Asked why the administration had not been active on the fire safety issue before, he said, “If there has been any negligence, the inquiry committee will find out.”

An inquiry committee has been formed for a “high-powered” investigation into the incident, Chaudhry noted. He said the committee will collect evidence — CCTV footage, presence of flammable equipment, why the door was locked, the number of doctors and nurses present — and present its findings.

In its update on the incident, CDA said fire and rescue teams reached the site within seven minutes after a call was received at 6:54am.

Fire tenders, rescue teams, ambulances of the Capital Emergency Services (CES) and the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) administration were part of the deployed resources.

Nation expresses grief

President Asif Ali Zardari expressed heartfelt condolences and sympathy to the bereaved families. In a statement, the president said that the loss of lives was “heartbreaking and an irreparable loss”.

“Responsibility for the incident should be determined and action should be taken in accordance with the law,” he said.

Effective fire safety and emergency arrangements must be ensured in hospitals for the protection of patients, especially newborn babies, the president urged.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said he was deeply saddened by the incident.

“My deepest condolences to the bereaved parents and families. No words can ease the pain of losing an innocent child. May Allah Almighty grant the families strength and sabr in this unimaginably difficult hour,” he said.

As per the prime minister’s orders an immediate and thorough investigation will establish the causes of this tragic incident to ensure that those found responsible face the strictest action. The safety of our children must remain paramount,” he said.

PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari wrote on X: “Mothers do not keep their children in the womb for nine months just so that, due to someone’s negligence, they burn alive as soon as they are born.
